veracity.explanation: Relays a commitment attributed to Simeon Brown while he was Minister of Transport, in order to contrast it with the charge this bill enables.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hansard, Beehive press releases and media reports of Simeon Brown's statements while Minister of Transport: true if he made a statement to this effect about not adding further road-user costs during the cost of living crisis; false if no such statement is on record.

rigor.statement: If they don’t do that, then I suspect this could be a way of just generating much-needed revenue to balance their books.
rigor.explanation: Infers the Government's motive (revenue-gathering) from the absence of accompanying public transport investment. The inference is about the policy, not the people, but it is an argument from absence of evidence to imputed intent — a real gap between what is shown and what is concluded, though it is hedged with "I suspect".
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: It didn’t sound like the beginning of a beautiful relationship to me, and so I think we need to make sure that the Government can have a relationship with councils that is going to enable real partnership, because if that doesn’t happen then, again, this is not going to work for many people.
civility.explanation: A wry, pointed dig at a named Minister's conduct that edges toward the person without landing on him — the criticism resolves into a substantive point about central-local partnership rather than an attack on Bishop's character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

divination.statement: That’s the key part to this: because we know that for planning purposes, having the congestion charge is great—it is going to change behaviours—but it’s really difficult for some people if there are not other options available to them.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that introducing a congestion charge will change travel behaviour — an outcome of the policy, not a promise about the speaker's own action.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Post-implementation evaluation of the Auckland congestion charging scheme by Auckland Transport / NZTA: true if the published evaluation reports a measurable reduction in peak-period vehicle trips in the charged area relative to the pre-scheme baseline; false if no measurable change in travel behaviour is found.

civility.statement: We respect the unions’ right to strike. We also encourage them to think about the impact they’re having on kids, parents, and patients.
civility.explanation: A genuinely contested exchange about limiting the right to strike, where an attack on the unions or on Hipkins was readily available. Luxon engages the substance and attacks nobody.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: To take each of the three stupid assertions in that question in reverse order: the tobacco claim by the member is inaccurate and wrong; in relation to the board directors, if the last Government had not appointed boards that ran so many Crown companies—like, to take a random example, Kāinga Ora—so badly, we would not have been put in a position where we had to bring in some commercial expertise to get the books back on track; and, in relation to the first part of the question, I always agree with the Prime Minister.
civility.explanation: Labelling a member's questions 'stupid assertions' is condescension toward the questioner rather than engagement with them. It stops short of a direct personal insult, but it is no longer civil under the re-anchored scale where 1.0 is the ordinary standard.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: He said that, ultimately, we need to balance the right to strike and actually make sure we protect the interests of other New Zealanders.
veracity.explanation: Luxon asserts that Simeon Brown said the Government needs to balance the right to strike against other New Zealanders' interests. The accuracy of the characterisation is Luxon's own, so subject is the speaker even though the words are Brown's.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The public record of Simeon Brown's remarks on doctors' right to strike (media interviews and transcripts, October 2025); true if he framed it as balancing the right to strike against the interests of other New Zealanders, false if his remarks were materially different or if he went further than Luxon's characterisation.

veracity.statement: But, again, there are offers that have been extended to the unions that haven’t been taken out to members.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that current pay offers exist which the unions have not put to their memberships for a vote.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public Service Commission, PPTA, NZEI and PSA statements on the status of the pay offers live as at 22 October 2025; true if at least one extended offer had not been taken to a member ballot by that date, false if every extended offer had been put to members.

veracity.statement: Why didn’t the Government increase eligibility for the game development rebate given the current $40 million budget for the rebate isn’t being fully utilised?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the $40 million budget for the game development rebate is not being fully drawn down.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE / CODE (Centre of Digital Excellence) reporting on the Game Development Sector Rebate: appropriated budget versus rebate actually paid out for the most recent year; true if payments fell materially short of the $40 million appropriation, false if the fund was fully or near-fully subscribed.

veracity.statement: When I looked at the numbers a few months ago—and don’t hold me to account—the 38 percent increase in the size of the gaming sector, I think it actually hit something like $780 million in the last year, which is fantastic.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two figures for the New Zealand game development sector: 38 percent growth, and a size of roughly $780 million in the last year. Hedged in delivery, but both figures are stated.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The New Zealand Game Developers Association annual industry survey for 2024 and 2025 (total industry revenue and year-on-year growth rate); true if revenue is within rounding of $780 million with growth near 38 percent, false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: Why isn’t he aware that the gaming sector has grown 86 percent in the last 2½ years since the gaming rebate was introduced by the previous Labour Government and that his Government, despite repeated requests from the sector, has not been willing to expand eligibility so that the budget that was set aside for it actually gets spent?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the gaming sector has grown 86 percent in the 2½ years since the rebate was introduced. The growth figure is the checkable claim; the characterisation of the Government's unwillingness is not operationalised.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Game Developers Association annual survey revenue figures for 2023 through 2025, measured from the introduction of the rebate (Budget 2023); true if cumulative growth over that period is near 86 percent, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: It’s also why we’re backing farmers because, actually, dairy’s up 14 percent, red meat’s up about 9 percent, and horticulture’s up 19 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts year-on-year growth of 14 percent for dairy, about 9 percent for red meat and 19 percent for horticulture.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI Situation and Outlook for the Primary Industries (June/September 2025 edition) export revenue figures by sector; true if each sector's growth is within rounding of the stated figure, false if any is materially different.

veracity.statement: This morning, the New Zealand Superannuation Fund published its latest annual report. It shows that the super fund's total size was $85 billion at 30 June 2025, with average return since its inception of 10.1 percent per annum.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the NZ Super Fund's total size was $85 billion at 30 June 2025 and its since-inception average return is 10.1 percent per annum.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The New Zealand Superannuation Fund Annual Report for the year ended 30 June 2025: net fund size and since-inception annualised return; true if both figures match within rounding, false if either is materially different.

veracity.statement: The other 70 percent have been divested or liquidated as Temasek invested, divested, and grew their portfolio to $434 billion Singaporean.
veracity.explanation: Asserts Temasek's portfolio has grown to S$434 billion, and that roughly 70 percent of its original seed assets have been divested or liquidated.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Temasek Review 2025 net portfolio value, and Temasek's own published account of how many of its 35 initial 1974 portfolio companies remain held; true if the portfolio value is within rounding of S$434 billion and around 10 of the 35 original companies remain, false if either is materially different.

veracity.statement: How can she stand by her statement that “Costs are under control, and inflation is under control” when there have been four consecutive increases in inflation?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the annual inflation rate has risen in four consecutive quarters as at October 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index annual rate for the four quarters to September 2025; true if the annual rate rose in each successive quarter, false if it fell or was flat in any of them.

veracity.statement: Three years ago, it was 7.3 percent. It is now 3 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts annual inflation was 7.3 percent three years before October 2025 and is 3 percent now.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI annual rate for the September 2022 quarter and the September 2025 quarter; true if the figures are within rounding of 7.3 percent and 3.0 percent respectively, false if either is materially different (note the 7.3 percent peak print falls in the June 2022 quarter, so the 'three years ago' anchor is part of what must be checked).

veracity.statement: The Government has come to the table and put a record investment in Budget 2025 of over $700 million.
veracity.explanation: Asserts Budget 2025 contained a record investment of over $700 million, in context for learning support in education.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2025 education vote documents for the learning support package: total appropriation and whether it exceeds any prior learning support allocation; true if the figure exceeds $700 million and is the largest such allocation, false if the appropriation is materially smaller or a previous Budget allocated more.

focus.statement: How is it in the interests of parents, patients, and kids for the Government to offer public sector workers—like teachers, doctors, nurses, and others—pay increases that are less than the rate of inflation and so amount to a real-terms pay cut and not address the workload issues that they have been raising?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the policy: names the workforces, the pay offers relative to inflation, and the workload issue. Legitimate scrutiny of a named government position, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Isn’t it great! We’re getting a question on the third Labour policy of this week, but we didn’t get one for one and two. This is really the big deal that’s going to move the needle from Labour! I’ll just say that getting in behind and backing fast track, public-private partnerships, roads of national significance, NCEA changes—those are things that we want to hear from the Leader of the Opposition on.
focus.explanation: The question was about rebate eligibility; the answer is about Labour's choice of questions and what Labour ought to be backing. The policies listed at the end are named only as a list of things the Opposition should support, not engaged with, so almost all the weight is party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How can she stand by her statement that “Costs are under control, and inflation is under control” when there have been four consecutive increases in inflation?
focus.explanation: Holds a named minister to a named statement against a specific data series. Textbook scrutiny with policy content, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How is it in the interests of parents, patients, and kids for the Government to offer public sector workers—like teachers, doctors, nurses, and others—pay increases that are less than the rate of inflation and so amount to a real-terms pay cut and not address the workload issues that they have been raising?
specificity.explanation: Names the affected groups and the mechanism (offer below inflation equals a real-terms cut), but supplies no figure for the offer, no inflation number and no timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Asking teachers to consider whether they could do their professional development and their teacher only days in one of the 12 weeks of the school holidays is not an unreasonable request.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete mechanism (professional development and teacher only days) and a concrete quantity (one of the 12 weeks of school holidays). Someone could check what is actually being proposed; it stops short of naming the offer or the number of days.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why didn’t the Government increase eligibility for the game development rebate given the current $40 million budget for the rebate isn’t being fully utilised?
specificity.explanation: Names the policy (the game development rebate), the budget figure ($40 million) and the precise action sought (widening eligibility). Directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It’s also why we’re backing farmers because, actually, dairy’s up 14 percent, red meat’s up about 9 percent, and horticulture’s up 19 percent.
specificity.explanation: Three named sectors each with a percentage figure. Precise and checkable, though the base period and the measure (export revenue? volume?) are left implicit.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is the Prime Minister aware of the recent gaming sector review where some businesses saw “increasing the number of grants available through CODE as the most effective lever for further development”?
specificity.explanation: Names a specific document (the recent gaming sector review), a named mechanism (CODE grants) and quotes its finding directly. Falls short of 1.0 only because no figure or timeframe is attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This morning, the New Zealand Superannuation Fund published its latest annual report. It shows that the super fund's total size was $85 billion at 30 June 2025, with average return since its inception of 10.1 percent per annum.
specificity.explanation: A named source, a dollar figure, a balance date and a return rate. About as checkable as a statement in the House gets.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The Government has come to the table and put a record investment in Budget 2025 of over $700 million.
specificity.explanation: A dollar figure attached to a named Budget, in context directed at learning support. Loses ground because 'over $700 million' is a floor rather than a number and the period it covers is unstated.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: To take each of the three stupid assertions in that question in reverse order: the tobacco claim by the member is inaccurate and wrong; in relation to the board directors, if the last Government had not appointed boards that ran so many Crown companies—like, to take a random example, Kāinga Ora—so badly, we would not have been put in a position where we had to bring in some commercial expertise to get the books back on track; and, in relation to the first part of the question, I always agree with the Prime Minister.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real policy, so it is eligible: poor board appointments by the previous Government therefore required commercial expertise therefore higher director pay. The chain has a genuine gap — nothing offered links board performance to the necessity or the size of the pay increases, and the causal step from 'ran companies badly' to 'we had to raise director fees' is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: As I outlined to the House yesterday, the Government’s spending $1.2 billion to move the next tranche of the roads of national significance to the next phase of development following the board’s approval of the investment cases.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific funding figure ($1.2 billion) allocated to advance the next tranche of roads of national significance following NZTA board approval of the investment cases.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA board minutes and the Minister of Transport's October 2025 announcement on the roads of national significance investment cases; true if the sum committed to move that tranche to the next development phase is $1.2 billion, false if the announced figure is materially different or no such board approval occurred.

veracity.statement: Tomorrow, I will be in Wellington, and I do understand that all rallies, planned events, and sign-waving events have been called off due to severe weather in Wellington.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that all education sector strike rallies and sign-waving events planned in Wellington for 23 October 2025 were cancelled because of severe weather.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZEI/PPTA public notices and contemporaneous news reports for 22–23 October 2025, plus MetService severe weather warnings for Wellington; true if the Wellington rallies and sign-waving events were called off on weather grounds, false if they proceeded or were only partly cancelled.

veracity.statement: I would like to just say that we have been listening to them, which is why we have delivered the biggest investment in learning support in a generation, more than they did in the last six years combined; which is why we have invested in paying for their teacher registration fees; which is why we’ve invested in an aspiring principal programme; which is why we’ve invested in a teacher bonding scheme, among many, many things we’ve done to back the sector.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that this Government's learning support investment is the biggest in a generation and exceeds the previous Government's learning support spending over its last six years combined.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget appropriations for learning support (Vote Education) under Budgets 2024–2025 compared with the equivalent learning support appropriations across Budgets 2018–2023; true if the current Government's new learning support funding exceeds the six-year total of the previous Government, false if the earlier total is equal or greater.

veracity.statement: Why have over 40,000 educators been forced to take to the streets just to get their Minister to listen to their concerns?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than 40,000 educators are taking strike action in the education sector strike referred to.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZEI Te Riu Roa and PPTA membership/participation figures for the 23 October 2025 education sector strike, and contemporaneous reporting of turnout; true if participants number over 40,000, false if materially fewer.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by his statement, in response to our questions yesterday, that nurses have safe staffing conditions, when Te Whatu Ora’s own data showed that 50 percent of day shifts were understaffed in 16 districts over 10 months last year in our hospitals?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Te Whatu Ora data shows half of day shifts across 16 districts were understaffed over a 10-month period in 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Te Whatu Ora care capacity demand management / shift-level staffing data released for 2024 (including via OIA); true if roughly 50 percent of day shifts in 16 districts over a 10-month period were recorded as below target staffing, false if the recorded proportion or district count is materially different.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by his statement that nurses have safe working conditions, when nurses report that emergency departments are currently, under his Government’s hiring freeze, so short-staffed that some patients who soil themselves are left lying for hours in their own excrement because staff do not have time to help?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that a Government hiring freeze is in place at Health New Zealand, and relays nurses' reports of emergency department conditions arising from it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand recruitment directives, vacancy control policies and Ministerial instructions in force in October 2025; true if a freeze or blanket pause on hiring applied to clinical roles including emergency department nursing, false if recruitment for those roles continued under normal or merely tightened approval processes.

veracity.statement: Is he concerned that neonatal wards across Auckland, Whangārei, Christchurch, Palmerston North, and Tauranga hospitals were understaffed for more than a third of the shifts in the first half of this year, and, if so, what impacts does he think that these unsafe working conditions have on parents and newborns?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that neonatal wards at five named hospitals were understaffed on more than a third of shifts in the first half of 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand neonatal unit shift staffing records for January–June 2025 for Auckland, Whangārei, Christchurch, Palmerston North and Tauranga; true if more than 33 percent of shifts were recorded below target staffing at those units, false if the recorded rate is materially lower.

veracity.statement: Well, in answer to the first part of the question, there is no hiring freeze.
veracity.explanation: Flat denial that a hiring freeze is in place in the health system, directly contradicting the premise of the question.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand recruitment policy documents and vacancy control settings in force in October 2025; true if no freeze or pause on recruitment applied, false if a hiring freeze or equivalent recruitment pause was in effect for any substantial part of the workforce.

veracity.statement: The fact that, in less than two years, we’ve added 2,100 extra nurses into Health New Zealand is a really good thing, and the fact that we’ve made consistent efforts and investments in the healthcare system—$17 billion in our first Budget; up another 7 percent in our second Budget—is all good stuff.
veracity.explanation: Asserts an increase of 2,100 nurses at Health New Zealand within two years, $17 billion in the first Budget and a further 7 percent increase in the second.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand nursing workforce (FTE or headcount) figures for late 2023 compared with late 2025, and Vote Health appropriations in Budgets 2024 and 2025; true if the net nurse increase is about 2,100 and the Budget figures match, false if the workforce growth or funding figures are materially different.

specificity.statement: Ultimately, if the project is built completely between Auckland and Whangārei, it will reduce travel times by 38 minutes and of course reduce deaths and serious injury, which is something that many members are concerned about, by 66 percent.
specificity.explanation: Names the corridor, and gives two quantified outcomes (38 minutes of travel time, 66 percent reduction in deaths and serious injuries) that can be checked against the investment case.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does he stand by his statement, in response to our questions yesterday, that nurses have safe staffing conditions, when Te Whatu Ora’s own data showed that 50 percent of day shifts were understaffed in 16 districts over 10 months last year in our hospitals?
specificity.explanation: Names the source of the data, the proportion (50 percent), the shift type, the number of districts (16) and the period (10 months last year). Fully checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Will the Prime Minister commit to empowering Government negotiators to turn up to the bargaining table equipped with the resources necessary to meet the actual real-world need to fix our education and healthcare systems?
specificity.explanation: Directed at a real mechanism (the negotiating mandate given to Government bargaining teams) but carries no figure, no offer, and no definition of 'the resources necessary' — nothing that could be costed or checked against.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: State Highway 6 is a vital connection for people and goods, will boost economic growth in Nelson-Tasman, reduce peak journey times through Richmond by at least 10 minutes by 2034, and of course developments continue on the Belfast to Pegasus and Woodend Bypass road of national significance, with a fast-track application being worked through currently.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that peak journey times through Richmond on State Highway 6 will be at least 10 minutes shorter by 2034. This is an outcome forecast, not merely a commitment to build.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA journey-time monitoring data for the State Highway 6 corridor through Richmond; true if the average peak journey time in 2034 is at least 10 minutes lower than the 2025 baseline, false if the reduction is under 10 minutes or peak times are unchanged/worse.

rigor.statement: I would like to just say that we have been listening to them, which is why we have delivered the biggest investment in learning support in a generation, more than they did in the last six years combined; which is why we have invested in paying for their teacher registration fees; which is why we’ve invested in an aspiring principal programme; which is why we’ve invested in a teacher bonding scheme, among many, many things we’ve done to back the sector.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion ('we have been listening') is supported only by a list of spending decisions. Funding choices made by the Minister are evidence of activity, not of engaging with the concerns actually raised (pay and bargaining) — the inference equivocates between 'investing in' and 'listening to'.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, they do have a choice, and here is an example of a union that did have a choice: the Primary Principals’ Collective Bargaining Union, with over 500 members, chose not to strike; chose to be at the bargaining table with the Public Service Commission; chose to be open and transparent; chose to come to a settlement—a good, fair, and reasonable settlement.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from a single 500-member union to the position of a 40,000-strong workforce in a different bargaining round. The example shows one union settled; it does not establish that the striking unions faced the same options, so the conclusion outruns the evidence offered (hasty generalisation).
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That is why more and more educators are joining their union, day by day: because they’re sick of the New Zealand Educational Institute.
rigor.explanation: A bare causal assertion: a claimed membership trend is attributed to a specific motive with nothing offered to establish either the trend or the motive. Post hoc causal attribution with no supporting evidence.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The fact that, in less than two years, we’ve added 2,100 extra nurses into Health New Zealand is a really good thing, and the fact that we’ve made consistent efforts and investments in the healthcare system—$17 billion in our first Budget; up another 7 percent in our second Budget—is all good stuff.
rigor.explanation: The question was about shift-level understaffing; the answer offers aggregate headcount and funding inputs as the response. Adding 2,100 nurses nationally does not establish that individual shifts are safely staffed — the conclusion about the working environment does not follow from the input figures offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, I’m just very proud of the progress that we’ve taken since the departure of a Labour-Greens Government—that, clearly, we have put more money in, in the history of New Zealand; we have put more workforce into the healthcare system; we have good clarity on targets; and we now expect delivery from Health New Zealand to support patients.
rigor.explanation: Answers a question about neonatal wards being understaffed on a third of shifts by listing spending, workforce and target-setting. Inputs are offered as proof of an outcome without any link between them and the staffing figures put to him — a non sequitur.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, it turns out I’ve got hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of friends, because that’s how many people are turning up to the Curriculum Roadshow to learn about the changes and the reform in education that is going to be raising achievement and closing the education gap in this country—which is more than those guys did in six years.
civility.explanation: Turns a jibe about 'her friends' back with a wry answer and keeps to the roadshow and the reform. The closing swipe is at the opposing party's record, not at any individual, so nothing lands on a person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does she realise that educators have no choice but to strike when she has refused to listen to them despite open letters signed by hundreds of principals and petitions signed by thousands of concerned teachers and whānau?
civility.explanation: Robust scrutiny of the Minister's handling of the dispute, but 'refused to listen' goes beyond criticising a decision to imputing a deliberate unwillingness to engage — pointed, edging toward the person without landing on them.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: What message does she think she sends educators when she is willing to prioritise her roadshow with her friends over meeting with those who are striking?
civility.explanation: 'Her roadshow with her friends' is a sneer rather than an argument: it insinuates that the Minister is spending her time with cronies and dismisses the attendees, imputing self-interest rather than contesting the choice on its merits.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, it turns out I’ve got hundreds and hundreds and hundreds of friends, because that’s how many people are turning up to the Curriculum Roadshow to learn about the changes and the reform in education that is going to be raising achievement and closing the education gap in this country—which is more than those guys did in six years.
focus.explanation: Names the Curriculum Roadshow and the education reform programme, but the answer's weight is carried by attendance numbers and a closing comparison to what 'those guys' did in six years rather than by the content of the changes.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, I’m proud of what we’re doing on improving on our health and education systems, given the mess that we inherited from the last lot. But I’d just say that we are ready 24/7—ready to go—so why don’t we actually cancel the strike tomorrow and actually go to the bargaining table tomorrow?
focus.explanation: Contains a genuine procedural point about bargaining availability, but no policy, resource or offer is named, and a good share of the answer is generic blame directed at 'the last lot' rather than the negotiating mandate that was asked about.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I could point to the progress made on our ambitious target to see 20,000 fewer victims of serious violent crime by 2029, and the most recent data released for the 12 months to May shows there were 29,000 fewer victims than when we came into Government; 9,000 ahead of our target.
specificity.explanation: Carries a named target, a baseline, a measurement window and three separate figures; anyone could look up whether the numbers hold.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, our trial of clamping and seizing the cars of people who have not paid their court fines and reparations began in July and is set to expand, after it achieved more than $225,000 in fines and the seizure of 115 vehicles.
specificity.explanation: A named mechanism (clamping and seizure for unpaid fines), a start date, a dollar figure and a vehicle count — fully checkable and actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Before the end of the year, we will introduce legislation to strengthen consequences for crime in the Crimes Act, including new citizens arrest powers, a raft of coalition commitments, as well as to pass legislation to make stalking an illegal and jailable offence—a lot of talk about that over many years but this Government will do it before the end of the year.
specificity.explanation: Names the statute to be amended, two concrete measures (citizens arrest powers, a stalking offence) and a deadline; the vaguer 'raft of coalition commitments' is the only unspecified part.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Was she or her office consulted before the Public Service Commission approved taxpayer-funded ads about the strike on Thursday, and were they involved in the content, timing, or authorisation?
specificity.explanation: Names the body, the spending, the event and three distinct points of possible involvement (content, timing, authorisation) — a precise question that could be answered precisely.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The first is creating cohesion and accountability across Government. The second is about targeting cashflows. The third is our role in supporting our Pacific neighbours.
specificity.explanation: Theme headings only: no mechanism, agency, funding or timeframe attaches to any of the three, so there is nothing here to check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: At the same time, $20 million to $25 million per year is being invested in new fire trucks. Currently, 78 are on order, including five aerial appliances.
specificity.explanation: An annual spending range, an order count and a breakdown by appliance type; the delivery timeframe is given in the surrounding text.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: I could point to the progress made on our ambitious target to see 20,000 fewer victims of serious violent crime by 2029, and the most recent data released for the 12 months to May shows there were 29,000 fewer victims than when we came into Government; 9,000 ahead of our target.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the published 12-months-to-May figures show 29,000 fewer victims of violent crime than at the change of government, putting the Government 9,000 ahead of its 20,000-by-2029 target.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The NZ Crime and Victims Survey series used for the Government's victims-of-assault target, and the Government Targets quarterly report for the 12 months to May 2025: true if the published estimate is a reduction of about 29,000 victims against the stated baseline and the target is 20,000 by 2029; false if the published reduction is materially smaller, or measured against a different baseline than the one implied.

veracity.statement: In a three-month period, bailiffs scanned more than 70,000 number plates and identified 982 with overdue court fines and reparations.
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific operational figures for the fines-enforcement trial: over 70,000 plates scanned and 982 vehicles identified with overdue fines in three months.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Justice fines-enforcement reporting on the July–October 2025 number-plate scanning trial: true if the official figures record more than 70,000 plates scanned and 982 vehicles identified; false if the recorded totals differ materially.

veracity.statement: Well, alongside our target to reduce the number of victims of serious crime, we’ve also got a target led by Minister Chhour to reduce the number of children and young people with serious and persistent offending by 15 percent, which, the good news is, we have achieved as a Government already.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government's 15 percent reduction target for children and young people with serious and persistent offending has already been met.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government Targets quarterly reporting for the youth serious and persistent offending target: true if the most recent published measurement before October 2025 shows a reduction of 15 percent or more against the stated baseline; false if the published reduction is under 15 percent.

veracity.statement: The ads clarified the information about the offers on the table and were a perfectly valid way of drawing attention to the enormous disruption being caused to families, to children, and to patients by the ongoing strikes.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact what the taxpayer-funded advertisements contained — that they set out the pay offers rather than attacking the unions' bargaining position.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published text and imagery of the Public Service Commission's October 2025 advertisements: true if they principally set out the details of the offers made; false if their principal content characterises or criticises the unions' bargaining stance.

veracity.statement: In the last financial year, more than nine tonnes of illicit drugs were stopped from entering New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific border interception total for illicit drugs in the 2024/25 financial year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Customs Service annual report / joint Customs-Police border seizure statistics for the 2024/25 financial year: true if the total weight of illicit drugs intercepted exceeds nine tonnes; false if the published total is below that.

veracity.statement: Since the merger of the voluntary and professional fire services in 2017, there has been a long period of time where the rate of replacement of fire engines has not kept up in such a way that it’s kept the average age down.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that fire appliance replacement rates since the 2017 FENZ merger were insufficient to hold the fleet's average age steady, so the fleet aged.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: FENZ fleet asset data / annual reports on appliance numbers, replacement rates and average fleet age from 2017 to 2023: true if the average age of the appliance fleet rose over that period; false if it held steady or fell.

veracity.statement: Bargaining is available. It’s simply a question of the firefighters turning up.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that bargaining has been offered and that the failure to bargain is on the firefighters' side rather than FENZ's.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The FENZ / NZ Professional Firefighters Union bargaining record for the period to October 2025 — dates offered, sessions scheduled and which party attended: true if FENZ made dates available that the union did not attend; false if FENZ cancelled, declined or failed to attend scheduled bargaining.

veracity.statement: Why should firefighters accept a pay offer that is a pay cut in real terms?
veracity.explanation: The question embeds a factual claim: that the pay offer on the table for firefighters amounts to a cut in real terms once inflation is accounted for.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The percentage increases in FENZ's 2025 offer to the NZ Professional Firefighters Union, compared with Stats NZ CPI annual inflation over the term of the offer: true if the offered increases fall below CPI over that period; false if they match or exceed it.

civility.statement: Does she think it is in good faith to spend public money on messaging that attacks the bargaining position of doctors, nurses, and teachers?
civility.explanation: Pointed: it puts the Minister's good faith in issue rather than only the decision, but stops short of imputing bad faith outright and stays anchored to the spending decision itself.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does she still stand by her claim that the strike is politically motivated, and if so, how is her own decision to attack the bargaining position of doctors, nurses, and teachers not itself politically motivated?
civility.explanation: Imputes a political motive to the Minister personally rather than testing the decision on its merits; a consistency challenge, but one aimed at motive.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I’m sure that a Labour member will realise that red things aren’t always reliable.
focus.explanation: A jibe at the other party's colour with no policy, figure or measure in it; strip out the party swipe and nothing remains. No individual is insulted, so Civility passes it — this is the case Focus exists for.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It is easy, in Opposition, to say that you think everybody should be paid more. However, it is also true that in these negotiations there are two sides that must be represented, and one of those are the New Zealanders who pay the cost.
focus.explanation: A genuine policy point — that the levy-payers' interest is a party to the negotiation — but it is framed around what Opposition members are like rather than the offer that was asked about.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does she agree with Brooke van Velden that all parties need to get around the bargaining table; if so, why has Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) failed to front up for bargaining?
focus.explanation: Names a specific agency, a specific stated position and a specific alleged failure to act on it. Legitimate scrutiny of a named commitment, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Since coming into office, this Government has added around 2,000 more nurses to the public health system compared to 2023, alongside hundreds of additional doctors.
specificity.explanation: Carries a figure (around 2,000), a baseline year (2023) and a named workforce; someone could go and check it. Loses a little for 'hundreds of additional doctors' being unquantified.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Recently, I announced the introduction of peer support workers in the North Shore emergency department, completing the roll-out of the service across all three major Auckland hospitals alongside Dunedin, Christchurch, Wellington, and Waikato hospitals.
specificity.explanation: Names the service, the specific site newly added, and every hospital covered by the roll-out. Concrete enough that anyone could go and verify whether the service exists at each named ED.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: That is why we are now able to go back to the 20 health districts, understand the performance of each of those areas, and ensure they deliver a level of service Kiwis should expect in mental health: one week for primary mental health and addiction support; three weeks for specialist mental health and addiction support.
specificity.explanation: Names the unit of measurement (20 health districts) and gives two concrete, checkable service standards with explicit timeframes. Falls short of 1.0 because it states the targets without the mechanism by which districts are held to them.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Will the Minister investigate the mental health crisis in Thames following a serious mental health incident that was brought to his attention by a local mental health rangatira in Hauraki earlier this Monday?
specificity.explanation: Names the location, the source of the concern and the timing, but the 'serious mental health incident' and the 'crisis' itself are not described, so there is a direction without the detail needed to act on it.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Since coming into office, this Government has added around 2,000 more nurses to the public health system compared to 2023, alongside hundreds of additional doctors.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a net increase of roughly 2,000 nurses and several hundred doctors employed in the public health system between 2023 and October 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand / Te Whatu Ora published workforce headcount (or FTE) data for nursing and medical staff, 2023 baseline versus the latest 2025 reporting period. True if the nursing increase is around 2,000 and the medical increase is in the hundreds; false if materially lower, or if the increase depends on a headcount-versus-FTE switch or a change in who is counted.

veracity.statement: That's backed by a record additional $16.68 billion investment in health over three Budgets, including initiatives focused on improving workplace safety and reducing wait-lists for patients.
veracity.explanation: Asserts both a quantum — $16.68 billion of additional health funding across Budgets 2024, 2025 and 2026 — and that this is a record for any comparable three-Budget period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget documents and Vote Health appropriations for the three Budgets referenced. True if the additional (not baseline) health funding across those Budgets sums to approximately $16.68 billion and exceeds the additional funding in any prior three-Budget span in nominal terms; false if the total is materially different, or if a previous three-Budget period delivered a larger nominal increase.

veracity.statement: Quality safety measures are stable or improving over the past five years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the published clinical quality and safety indicators for the public hospital system have not deteriorated over the 2020–2025 period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health Quality & Safety Commission quality and safety markers and adverse events reporting, plus Health NZ quality indicators, for the five years to 2025. True if the indicator set as a whole is flat or improving over that span; false if a material share of the published measures show deterioration.

veracity.statement: Recently, I announced the introduction of peer support workers in the North Shore emergency department, completing the roll-out of the service across all three major Auckland hospitals alongside Dunedin, Christchurch, Wellington, and Waikato hospitals.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that peer support workers are now operating in the emergency departments of North Shore and the other two major Auckland hospitals, and of Dunedin, Christchurch, Wellington and Waikato hospitals — i.e. that the roll-out across those sites is complete.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand service records and ministerial announcements for peer support workers in emergency departments at each named hospital. True if the service is operating at all sites listed as at October 2025; false if any named ED has no peer support worker in place, or if the Auckland roll-out covers fewer than all three major hospitals.

veracity.statement: Since coming into Government, the peer support lived experience workforce has grown by almost 100 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the peer support / lived experience workforce has roughly doubled between the change of government in late 2023 and October 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand peer support and lived experience workforce headcount (or FTE) for late 2023 versus 2025, or the equivalent figure in the Ministry of Health mental health workforce reporting. True if growth over that period is close to 100 percent; false if materially lower, or if the doubling depends on a change in which roles are counted as peer support.

divination.statement: Those wait-lists are only going to increase with tomorrow's strikes.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the nurses' strike action scheduled for 23 October 2025 will drive an increase in patient wait-lists. This is a prediction about an outcome, not a promise about the Government's own action.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand planned care / elective wait-list reporting and its published count of appointments and procedures deferred because of the 23 October 2025 strike. True if Health NZ reports deferred appointments or procedures attributable to the strike and the wait-list count rises across the period covering it; false if no material deferrals are recorded or the wait-list count does not rise.

focus.statement: We're focused on front-line service delivery while they were focused on restructuring bureaucracy.
focus.explanation: A bare us-versus-them contrast. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named on either side of it — 'front-line service delivery' and 'restructuring bureaucracy' are characterisations of the two parties' priorities, not policy content. Nobody is personally insulted, so Civility is untouched; this is exactly the tribal framing Focus exists to catch.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We're focused on patients; they're focused on bureaucracy.
focus.explanation: Entirely a statement about which team cares about what. No policy, mechanism, figure or outcome is named. It insults no individual, so it passes Civility cleanly — Focus is the only attribute that registers it.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Who is correct: nurses across the country who are telling us that they do not have safe working conditions or the Prime Minister who said that nurses have safe working conditions?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the policy question at issue — whether hospital staffing levels are safe — and puts the Government's own stated position against reported front-line experience. This is legitimate scrutiny of a named claim by a named office-holder, which is the job of an opposition MP and scores high, not low.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Will the Minister investigate the mental health crisis in Thames following a serious mental health incident that was brought to his attention by a local mental health rangatira in Hauraki earlier this Monday?
focus.explanation: Directed at a specific service-delivery failure in a named place, arising from a specific incident with a specific date. Scrutiny anchored to an identifiable case rather than to the Government's character — high Focus.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, the facts speak for themselves, and the facts are that there are more nurses working at Health New Zealand today than under the Labour-Greens coalition, which was more focused on restructuring our health system during a pandemic.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real policy question, and a weak one. The question asked whether ward conditions are safe; total national headcount does not settle whether staffing on a given ward is safe, so the conclusion does not follow from the premise offered — a non sequitur, prefaced by an assertion ('the facts speak for themselves') that substitutes for the connecting step. Scored here rather than under Focus because there is a genuine argument left once the party contrast is stripped out.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Two years into the term of this Government, it is now abundantly clear that all they have to offer New Zealanders is blame, excuses, and anger.
focus.explanation: Entirely a characterisation of the other side's general disposition — no policy, measure, figure or named outcome anywhere in it. This is the content-free party-bashing case Focus exists to catch. No individual is insulted, so Civility passes it cleanly, and there is no inference to assess for Rigor.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The game development rebate that's created jobs, that’s seen the gaming development sector grow by nearly 80 percent during the 2½ years that that rebate has been in place—they want it expanded.
focus.explanation: Squarely on a named policy measure and what the Government decided about it. On-policy engagement, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: One job—they’ve got one job: come up with some policies to actually back up their words. They’ve got lots of words, but nothing to back it up.
focus.explanation: Wholly about the Opposition as a party — what they have failed to produce in general terms. No policy, figure or specific commitment is named, so this is not scrutiny of a measure; it is party framing. Rigor is deliberately not scored: strip out the part about the other side and no argument remains.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Eleven pages; no detail. I think there was one figure.
focus.explanation: Directed at a specific policy document released by the Opposition and at how much substance it contains. Scrutiny of a named policy is on-policy and scores high, even though the criticism is about presentation rather than mechanism.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: When you think about what’s happening over the other side two years in, I think they’re living their own horror show over there. Their financial and economic credibility continues to be in the grave, and, unfortunately, it’s a pattern.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the other party's general standing and what they are 'really like'. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named. Nobody is individually insulted, so Civility is untouched; there is no argument left once the party characterisation is removed, so nothing is emitted for Rigor.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: New Zealanders are looking to this Government for a sense that things will get better; that New Zealand can be a place where our kids want to stay, where they see a future, and where opportunities abound.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic aspirations — no figure, mechanism, timeframe or named policy. Nothing here could be checked or acted on. It is trying to convey substance, so it is eligible, but it carries none.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The game development rebate that's created jobs, that’s seen the gaming development sector grow by nearly 80 percent during the 2½ years that that rebate has been in place—they want it expanded.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific policy (the game development rebate), gives a growth figure (nearly 80 percent) and a period (2½ years). Someone could go and check it. Short of 1.0 only because the growth measure itself (revenue? headcount? firms?) is unstated.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: A future fund that uses our existing asset base to grow opportunities and grow jobs for New Zealand—a Government that backs innovation here in New Zealand is what the Labour Party stands for.
specificity.explanation: Names a vehicle (a future fund) but supplies no size, no funding mechanism, no timeframe and no criteria for what it would invest in. A direction with almost no operational detail attached, even allowing for the surrounding paragraphs.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: If we look at inflation: inflation has stayed within the band of 1 percent to 3 percent. From a high of 7.3 percent—eight official cash rate drops.
specificity.explanation: Precise and checkable: a named target band with numbers, a peak inflation figure, and a count of OCR reductions. Whether the claims hold is a separate question from how much checkable content they carry.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We heard earlier from the Minister of Justice about the progress we’re making on violent crime reduction, aimed at ensuring that there are 20,000 fewer victims of crime. And on youth offending, we’re also well on track with our targets.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific target figure (20,000 fewer victims) and two target areas, but gives no measure of where progress actually stands, no baseline and no date — 'well on track' carries no checkable content of its own. A direction with partial detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Our economy has been shrinking. Jobs have been disappearing. Unemployment is increasing.
veracity.explanation: Three factual assertions about the recent past and present state of the NZ economy: that real GDP has contracted, that employment has fallen, and that the unemployment rate has risen.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ national accounts (real production GDP, quarterly) and the Household Labour Force Survey for the quarters to September 2025. True if real GDP contracted in recent quarters, employment/filled jobs fell, and the unemployment rate rose over 2024-25; false if GDP grew, employment rose and unemployment fell over that period.

veracity.statement: New Zealanders are voting with their feet; record numbers of New Zealanders are simply giving up and leaving the country.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that departures of New Zealanders have reached a record level. The checkable core is 'record numbers' — a claim about the migration series, not a general observation about mood.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ international migration statistics: annual NZ-citizen departures and net NZ-citizen migration loss for the year to the statement date. True if either series reached a record high in the published series; false if it sat below earlier peaks.

veracity.statement: Instead of giving those young New Zealanders hope, we have a Government that describes New Zealand as “wet, whiny and miserable”; that calls New Zealanders “bottom-feeders”; and that says that our emerging businesses, those who are creating the jobs of the future, are “C-listers” and unworthy of Government support.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Ministers in this Government used three specific phrases — 'wet, whiny and miserable' about New Zealand, 'bottom-feeders' about New Zealanders, and 'C-listers' about emerging businesses. The speaker asserts these as fact rather than relaying someone else's claim, so the judgement is his own.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The public record (Hansard, transcripts, contemporaneous media reports) of statements by members of the current Government. True if each of the three quoted phrases is attributable to a Government member in the sense described; false if any of the three is not so attributable or is materially misquoted.

veracity.statement: The game development rebate that's created jobs, that’s seen the gaming development sector grow by nearly 80 percent during the 2½ years that that rebate has been in place—they want it expanded.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the game development sector grew by close to 80 percent over the roughly 2½ years the screen/game development rebate has operated.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Game Developers Association annual industry survey figures for sector revenue/employment across the years spanning the rebate's introduction (2023) to 2025. True if growth over that period is close to 80% on the headline measure; false if materially lower.

veracity.statement: Eleven pages; no detail. I think there was one figure.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two checkable properties of Labour's future fund document: that it runs to eleven pages and that it contains approximately one numerical figure.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Labour future fund policy document released in the week to 22 October 2025. True if it runs to about eleven pages and contains roughly one numerical figure; false if materially longer or if it contains multiple substantive figures.

veracity.statement: If we look at inflation: inflation has stayed within the band of 1 percent to 3 percent. From a high of 7.3 percent—eight official cash rate drops.
veracity.explanation: Three assertions: that inflation has remained inside the 1-3 percent target band, that it peaked at 7.3 percent, and that there have been eight OCR reductions. The scope of 'has stayed' matters — whether it covers the whole parliamentary term or only recent quarters.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI annual inflation for each quarter since late 2023 and the RBNZ record of OCR decisions. True if every quarterly annual CPI print in the period referred to fell between 1% and 3%, the series peak was 7.3%, and exactly eight OCR cuts had been made by 22 October 2025; false if any quarter in scope printed above 3% or the count of cuts differs.

rigor.statement: They don’t even understand how Temasek works: when you buy assets, you then sell assets for ones that have better returns. That’s basic economics, basic trading, basic investment.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the policy, and a weak one. The premise — that portfolio investors buy and sell to chase returns — is offered as though it establishes the conclusion that the Opposition misunderstands the Temasek model, but no gap between that premise and what they actually proposed is identified. Assertion plus a truism, presented as a demonstration: the conclusion does not follow from what was offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But don’t take it from my words. It was described as a flop; vague; lacking in any meaningful costings, asset listings, or clarity.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to authority, and to an unnamed one. The weight of the criticism rests entirely on how unspecified others described the policy; no source is identified and no reasoning from the document itself is offered. It does engage the policy, which is why it is eligible here rather than being a Focus-only jibe.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That comes from fiscal discipline. It comes from understanding economic levers. It comes from understanding that you have to reduce wasteful spending, and focus on getting outcomes and results.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc causal attribution. Inflation returning to band and the OCR cuts that followed are outcomes of monetary policy set by an independent central bank; nothing is offered to connect them to the Government's spending decisions beyond the fact that both occurred. The conclusion is asserted, not supported.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Unfortunately, New Zealanders would have been really disappointed by—well, actually, probably not surprised, really, in terms of the stupid, illiterate nonsense that we got served up.
civility.explanation: The target is the policy document rather than a person, so this is not a personal attack — but 'stupid, illiterate nonsense' is sneering rather than substantive, and derision of that kind is a genuine failure under the re-anchored scale. Hard criticism of the policy's content would have scored near 1.0; contempt for it does not.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Actually, on this side of the House, when we plan infrastructure, we’ve actually got a plan for how we’re paying for that project; unlike the economically illiterate on the other side of the Chamber.
civility.explanation: 'The economically illiterate on the other side of the Chamber' attacks the competence and intelligence of the members opposite, not their policy. The first half is a legitimate substantive contrast; the tag turns it onto the people. That the insult is aimed at others does not make it anyone else's conduct — it is the speaker's own.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Our main issue is it’s one of our policies, one that the Rt Hon Winston Peters announced some 14 months ago at our 2024 convention.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand First, via Winston Peters, announced a sovereign wealth fund policy at its 2024 convention roughly 14 months before October 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand First's 2024 convention materials and contemporaneous news reports (approx. August-September 2024); true if Peters announced a sovereign wealth fund policy at that convention, false if no such announcement was made then or it was made by someone else at a materially different time.

veracity.statement: The turn around is on: strong wool—I should have told the Prime Minister this; he could have quoted it earlier—up 32 percent this year; fine wool: up 34 percent; and mid-micron wool up 41 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts year-to-date 2025 price increases of 32% for strong wool, 34% for fine wool and 41% for mid-micron wool.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand wool auction price indices (e.g. PGG Wrightson / NZ Wool Services International market reports, or Beef+Lamb NZ wool price series) for calendar 2025 to October; true if each of the three categories shows a rise within a few points of 32%, 34% and 41% respectively, false if any is materially different.

veracity.statement: It’s biodegradable, it’s flame retardant, it’s moisture absorbent, it’s anti-allergenic, it’s carbon negative.
veracity.explanation: A bundle of claimed physical properties of wool, of which the load-bearing and contestable one is that wool is carbon negative.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Peer-reviewed life-cycle assessments of New Zealand wool (e.g. AgResearch / IWTO LCA work) covering on-farm emissions through processing; true if the net carbon balance of wool is negative on a full LCA basis and wool is naturally flame-retardant and biodegradable, false if full-LCA studies show a net positive carbon footprint.

veracity.statement: The Government has put its money where its mouth is: New Zealand First and National and a coalition agreement to put wool back into Government buildings.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the National–New Zealand First coalition agreement contains a commitment to use wool in government buildings.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published National–New Zealand First coalition agreement (November 2023); true if it contains a commitment requiring or preferring woollen fibre in government building fit-outs, false if no such clause appears.

veracity.statement: Two hundred people every day—a plane load every day—are now going offshore because they can no longer find the opportunities for them, for their children, and for their families.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that around 200 people per day (roughly 73,000 a year) are departing New Zealand to live overseas.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ international migration estimates for the most recent 12 months to October 2025; true if departures of New Zealand residents/citizens average close to 200 per day, false if the figure is materially below (e.g. under 150/day) or the claim only holds for gross departures of all travellers.

veracity.statement: The fact that we have lost almost the size of Napier City in the last year should be concerning every single one of those Government backbenchers, because Kiwis vote with their feet.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's population loss to overseas migration in the past year is close to the population of Napier city.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ migration estimates for the year to mid/late 2025 compared with Napier city's usually-resident population (approx. 67,000); true if the relevant loss figure is within roughly 10% of that population, false if it is materially smaller or only reaches that size on a gross-departures rather than net basis.

focus.statement: They’re like a cheap tributes band. I see them more as Cliff Richard and the Shadows, and I see us as a bit more like The Rolling Stones.
focus.explanation: Pure party-versus-party mockery. No policy, figure, mechanism or outcome is named once the band comparison is removed. No individual is insulted, so this is a Focus failure rather than a Civility one.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The Government has put its money where its mouth is: New Zealand First and National and a coalition agreement to put wool back into Government buildings.
focus.explanation: Names a specific commitment in a specific document and the concrete action it requires. Squarely on the policy.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But I will give it something; at least Chris Hipkins knew that this policy was being announced.
civility.explanation: A sneer aimed at a named individual, implying Hipkins is usually not told what his own party is doing. Short of a direct insult but it imputes incompetence to the person rather than engaging the policy.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The turn around is on: strong wool—I should have told the Prime Minister this; he could have quoted it earlier—up 32 percent this year; fine wool: up 34 percent; and mid-micron wool up 41 percent.
specificity.explanation: Three named wool categories each with a precise percentage change over a stated period. Directly checkable against price data.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I'm determined that wool will be one of the great comeback stories of New Zealand agriculture, adding to its storied heritage, restoring pride for our growers and wool harvesters, and much needed profitability, back for our hard-working hill country farmers.
specificity.explanation: A string of aspirational virtues — pride, heritage, profitability — with no figure, mechanism, target or timeframe. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Two hundred people every day—a plane load every day—are now going offshore because they can no longer find the opportunities for them, for their children, and for their families.
specificity.explanation: A precise rate — 200 people per day — attached to a named phenomenon. Directly checkable against migration statistics.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: This revival hasn't happened by accident. There has been strong leadership from the Government, and the sector is rallying; it is uniting.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc attribution: the price recovery is asserted to be caused by government leadership with nothing offered to connect the two — no mechanism, no counterfactual, no timing evidence. Denying coincidence is not the same as showing causation.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If we're not prepared to use wool in our own buildings, how can we ask anyone else?
rigor.explanation: A consistency argument for the procurement policy: domestic use is offered as a precondition for credibly promoting wool abroad. The inference is reasonable, though it leans on an appeal to consistency rather than evidence that the market signal actually works.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: To the member’s point: you can say that Labour copied you—however, the problem is, I couldn’t find any detail on your particular policy to be able to copy.
rigor.explanation: A valid rebuttal in form: if the accusing party's policy carries no published detail, there was nothing to copy. It rests on the speaker's own inability to find detail rather than on a demonstration that none exists, which is a mild argument from absence.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: There’s going to be growing migration, growing business liquidations.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that both outward migration and business liquidations will continue to increase after October 2025.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ migration estimates and NZ Companies Office / Centrix liquidation counts for the 12 months from October 2025; true if both outward migration and liquidations rise relative to the preceding 12 months, false if either falls.

civility.statement: Which just goes to show that when Chris Hipkins stood up there to use someone else's homework, he didn't read to the end of the document.
civility.explanation: Imputes plagiarism and laziness to a named individual ('use someone else's homework', 'didn't read to the end'). Short of a direct insult but it sneers at the person rather than engaging the policy, which under the re-anchored scale is a genuine failure.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: One small word of advice to Mr Hipkins, who doesn't take advice well: read to the end of the policy.
civility.explanation: The parenthetical 'who doesn't take advice well' is a condescending aside about the person's character rather than about the policy; the advice framing is patronising rather than substantive.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: In the last two years, this Government has reduced inflation, got it down from record levels to one now that businesses have confidence to invest.
focus.explanation: Squarely about a named economic outcome (inflation) and its effect on business investment. Defending the government's record on a specific measure is policy content, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And actually, it was a line that was drawn when Labour forgot about Te Tiriti o Waitangi, hapū, and iwi who never surrendered their foreshore and seabed.
focus.explanation: Criticises another party, but anchored to a specific and identifiable policy episode — the foreshore and seabed legislation and Treaty obligations — rather than generalised party-bashing. Named policy content keeps this well above the tribalism floor, though the framing is partly about Labour as a party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: What we have heard—and I'm going to say this straight up for everyone to hear—is that nothing that is going on in Te Pāti Māori is as rotten as some of the things that we have gone and seen in other parties.
focus.explanation: Entirely a comparison of party conduct — no policy, measure, figure or outcome is named. The point is that other parties are worse, which is exactly the content-free party framing Focus exists to catch. No argument survives removing the part about the other side, so nothing is emitted for Rigor.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: In the last two years, this Government has reduced inflation, got it down from record levels to one now that businesses have confidence to invest.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that inflation was at record levels two years prior and has since been reduced under this Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI annual inflation series: compare the annual rate for the September 2023 quarter (start of the two-year window) with the most recent quarter before 22 October 2025. True if the rate has materially fallen AND the 2023 level was a record high in the CPI series; false if the rate has not fallen, or if 'record levels' is wrong because higher annual rates appear earlier in the series (e.g. the 1970s-80s).

veracity.statement: And we have seen a trade negotiation start with India when that Government, Labour, said it was not a priority for them: $12 billion of extra exports.
veracity.explanation: Three assertions: that NZ-India FTA negotiations have begun; that the previous Labour government said India was not a priority; and that the deal carries $12 billion of extra exports.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: (a) MFAT trade agreement pages / official announcements on whether NZ-India FTA negotiations formally launched before 22 October 2025; (b) statements by Labour trade ministers 2017-2023 on India's priority in the FTA programme; (c) the source of the $12 billion figure — official MFAT/NZIER modelling. True if negotiations launched, Labour is on record deprioritising India, and $12bn traces to a published estimate; false if any of the three is contradicted.

veracity.statement: We have reduced ram raids from records high all over the country, when New Zealanders were just expecting when they got out of bed there would be another ram raid in their community to now a level so low that we hardly hear about them.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that ram raid offending peaked at record levels and has since fallen to a very low level under this Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police retail crime / ram raid offence counts by month, 2022 through 2025. True if monthly ram raid counts peaked in the 2022-23 period and the most recent 2025 figures are down substantially (e.g. a majority reduction); false if counts are flat, rising, or the reduction is marginal.

veracity.statement: Anybody who doesn't know that really just has to understand that 80 percent of all our goods exports that go overseas come from the primary sector.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the primary sector accounts for 80 percent of New Zealand's goods exports.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries / Stats NZ merchandise trade data for the year to 2025: primary sector share of total goods exports by value. True if approximately 80% (say 75-85%), false if materially outside that band.

veracity.statement: In fact, what we want to do is acknowledge the fact that people in Aotearoa are leaving in droves.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that people are emigrating from New Zealand at an unusually high rate.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ international migration estimates: annual departures of New Zealand citizens, and net migration loss of NZ citizens, for the years to 2024 and 2025 compared with the pre-2020 historical range. True if citizen departures or net citizen outflow are at or near series records; false if they sit within the ordinary historical range.

veracity.statement: We have $629.4 billion fraud that goes on in this country, and this country does nothing about it.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that tax evasion / fraud in New Zealand amounts to $629.4 billion, set against $80 million of welfare fraud said to be 1 percent of the total.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: IRD tax gap estimates and any Treasury or academic estimate of total fraud/tax evasion in New Zealand, compared against NZ nominal GDP (~$430bn). True if a credible published estimate puts the figure at approximately $629.4 billion; false if published estimates are orders of magnitude lower, or if the figure is internally inconsistent with the accompanying claim that $80 million is 1 percent of it (which would imply $8 billion).

specificity.statement: And we have seen a trade negotiation start with India when that Government, Labour, said it was not a priority for them: $12 billion of extra exports.
