specificity.explanation: Names the exact change sought — the commencement date moved from one stated date to another stated date — so a member could act on it or check it against the amendment paper. Short of 1.0 only because no reason for the twelve-month shift is supplied.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Currently, the commencement date is quite specific. It’s 1 January 2024.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a fact about the text of the bill under consideration — that clause 2 fixes commencement at 1 January 2024 rather than tying it to Royal assent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Clause 2 of the Land Transport (Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme Repeal) Amendment Bill as before the committee of the whole House on 12 December 2023: true if clause 2 states the Act comes into force on 1 January 2024, false if it specifies any other commencement (e.g. the day after Royal assent, or a different date).

veracity.statement: Today, our incomes are 66 percent lower than the Swiss, and we rank only in the mid-30s.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand per-capita incomes are 66 percent below Switzerland's and that New Zealand ranks somewhere in the mid-30s internationally on that measure.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: OECD/World Bank GDP or income per capita (PPP and nominal) for New Zealand and Switzerland for the most recent year before December 2023: true if the New Zealand figure is approximately 66% below the Swiss figure and New Zealand's international rank on that series is in the low-to-mid 30s; false if the gap or the rank is materially different (e.g. a gap nearer 45-50%, or a rank in the 20s).

veracity.statement: In the 1950s, some assessments had New Zealanders enjoying the world’s third-highest per capita incomes, equivalent to Switzerland.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that at least some historical assessments placed New Zealand third in the world for per-capita income during the 1950s, on par with Switzerland.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Maddison Project / historical national accounts estimates of GDP per capita by country for the 1950s: true if New Zealand appears at or about third place in at least one recognised series for a year in that decade with a level comparable to Switzerland's; false if no such series places New Zealand near third.

veracity.statement: Mortgage rates touched an eye-watering 20 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand residential mortgage interest rates reached approximately 20 percent during the Rogernomics period referred to in the surrounding sentences.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: RBNZ historical series for new residential mortgage / first mortgage interest rates, 1984-1990: true if the peak rate reaches approximately 20% or above in that window; false if the peak is materially below (e.g. under 17%).

veracity.statement: Rail was saved by sacking three-quarters of the staff.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the restructuring of New Zealand's railways in the Rogernomics period cut roughly 75 percent of the rail workforce.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Railways Corporation employment figures before and after the 1986-1990 restructuring (annual reports / Treasury and NZ Railways corporate records): true if headcount fell by approximately three-quarters over that restructuring; false if the reduction is materially smaller (e.g. around half) over the period referred to.

veracity.statement: Then, after being re-elected, Labour went on a massive State asset sale programme, and I’m not sure that they signalled that very clearly.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a large programme of State asset sales followed Labour's 1987 re-election, and that it was not clearly signalled to voters beforehand.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury / State-owned enterprise privatisation records for 1988-1990 (list and value of assets sold), plus Labour's 1987 election manifesto: true if a substantial sale programme ran after the 1987 election and the 1987 manifesto did not set out that programme; false if the sales were small in scale or were set out in the manifesto.

veracity.statement: Zealandia has a staggering 16,000 members paid up and 600 active volunteers.
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific membership and volunteer numbers for the Zealandia sanctuary as at late 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Zealandia's annual report / Karori Sanctuary Trust financial statements for the year to mid-2023: true if paid-up membership is about 16,000 and active volunteers about 600; false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: Wellington’s Miramar Peninsula has recently become the first urban area on the planet to eradicate introduced predators, including rats.
veracity.explanation: Asserts both that introduced predators including rats had been eradicated from the Miramar Peninsula by December 2023, and that this was a world first for an urban area.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Predator Free Wellington / DOC announcements and monitoring reports on Miramar Peninsula eradication status as at December 2023, plus any prior claim of urban predator eradication elsewhere: true if eradication of rats and other named predators had been declared for Miramar by that date and no earlier urban eradication is documented; false if eradication had not yet been declared (e.g. residual rat detections ongoing) or an earlier urban precedent exists.

rigor.statement: Imagine if everyone earned 66 percent more. We probably wouldn’t be having half the arguments we do.
rigor.explanation: A non sequitur: nothing is offered to connect a rise in incomes to a reduction in political disagreement, and the inference simply asserts that the second would follow from the first. The passage is squarely about economic performance, so this is a reasoning failure rather than an off-policy jibe.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We need to be smarter; invest more in technology, research, and development; and support emerging creative businesses better.
specificity.explanation: A list of generic directions with no figures, mechanisms, timeframes or named programmes; the surrounding sentences continue in the same register (grow savings, reduce regulation) without supplying detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Provincial Growth Fund in Marlborough helped to fund a number of incentives, including the now completed Blenheim Library.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Provincial Growth Fund contributed funding to projects in Marlborough, specifically the Blenheim library, and that the library was complete as at December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE/Provincial Growth Fund funding announcements and contracts for Marlborough, plus Marlborough District Council records for the Blenheim library project; true if PGF money went to the library project and the building was open by December 2023, false if the library was funded entirely from other sources or was still incomplete at that date.

veracity.statement: The result was that I was the highest polling Blenheim Ward councillor, something I have achieved now five times in a row.
veracity.explanation: Claims he topped the vote in the Blenheim Ward at five consecutive Marlborough District Council elections (2010 through 2022).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Marlborough District Council declared election results for the Blenheim Ward for 2010, 2013, 2016, 2019 and 2022; true if he received the highest vote count in the ward at each of those five elections, false if another candidate polled higher in any of them.

focus.statement: The constant and major reforms like three waters and many more, have taken a major toll on the relationship between councils and central government.
focus.explanation: Names a specific reform programme (three waters) and identifies a concrete consequence for local government. Criticism of a named policy and its effect is scrutiny, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Many of those remote sites will never be seen by the majority of New Zealanders, so to stop development on amenity or landscape values, in my view, needs to be reconsidered.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the policy — the specific RMA grounds (amenity values, outstanding natural landscapes) on which offshore aquaculture applications are declined. No party content at all.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The previous Government often called for submissions but, in many people’s views, did not take the time to hear or listen to what people had to say.
civility.explanation: Criticises the previous Government's handling of consultation, hedged as other people's view. Pointed about a record rather than any individual; edges toward imputing indifference but lands on the process, not a person.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Many of those remote sites will never be seen by the majority of New Zealanders, so to stop development on amenity or landscape values, in my view, needs to be reconsidered.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real consenting rule, but with a gap: it treats amenity and landscape protection as resting solely on how many people view a site, when those provisions also cover intrinsic and ecological values. The conclusion is broader than the premise supports.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: With our rural regions and primary production, it is important that we don’t forget that our rural regions account for much of the country’s GDP. If our rural regions are supported, our economy will grow.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion overreaches the premise: a sector's share of GDP does not establish that support directed to it produces net growth, since nothing is offered about what that support costs or displaces. An enthymeme with the load-bearing step missing.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I have witnessed the worst of the RMA when those wanting to expand or try something new were stonewalled by legislation and environmental scaremongering.
specificity.explanation: Trying to convey substance about RMA failure but supplies nothing checkable: no application, provision, sector, cost or timeframe is named — only a general characterisation of being blocked.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I want us to move forward as one, but we seem to be a country with an identity crisis.
specificity.explanation: A statement of aspiration on Māori-Crown relations with no mechanism, measure or action attached; nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Which is why I’m committed, during my time in Parliament, alongside my fellow colleagues, to take heed and do what we can to reverse the declining outcomes we are seeing in our education system; to be a voice for our children and youth, who are our future; to show them, and their parents if necessary, that it is possible to choose a different path; and to break one’s self-defeating patterns, to see one’s worth, and, in time, to experience what is possible for their future.
specificity.explanation: A stated policy direction with no mechanism, figure, named programme or timeframe — 'do what we can', 'be a voice', 'show them' are aspirational framings. Nothing here could be checked or acted on. Comparable to the string-of-virtues example in the rubric.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I will work tirelessly to ensure our seniors are not forgotten.
specificity.explanation: A commitment with no content: no policy named, no measure, no threshold for what 'not forgotten' would mean. She could have named superannuation settings, aged-care funding or a service, and did not.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Which is why I’m committed, during my time in Parliament, alongside my fellow colleagues, to take heed and do what we can to reverse the declining outcomes we are seeing in our education system; to be a voice for our children and youth, who are our future; to show them, and their parents if necessary, that it is possible to choose a different path; and to break one’s self-defeating patterns, to see one’s worth, and, in time, to experience what is possible for their future.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as present fact that outcomes in the New Zealand education system are declining. The commitment wrapped around it is not the claim; the embedded factual premise is.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ education outcome series over the decade to 2023: OECD PISA reading, maths and science scores for New Zealand across the 2012, 2015, 2018 and 2022 cycles, and Ministry of Education regular-attendance rates over the same period. True if these show a material decline; false if they are flat or improving.

specificity.statement: This bill, which repeals Labour’s regressive ute tax—inequitable ute tax—scheme, is now before Parliament, ready to be passed into law, to end the ute tax on 31 December 2023.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific measure being repealed and the exact date the charge ends (31 December 2023). Checkable and actionable, though it gives no figures on scale or cost.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Climate change is indeed an extremely pressing issue, but what the Government is doing with this piece of legislation is they are heading in the wrong direction when it comes to addressing climate change—providing an opportunity to meet the needs that our communities need to take up the responsibilities to do their bit when it comes to addressing that pressing issue of climate change.
specificity.explanation: Trying to convey substance about climate policy but supplies no figures, mechanism, emissions measure or timeframe — 'wrong direction', 'do their bit' and 'take up responsibilities' commit to nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But they have cited—and I used this earlier today—that the research that they’ve provided to all members of the House shows that the new Government’s policy that they are seeking to progress under urgency this evening, to remove the discount and also to weaken the Clean Car Standard, would mean between 100,000 and 350,000 fewer electric vehicles (EVs) on the roads in New Zealand by 2030.
specificity.explanation: Names the two policy changes, cites a numeric range and a date, and attributes the figures to an identified source, so the claim can be traced and checked.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: This Government was elected with all three parties—National, ACT, and New Zealand First—committing to the repeal of the ute tax as part of our coalition agreement, and this bill gives effect to that as part of our 100-day plan.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that all three governing parties committed to repealing the Clean Car Discount in the November 2023 coalition agreements, and that the repeal is a listed 100-day plan item.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published National–ACT and National–New Zealand First coalition agreements (24 November 2023) and the Government's published 100-day plan; true if repeal of the Clean Car Discount appears as a commitment across those documents, false if it appears in none or only one of them.

veracity.statement: As I’ve said in my other reading speeches on this particular piece of legislation, the policy which was put in place by the prior Government was fiscally irresponsible—a $300 million deficit left behind by the previous Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific figure: that the Clean Vehicle Discount scheme was carrying roughly a $300 million deficit at the time of the change of government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / NZ Transport Agency financial reporting on the Clean Vehicle Discount scheme (rebates paid less fees collected) to late 2023, and Treasury/Budget forecasts of the scheme's net position; true if the cumulative or forecast shortfall is approximately $300 million, false if it is materially smaller or the scheme was in surplus.

veracity.statement: Yet we know that with the changes that the Labour Government had put in place in July of this year, already the take of the rebate is $33 million higher than the actual cost.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that following the July 2023 rebalancing of fees and rebates, the Clean Vehicle Discount scheme's revenue exceeded its costs by $33 million.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Transport Agency Clean Vehicle Discount scheme revenue and expenditure reporting for the period from July 2023 to December 2023; true if fees collected exceed rebates paid by approximately $33 million over that period, false if the scheme was in deficit or the surplus is materially different.

veracity.statement: Well, I look forward to their arguments about them progressing their smoke-free legislative change that they didn’t go to the community or to the electorate about, saying that they were going to change that—shame on them; shame on them.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the incoming Government's planned changes to the smokefree legislation were not put to voters or consulted on before the election.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2023 election manifestos and published campaign policy of National, ACT and New Zealand First, plus the November 2023 coalition agreements; true if repeal of the smokefree amendments (denicotinisation, retailer reduction, smokefree generation) appears in none of the pre-election policy documents and first appears in the coalition agreements, false if any party campaigned on it.

rigor.statement: It was inequitable, by taking money from people who have very little or no choice as to what type of vehicle they can use and giving money to people who can already afford to buy electric vehicles.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference: if the fee falls on buyers with no alternative and the rebate flows to buyers who could pay anyway, the transfer is regressive. The conclusion tracks the premises, but the premises are asserted rather than shown, and the step from 'a high-emission vehicle' to 'no choice' is assumed rather than argued.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So what this Government is doing is in a point in time they are removing a particular amount of money that has been of benefit to the Government and the Crown when they are so concerned about things being fiscally more responsible and indeed unsustainable.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the measure — the scheme is currently revenue-positive, so repealing it sits awkwardly with a fiscal-responsibility rationale. But it rests on a single point-in-time surplus and never addresses the scheme's cumulative position, so there is a gap between what is shown and the conclusion that the repeal 'does not make any sense'.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It was inequitable, by taking money from people who have very little or no choice as to what type of vehicle they can use and giving money to people who can already afford to buy electric vehicles.
focus.explanation: Engages the mechanism of the scheme directly — who pays the fee, who receives the rebate, and the distributional effect. No party-directed content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Of course, we have members opposite who believe they know better—they know better than communities around the country.
focus.explanation: Characterises the other side's attitude rather than the measure. It gestures at the absence of consultation, but names no policy, figure or outcome — the weight of the line is what the members opposite are like.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, I look forward to their arguments about them progressing their smoke-free legislative change that they didn’t go to the community or to the electorate about, saying that they were going to change that—shame on them; shame on them.
focus.explanation: Names a specific measure — the smokefree legislative change — and makes a real mandate point about it, which is legitimate scrutiny. But the argument is delivered as party framing and closes on 'shame on them', so a substantial part of the statement is about the other side rather than the policy.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We know that there will continue to be an increased uptake of electric vehicles as more and more car manufacturers produce more and more electric vehicles and bring them into New Zealand, and we will continue to invest in the electric vehicle charging infrastructure to support this uptake over time.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that electric vehicle uptake in New Zealand will keep rising after the discount is removed, driven by increased manufacturer supply. (The charging-investment clause is a promise about the speaker's own action and is not part of this forecast.)
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZ Transport Agency motor vehicle registration statistics for new and used light electric vehicles; true if annual EV registrations in 2024 and 2025 exceed the 2023 total, false if annual registrations fall below the 2023 level.

divination.statement: But they have cited—and I used this earlier today—that the research that they’ve provided to all members of the House shows that the new Government’s policy that they are seeking to progress under urgency this evening, to remove the discount and also to weaken the Clean Car Standard, would mean between 100,000 and 350,000 fewer electric vehicles (EVs) on the roads in New Zealand by 2030.
divination.explanation: Relays Drive Electric's forecast that repealing the discount and weakening the Clean Car Standard will leave 100,000–350,000 fewer EVs in the New Zealand fleet by 2030 than would otherwise have been the case. The speaker is reporting the modelling, not asserting it as his own analysis.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: Drive Electric's published modelling and its stated baseline, compared against NZ Transport Agency light-EV fleet statistics at 31 December 2030; true if the observed fleet falls short of that baseline by 100,000–350,000 vehicles, false if the shortfall falls outside that range.

veracity.statement: The Conference of Parties at the UN has made an agreement and made it very clear that we have to transition away from fossil fuels as quickly as possible.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the COP negotiations then concluding produced an agreement calling for a transition away from fossil fuels.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The final COP28 decision text (the first global stocktake outcome, Dubai, December 2023): true if the agreed text calls on parties to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems; false if the adopted text contains no such call.

veracity.statement: He’s committed to achieving them, and yet all of the evidence we’ve received from the Climate Change Commission and the Ministry of Transport says that in order to achieve those carbon budgets, we need a price signal at the point of purchase of vehicles so that people can find it easier to get into more electric vehicles.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that official advice from the Climate Change Commission and the Ministry of Transport identifies a purchase-point price signal on vehicles as necessary to meet the emissions budgets.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Climate Change Commission advice on the emissions budgets and Ministry of Transport advice / regulatory impact statements on the Clean Car Discount: true if those documents state that a price incentive at the point of vehicle purchase is required to meet the transport contribution to the budgets; false if they identify no such requirement or treat it as optional among alternatives.

veracity.statement: I want to give a shoutout—of course, many of the members of the Government, including the Prime Minister and a few senior Ministers, their families took the rebate for their electric vehicles.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Prime Minister and several senior Ministers, or their families, personally claimed Clean Car Discount rebates on electric vehicles.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Clean Car Discount rebate records and contemporaneous reporting / ministerial statements: true if Christopher Luxon and more than one other senior Minister (or their households) claimed the rebate; false if no such claims can be documented for those individuals.

veracity.statement: We will hold the Government to account as we see what the consequences of repealing this are, but, no matter what, they can’t take away the two megatonne of carbon emissions that we saved.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a quantified abatement figure — two megatonnes of CO2 saved — attributable to the Clean Car Discount over its operating period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Ministry for the Environment estimates of lifetime CO2-e abatement attributable to the Clean Car Discount: true if the central estimate is around 2 Mt, false if it is materially lower or the abatement is not attributed to the scheme.

veracity.statement: It disproportionately affects some of the constituents we are most keen to represent, particularly the rural community, who this ute tax unfairly affected.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Clean Car Discount's fees on high-emitting vehicles fell disproportionately on rural purchasers.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA / Ministry of Transport data on Clean Car Discount fees paid, broken down by region and vehicle type: true if rural purchasers paid a share of fees materially above their share of new-vehicle registrations; false if fee incidence tracked registrations or was concentrated in urban areas.

rigor.statement: If the Government—the National - ACT - New Zealand First Government—cared one bit for equity, they wouldn’t be proposing substantial tax cuts for the people who have the most money. They wouldn’t be proposing tax breaks for landlords. They wouldn’t be proposing or actually undertaking the repeal of fair pay agreements.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about three named policies, but it infers a motive (not caring about equity) from policy choices — the conclusion about intent goes further than the premises support, and it treats the speaker's own distributive priorities as the only possible reading of 'equity'.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: As I’ve already made clear, and as members will soon see, if you don’t have the price incentive at the point of purchase, you will get less uptake of the low-emissions vehicles, and then, if you’re relying on the emissions trading scheme, you will see higher fuel prices and people will have no choice to avoid those higher fuel prices because they’ve already purchased a vehicle that isn’t as fuel-efficient as it could be.
rigor.explanation: A genuine causal argument distinguishing a one-off purchase-price signal from a recurring fuel-price signal, and the conclusion largely tracks the mechanism offered; marked down because 'no choice to avoid those higher fuel prices' overstates — vehicle owners retain resale, mileage and mode options.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: As I’ve already made clear, and as members will soon see, if you don’t have the price incentive at the point of purchase, you will get less uptake of the low-emissions vehicles, and then, if you’re relying on the emissions trading scheme, you will see higher fuel prices and people will have no choice to avoid those higher fuel prices because they’ve already purchased a vehicle that isn’t as fuel-efficient as it could be.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that removing the purchase-price incentive will reduce uptake of low-emissions vehicles, leaving buyers locked into less fuel-efficient vehicles when carbon-priced fuel costs rise.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA light-vehicle registration statistics for 2024 compared with 2023: true if the share of new zero- and low-emissions vehicles in registrations falls materially after the Clean Car Discount ends; false if that share holds steady or rises.

focus.statement: The new National - ACT - New Zealand First Government was elected on a hodgepodge of culture war slogans that were seeking to divide New Zealand rather than constructive positive, practical, evidence-based policies that will help us address the challenges that we actually have.
focus.explanation: Entirely a characterisation of the other parties' campaign and motives. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named, and nothing here bears on the bill before the House.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But, see, this is the difficulty in dealing—they’re so far down the rabbit hole, so out of touch with reality, that this new dinosaur Government doesn’t understand that decades of Government policy have led to a situation where New Zealanders have no choice but to use a car.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy claim inside it — that decades of transport investment decisions produced car dependence — but the weight of the sentence is party framing ('rabbit hole', 'dinosaur Government', 'out of touch').
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What this Government is doing is actually restoring a sensible, coherent climate change policy that will actually work.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic virtues — sensible, coherent, will work — with no mechanism, no figure, no timeframe and no named replacement policy. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Of course, there’s actually only been one one-party majority Government in the entire history of MMP in New Zealand, but there was concern back in 1996 about whether or not this would politicise the role of the Governor-General and that they may have to choose who got to be the Government—of course, it turns out that the man who gets to often choose the Government is still here.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that exactly one government since the introduction of MMP in New Zealand has been formed by a single party holding a parliamentary majority.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Electoral Commission / Parliamentary Library records of seat counts after each MMP general election (1996, 1999, 2002, 2005, 2008, 2011, 2014, 2017, 2020, 2023); true if exactly one of those elections produced a single party with 50%+ of seats governing alone, false if none or more than one did.

focus.statement: It’s taking no options away for urban people. They can still buy their Teslas. This is a deeply regressive tax for rural communities. It is a direct transfer of money from rural to urban, particularly utes.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the House: who bears the fee, who receives the rebate, and the distributive effect of the Clean Car Discount. No party-bashing content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This Government had an opportunity to achieve a net marginal abatement cost, and, frankly, I find that stunning coming from that side of the Whare which purports to know something about business.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy point here (the scheme's marginal abatement cost), but half the sentence is spent on what the other side of the House pretends to be rather than on the measure. A genuine argument wrapped in party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I want to celebrate a little bit on behalf of New Zealanders who, thanks to the Clean Car Discount and Clean Car Standard, have a greater choice thanks to applying those mechanisms at the supply side so that the vehicle importers could bring a wider choice of electric vehicles into the country and at a faster rate.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the named policies and the mechanism by which they are said to work — supply-side obligations on importers changing the range of vehicles available. No content about the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This ute tax and Clean Car Discount is a reverse Robin Hood scheme which is taxing hard-working Kiwis, for the vehicles they need, to subsidise other people to buy new cars.
focus.explanation: Engages the scheme's actual mechanism — who pays the fee and who receives the subsidy — rather than the opposition party. Loaded framing ('reverse Robin Hood') but the substance is the policy.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: To our hard-working famers and tradies: you have done it tough for the last six years. Under the previous Government, you were public enemy number one. Well, under this Government, we back you.
focus.explanation: No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named. It is a characterisation of how the previous government supposedly regarded a group of voters, set against a general assurance of support — party framing with no policy content to hold on to.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: It’s taking no options away for urban people. They can still buy their Teslas. This is a deeply regressive tax for rural communities. It is a direct transfer of money from rural to urban, particularly utes.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Clean Car Discount operates as a net financial transfer out of rural communities and into urban ones, with ute owners as the main payers.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Waka Kotahi Clean Car Discount scheme data: true if the rebates were funded by fees levied on high-emission vehicles (utes prominent among them) AND fee-paying registrations skew rural while rebated EV registrations skew urban; false if rebates were funded from general revenue or the fee/rebate split does not track a rural-urban divide.

veracity.statement: Irrespective of, you know, what’s going to go down today with respect to this bill, 2 megatonnes of carbon dioxide were saved thanks to this policy.
veracity.explanation: Attributes roughly 2 Mt of carbon dioxide abatement to the Clean Car Discount scheme.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published Ministry of Transport / Ministry for the Environment estimates of CO2 emissions abated by the Clean Car Discount; true if the official abatement estimate is approximately 2 megatonnes CO2-e, false if the official figure is materially lower or no such estimate supports that magnitude.

veracity.statement: We see many overseas examples where the mechanism has been in place for more than 20 years and they have achieved fiscal neutrality.
veracity.explanation: Claims that multiple overseas feebate schemes have operated for over two decades and have proved fiscally neutral (fees covering rebates).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Documentation of vehicle feebate / bonus-malus schemes internationally (e.g. France's bonus-malus, Nordic registration-tax regimes) with their start dates and fiscal outturns; true if several such schemes have run more than 20 years and independent accounts show fees covering rebates, false if the long-running examples are few or ran persistent deficits requiring top-ups.

rigor.statement: They’re not lifestyle choices, as the member over there tried to articulate before. They carry tools, they carry stock feed, they carry the dogs, they carry injured stock at times, and those utes don’t have viable alternatives. They don’t live near a cycle lane.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference about the policy: concrete working uses are offered to support the conclusion that utes are a necessity rather than a discretionary purchase. Weakened by the bare assertion that no viable alternative exists (nothing is offered on alternative vehicles), and by restating the opposing position in its weakest form ('lifestyle choices').
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So those are the sort of people that you’re not thinking about when you’re having your intellectual arguments about whether urban people have choices.
civility.explanation: Imputes indifference to members opposite — that they are 'not thinking about' distressed rural families — and dismisses their contributions as merely 'intellectual'. Condescending and edging into bad faith, though short of a direct insult.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Irrespective of, you know, what’s going to go down today with respect to this bill, 2 megatonnes of carbon dioxide were saved thanks to this policy.
specificity.explanation: A named policy attached to a quantified outcome in a stated unit — precise enough for someone else to go and check the abatement figure.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: More than 50 nations have been affected in more than 30 attacks by the Houthi on ships in recent months.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two countable quantities: the number of Houthi attacks on shipping in the months preceding January 2024, and the number of nations affected by them.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Coalition/US CENTCOM and IMO tallies of Houthi attacks on commercial and naval shipping from roughly November 2023 to 30 January 2024, plus the flag/ownership/crew nationalities recorded for the vessels struck; true if the attack count exceeds 30 and the affected-nation count exceeds 50, false if either is materially lower.

veracity.statement: Disruptions to shipping in the Red Sea and Suez Canal mean higher costs for New Zealanders—in fact, nearly 15 percent of global trade flows through this shipping lane.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that close to 15 percent of world trade transits the Red Sea / Suez Canal route.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Suez Canal Authority and UNCTAD figures for the share of global trade (by volume or value) transiting the Suez Canal in 2022-23; true if the share is close to 15 percent, false if materially below (e.g. under 10 percent) or above.

veracity.statement: The Labour Party has made their position clear: that we should not be involved in this conflict. There’s no UN resolution in favour of such actions, and there are countries in Europe and Scandinavia that are against joining this conflict.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that no United Nations resolution supports the coalition military action against Houthi targets, as at 30 January 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: UN Security Council resolutions adopted between October 2023 and 30 January 2024 concerning the Red Sea and Houthi attacks, in particular Resolution 2722; true if none of them authorises or endorses military action against Houthi targets, false if any does.

veracity.statement: In the Minister’s statement she talked with respect to adding hugely inflationary costs to New Zealanders.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a fact about what the Minister said in the ministerial statement delivered minutes earlier — specifically that she described the Red Sea disruption as adding 'hugely inflationary' costs.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of Collins's ministerial statement of 30 January 2024 as recorded in Hansard; true if it characterises the disruption as adding hugely inflationary costs, false if it makes only a weaker claim (e.g. 'higher costs for New Zealanders') or no cost claim at all.

specificity.statement: The NZDF personnel being deployed will support coalition forces to carry out precision attacks on identified Houthi military targets. They will be in roles in operational headquarters in the wider Middle East region and elsewhere. None of our personnel will enter Yemen.
specificity.explanation: States the function of the deployment, where the personnel will be posted, and an explicit geographic limit. Missing only numbers already given elsewhere; the roles are described in operational terms rather than generalities.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Very happy to advise the member in the House that the deployment will be finishing before or on 31 July this year, so that’s when, after that, I’d expect families will be able to see their loved ones again, and the costing is around $500,000, and that’s being paid for within NZDF baselines.
specificity.explanation: An end date, a dollar figure and the funding source, all in one answer. Fully checkable and actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, there are two options: one was to deploy a number of personnel, and the second was to deploy six, so those were the options and Cabinet agreed.
specificity.explanation: Only one of the two options is defined; the alternative is 'a number of personnel', with no size, role, cost or risk attached. A real opportunity to lay out the costed alternatives was available and not taken.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: My first series of questions to the Minister is: how long is this deployment intended for? Is it costed, and when can the families of these personnel expect them home; sooner or later?
specificity.explanation: Asks for three defined things — duration, cost, and return date — so the answer is checkable against what is asked. It carries no figures of its own, which caps it below the top.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: What he should take it as is being that the New Zealand Defence Force has been left in a very difficult position after six—well, actually, the last three years of neglect, and that, clearly, promises that were made by a previous Minister, himself, to Defence around capital funding have not been complied with.
focus.explanation: Names a real policy area — Defence capital funding commitments — which is legitimate accountability content, but it is reached by pivoting away from the question about future deployments into the previous government's general record ('years of neglect') without naming a project or figure.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: My first series of questions to the Minister is: how long is this deployment intended for? Is it costed, and when can the families of these personnel expect them home; sooner or later?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the House: the duration, cost and terms of the deployment just announced. Scrutiny of a named government decision, with no party content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We have to be very mindful about getting involved in such conflicts, and I don’t believe that the Government have made a clear case for it.
focus.explanation: Directed at the decision itself and the adequacy of the case made for it, not at the governing parties' character or record. It is a general framing rather than an engagement with a specific clause or figure, which holds it just below the top.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So it is outrageous that this debate is being used to attack Defence on funding when, in fact, he’s left Defence in the position that they are.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith to the questioner — that he is misusing the debate — rather than engaging the question he asked. Short of a direct insult, but it attributes motive to the person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Sorry, but the member clearly wasn’t listening to the statement I just read out.
civility.explanation: Condescension aimed at the person's attentiveness rather than a correction of the substance. The correction itself follows separately; this sentence adds only the jab.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So it is outrageous that this debate is being used to attack Defence on funding when, in fact, he’s left Defence in the position that they are.
rigor.explanation: Tu quoque: the conclusion that the member's line of questioning is illegitimate rests entirely on his own past record, not on the merits of the question. It also rests on a strawman — he asked whether further deployments were coming, not whether Defence funding was adequate.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I’m happy to remind him that 15 percent of world trade goes through there, and if anyone really wants to know what happens when our shipping lanes and our supply chains are interrupted, just think back to what happened to New Zealanders and to their lack of buying power when we had the COVID-19 situation.
rigor.explanation: Argument from analogy in answer to a request for evidence. The comparability of a global pandemic's supply-chain shock to disruption of one shipping lane is asserted rather than shown, and the invitation to 'just think back' substitutes recollection for the data that was asked for. The trade-share premise is genuine support, which keeps it above the floor.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The Labour Party has made their position clear: that we should not be involved in this conflict. There’s no UN resolution in favour of such actions, and there are countries in Europe and Scandinavia that are against joining this conflict.
rigor.explanation: Two reasons are offered for the position. The absence of a UN mandate is a genuine reason on the merits; 'other European and Scandinavian countries are against it' is an appeal to the conduct of others, which does not bear on whether the deployment is justified. A real argument, leaning partly on an appeal.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Just to remind the Minister, in her own statement today she clearly sets out that this means higher costs for New Zealanders, which is the thrust of my question. My final question to the Minister with respect to this statement is: given the challenges that she even pointed out in the line of questioning that I’ve presented to her, given the challenges to the New Zealand Defence Force, does the Minister think that this is indeed the priority for the Defence Force?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure at issue: it cites the Minister's own statement about higher costs and asks whether the Red Sea deployment is the right priority for the NZDF. This is named-policy scrutiny, not party-bashing, and scores at the top even though it is an attack on the Government's decision.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Yes, can I just tell the member and the House that the Defence Force are delighted to be trusted to undertake this deployment, that the morale seems to be improving, they are getting to do the work that they came to Defence to do, and they are so happy that they’ve got a Minister who’s on their side.
specificity.explanation: An answer offered as substance but carrying nothing checkable: 'delighted', 'morale seems to be improving', 'happy'. No survey figure, attrition number, mechanism or timeframe that anyone could verify or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The ACT Party supports the deployment, announced 23 January, of the six New Zealand Defence Force personnel to the Middle East to help and assist our partners with current and future military actions against the Houthi targets based in Yemen and the Red Sea.
specificity.explanation: Names the announcement date, the exact number of personnel, the destination and the purpose of the deployment. Every element is checkable against the ministerial statement.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: These attacks are actually forcing ships to take the long route around the Cape of Good Hope, and that’s adding 10 to 15 days on to that journey—10 to 15 days of extra fuel and of wages—and it means fewer journeys.
specificity.explanation: Gives the mechanism (rerouting around the Cape of Good Hope), a quantified effect (10 to 15 extra days) and the cost drivers (fuel, wages, fewer voyages). Concrete enough to be checked against shipping data.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What is really striking is when one looks over a longer time frame: the Stats NZ figures show, for example, that over the last three years, prices have risen a total of 19 percent.
specificity.explanation: A named source, a defined window and a single figure — cumulative CPI growth of 19 percent over three years. Anyone can pull the series and check the arithmetic.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: This Government’s denial—which will lead to some of our questions that I have—that this conflict in Yemen is connected to the war in Gaza is naive and dangerous—at best, wilfully ignorant—because we have seen, quite clearly across the world, that the Houthi have stated that their attacks on shipping are in response to Israel’s bombardment of Gaza and will only stop when a ceasefire is reached.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the policy: premise (the Houthi publicly tie the attacks to Gaza and to a ceasefire) supporting the conclusion (the conflicts are connected, so denying it is unsafe). The gap is that it takes a belligerent's stated motive as establishing the causal link — a reasonable but incomplete step, not a fallacy.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The decision to send the New Zealand Defence Force personnel to the Red Sea has already been agreed, by many different global international relations experts, here and around the world—that it has every chance of escalating violence. Now, that is not even up for debate.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion rests entirely on a bare appeal to authority — unnamed 'international relations experts' — reinforced by declaring the matter closed ('not even up for debate'). No mechanism, evidence or reasoning connecting the deployment to escalation is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, I suggest to her that she looks at that, compared to her statements about how global commentators should be, obviously, influencing our foreign policy.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: the inconsistency only bites if Davidson argued that commentators should set foreign policy, which she did not — she cited expert assessments of escalation risk. The conclusion (that her independent-foreign-policy argument is self-contradictory) follows only from the misdescribed version.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: This Government’s denial—which will lead to some of our questions that I have—that this conflict in Yemen is connected to the war in Gaza is naive and dangerous—at best, wilfully ignorant—because we have seen, quite clearly across the world, that the Houthi have stated that their attacks on shipping are in response to Israel’s bombardment of Gaza and will only stop when a ceasefire is reached.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Houthi leadership has publicly stated its Red Sea shipping attacks are a response to Israel's bombardment of Gaza and will cease on a ceasefire.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public Houthi statements up to 30 January 2024 (Abdul Malik al-Houthi speeches, spokesman Yahya Saree's announcements) as reported by Reuters/AP/BBC; true if they explicitly tie the shipping attacks to Gaza and condition their end on a ceasefire, false if no such statement exists or the stated rationale is different.

veracity.statement: I’d also remind the member that New Zealand has been involved in matters around the Red Sea since 2013.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a continuous New Zealand involvement in Red Sea security matters dating from 2013.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZDF deployment records and ministerial statements on New Zealand contributions to the Combined Maritime Forces / counter-piracy task forces in the Gulf of Aden and Red Sea; true if NZ personnel or assets were committed from 2013 onwards, false if the first such commitment postdates 2013 or was not Red Sea related.

veracity.statement: New Zealand is not going to—and the member may wish to, as she has today—express support for the Houthis.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that Marama Davidson expressed support for the Houthi during this debate.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard record of Marama Davidson's contribution on 30 January 2024; true if she voices approval of or support for the Houthi or their attacks, false if she only reports their stated rationale while opposing the deployment.

veracity.statement: The disruptions in the Red Sea are having a profound effect on the 15 percent—and I clarify that nearly 15 to 16 percent of all the global trade uses these traditional shipping lanes.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that nearly 15-16 percent of all global trade transits the Red Sea / Suez shipping lanes.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: UNCTAD, IMF PortWatch or Suez Canal Authority figures for the share of global trade volume transiting the Suez Canal / Red Sea in 2023; true if the published share is approximately 15-16%, false if it is materially lower or higher (e.g. around 12%).

veracity.statement: These attacks are actually forcing ships to take the long route around the Cape of Good Hope, and that’s adding 10 to 15 days on to that journey—10 to 15 days of extra fuel and of wages—and it means fewer journeys.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Red Sea attacks are diverting shipping around the Cape of Good Hope and that this adds 10 to 15 days to the voyage.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Carrier and industry route data for January 2024 (Maersk/Hapag-Lloyd announcements, Clarksons/Lloyd's List transit figures) on Asia-Europe voyages diverted via the Cape; true if the diversion is documented and the added transit time falls in the 10-15 day range, false if the typical added time is materially outside it.

veracity.statement: Last week, Stats New Zealand released the Consumers Price Index for the final quarter of last year. This showed that inflation was 4.7 percent in the year to December.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the New Zealand annual CPI inflation rate for the year to December 2023 was 4.7 percent, as published by Stats NZ in the January 2024 release.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index release for the December 2023 quarter; true if the annual rate is 4.7%, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: What is really striking is when one looks over a longer time frame: the Stats NZ figures show, for example, that over the last three years, prices have risen a total of 19 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Stats NZ CPI data shows a cumulative price rise of 19 percent over the three years to December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI index levels for the December 2020 and December 2023 quarters; true if the compounded increase is approximately 19%, false if materially different.

civility.statement: Well, I think I found a question in there.
civility.explanation: Condescension aimed at the member rather than at her argument — a put-down of her ability to frame a question. Short of a direct insult, but it engages nothing of the substance and belongs below the expected standard.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: New Zealand is not going to—and the member may wish to, as she has today—express support for the Houthis.
civility.explanation: A personal imputation: it attributes to the member sympathy for an armed group attacking shipping, on the basis that she described the group's stated motives. This lands on her character and loyalties rather than on her argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But I would say to that member that we all love world peace; we’d just like to see a bit more of it.
civility.explanation: Sarcasm directed at the member in place of an answer on a contested question about a ceasefire and public debate. It treats her position as naive posturing rather than engaging it — mockery rather than a direct insult.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Mr Robertson should listen because I think he’ll learn something.
civility.explanation: Condescension aimed at a named member — the implication is that Robertson is ignorant rather than wrong on the substance. Short of a direct insult, but it lands on the person, not the argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: If any Minister or Ministers in his Government have received donations from anyone associated with the tobacco lobby, would he regard that as a conflict of interest and exclude them from decision making on any future changes to smoke-free legislation?
civility.explanation: Framed conditionally and directed at a governance question rather than naming anyone, but the insinuation of a purchased policy decision is unmistakable. Pointed and edging toward imputing bad faith without landing on a named person.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But global factors are not the main contributors to inflation. The Stats NZ figures from last week show that tradables inflation, covering goods and services that are imported or that compete with foreign goods, has dropped significantly. On the other hand, non-tradables inflation has stayed stubbornly high. So domestic factors, rather than global factors, are playing the greatest role in driving inflation right now.
rigor.explanation: A clean inference: the tradables/non-tradables split is the standard decomposition of imported versus domestic price pressure, and if tradables have fallen while non-tradables have not, the conclusion that domestic factors dominate follows. No fallacy; the only gap is that she does not address whether some non-tradables costs have imported inputs.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I disagree completely. The legislation that we are reverting to is the same legislation that has seen a consistent decrease in daily smoking. If you just look at the last year, it’s gone from 8.6 percent in 2022 down to 6.8 percent in 2023. The legislation was working. It was driving smoking rates down, and that’s what we’ll continue to do in Government.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc: the decline in smoking under the existing settings is offered as proof that those settings caused it and that the repealed measures were unnecessary. Nothing is offered to separate the legislation's effect from the long-running downward trend, tax increases or vaping substitution.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, I think the member raises a very good question, which was the problem with the previous Government’s proposed changes to legislation—that it would encourage a black market and would actually lead to increasing levels of crime and ram raids.
rigor.explanation: A causal chain asserted with nothing to connect its links: restricted supply to a black market to 'increasing levels of crime' to ram raids specifically. The final step is a non sequitur — no mechanism or evidence ties tobacco supply restrictions to ram raids.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But global factors are not the main contributors to inflation. The Stats NZ figures from last week show that tradables inflation, covering goods and services that are imported or that compete with foreign goods, has dropped significantly. On the other hand, non-tradables inflation has stayed stubbornly high. So domestic factors, rather than global factors, are playing the greatest role in driving inflation right now.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Stats NZ CPI release of the previous week showed a significant fall in annual tradables inflation while annual non-tradables inflation remained high.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI release for the December 2023 quarter (published 24 January 2024): true if annual tradables inflation fell materially from the previous quarter's print while annual non-tradables inflation was roughly unchanged and higher than tradables; false if tradables did not fall materially or non-tradables was not the higher of the two.

veracity.statement: Well, nothing can instantly make up for a 19 percent increase in costs, but New Zealanders will welcome measures such as cancelling fuel tax increases for the remainder of this term and removing the Auckland regional fuel tax.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealanders' costs have risen 19 percent over the period she is referring to (the recent inflationary run under the previous government).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ consumers price index, all groups: true if the cumulative rise over the period Willis refers to (the roughly three years to the December 2023 quarter, or the previous government's term) is approximately 19 percent; false if the cumulative rise over any reasonable reading of that period is materially different.

veracity.statement: The Government is particularly concerned about the state of kids’ school attendance—we have 55 percent of our kids not going to school regularly.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 55 percent of New Zealand school students do not attend school regularly, on the official definition of regular attendance.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education attendance statistics, regular attendance defined as present for 90 percent or more of half-days: true if the share of students below that threshold in the most recent reported term is approximately 55 percent; false if it is materially lower or higher.

veracity.statement: I disagree completely. The legislation that we are reverting to is the same legislation that has seen a consistent decrease in daily smoking. If you just look at the last year, it’s gone from 8.6 percent in 2022 down to 6.8 percent in 2023. The legislation was working. It was driving smoking rates down, and that’s what we’ll continue to do in Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that daily smoking prevalence fell from 8.6 percent in 2022 to 6.8 percent in 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Health Survey adult daily smoking prevalence for the 2021/22 and 2022/23 survey years: true if the two figures are approximately 8.6 percent and 6.8 percent respectively; false if either differs materially from the figure quoted.

veracity.statement: As has been well canvassed, there is no commitment to support the bill after first reading.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the coalition agreement contains no commitment binding National to support the Treaty Principles Bill at any stage beyond its first reading.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Text of the National–ACT coalition agreement clause on the Treaty Principles Bill: true if the commitment extends no further than supporting the bill at first reading; false if it commits National to support the bill at a later stage (for example, through a select committee process that requires support beyond first reading).

veracity.statement: How much revenue would the Government get from illegally smuggled and sold counterfeit cigarettes that are now dominating the Australian market, with organised crime taking over and the situation getting out of control?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that illicit and counterfeit cigarettes currently dominate the Australian tobacco market and that organised crime has taken it over.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Australian Taxation Office illicit tobacco gap estimates and industry consumption surveys for 2023: true if illicit product accounted for a majority (over 50 percent) of Australian tobacco consumption at the time of the statement; false if the illicit share was a minority of consumption.

veracity.statement: Earlier this month, I announced that I had written to the board of Kāinga Ora—Homes and Communities to make it clear that the number of social houses sitting vacant across New Zealand is completely unacceptable. As of late last year, the total number of vacant social homes in New Zealand was 3,906—5 percent of New Zealand’s total public housing stock. Twenty percent of new public homes delivered by Kāinga Ora—Homes and Communities between June 2022 and October 2023 were still sitting vacant in October last year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 3,906 social homes — 5 percent of public housing stock — were vacant as at late 2023, and that 20 percent of new Kāinga Ora homes delivered between June 2022 and October 2023 were still vacant in October 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Kāinga Ora vacancy reporting and total public housing stock figures for October–December 2023: true if the vacant count is approximately 3,906, that is approximately 5 percent of stock, and approximately 20 percent of homes delivered in the stated window were vacant in October 2023; false if any of the three figures is materially different.

veracity.statement: The letter outlined my disappointment with the numbers, and it made clear my expectation that with over 25,000 families on the social housing wait-list—20,000 more than six years ago—social housing homes should not be left empty for a day longer than absolutely necessary.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the social housing wait-list exceeds 25,000 applicants and is 20,000 higher than it was six years earlier (i.e. around 5,000 in late 2017).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Social Development Housing Register quarterly figures: true if the register stood above 25,000 in the December 2023 quarter and at approximately 5,000 in the corresponding 2017 quarter; false if either figure is materially different from those implied.

veracity.statement: Well, that number is publicly available. From memory, without checking my information, as of 30 September 2023—again, from memory—the number in Lower Hutt City of people on the wait-list was 623, and I would note that that is a fivefold increase compared to October 2017.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 623 applicants from Lower Hutt City were on the social housing register at 30 September 2023, and that this is roughly five times the October 2017 level.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Social Development Housing Register broken down by territorial authority: true if the Lower Hutt City count at 30 September 2023 is approximately 623 and the corresponding late-2017 count is approximately one-fifth of that; false if either figure is materially different.

specificity.statement: Well, nothing can instantly make up for a 19 percent increase in costs, but New Zealanders will welcome measures such as cancelling fuel tax increases for the remainder of this term and removing the Auckland regional fuel tax.
specificity.explanation: Two named, checkable measures (cancelling scheduled fuel tax increases for the term, removing the Auckland regional fuel tax) plus a figure for the cost increase. No dollar amounts or dates attached to the measures, which is what holds it below the top.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I am very proud of our Government’s statements and actions around education, particularly banning mobile phones; making sure we have one hour of maths, reading, and writing every day at primary and intermediate schools; and, importantly, reviewing the curriculum.
specificity.explanation: Three named actions, one with a quantified requirement (an hour a day each of maths, reading and writing) and a named scope (primary and intermediate). No timeframes or funding, and 'reviewing the curriculum' carries no detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We care about our kids. We want them to get well educated so they can have a great future.
specificity.explanation: A pure sentiment: no mechanism, figure, timeframe or named policy. Nobody could check it or act on it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I disagree completely. The legislation that we are reverting to is the same legislation that has seen a consistent decrease in daily smoking. If you just look at the last year, it’s gone from 8.6 percent in 2022 down to 6.8 percent in 2023. The legislation was working. It was driving smoking rates down, and that’s what we’ll continue to do in Government.
specificity.explanation: Two dated figures for daily smoking prevalence and an identified legislative change. Checkable as stated; short of the top only because the measure and source behind the percentages are not named.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Earlier this month, I announced that I had written to the board of Kāinga Ora—Homes and Communities to make it clear that the number of social houses sitting vacant across New Zealand is completely unacceptable. As of late last year, the total number of vacant social homes in New Zealand was 3,906—5 percent of New Zealand’s total public housing stock. Twenty percent of new public homes delivered by Kāinga Ora—Homes and Communities between June 2022 and October 2023 were still sitting vacant in October last year.
specificity.explanation: An exact count, a percentage of stock, a second percentage with a named delivery window and an as-at date, plus the named action taken. Fully checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, that number is publicly available. From memory, without checking my information, as of 30 September 2023—again, from memory—the number in Lower Hutt City of people on the wait-list was 623, and I would note that that is a fivefold increase compared to October 2017.
specificity.explanation: A named territorial authority, an exact figure, an as-at date and a stated multiple against a named baseline. Hedged as being from memory, but entirely checkable as stated.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Yes, I do, and particularly our Government’s statements on education—of course, that member was the Minister of Education for 5½ years.
focus.explanation: Education policy is genuinely the topic, but the content here is a reminder of who held the portfolio rather than anything about a measure, a figure or an outcome. A real policy area wrapped in party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I disagree completely. The legislation that we are reverting to is the same legislation that has seen a consistent decrease in daily smoking. If you just look at the last year, it’s gone from 8.6 percent in 2022 down to 6.8 percent in 2023. The legislation was working. It was driving smoking rates down, and that’s what we’ll continue to do in Government.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure at issue — the smokefree legislation and the prevalence numbers attached to it — rather than on the opposition's character or record in general.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We’re very pleased to see that the current legislation which we’re reverting to has actually driven daily smoking down by two points, back to 6.8, and we’re on track to deliver Smokefree 2025.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that New Zealand will meet the Smokefree 2025 goal — daily smoking prevalence below 5 percent — on the legislative settings being reverted to.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Health Survey adult daily smoking prevalence for the 2025 target period: true if it is below 5 percent (the Smokefree 2025 threshold); false if it remains at or above 5 percent. Māori daily smoking prevalence should be reported alongside, since the goal is framed for all population groups.

civility.statement: The member just needs to learn a little website: www.google.com.
civility.explanation: A sneer at the questioner's competence rather than an answer about the data — condescension aimed at the member, not at her argument. Short of a direct insult, so above 0.25, but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Minister, how did the Government manage to spend so much more money and yet get so much worse results, and is that an example of the previous finance Minister’s fiscal incontinence?
civility.explanation: "Fiscal incontinence" is a bodily-function jibe aimed at a named individual rather than at his spending decisions — a clear personal attack, even though the first half of the question is a legitimate spending-versus-results point.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: How can she reconcile the inclusion of Corrections in the departments to be cut with the commitment in the coalition agreement with ACT to increase its funding, or is this going to be another example of David Seymour’s political impotence?
civility.explanation: The substantive first half is sound, but the tail attacks a named member's personal effectiveness ("political impotence") rather than the coalition commitment itself.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Could I ask the Minister as to whether this is the problem about trying to establish what the relationship means, or is it a fact that on 5 February 1840, no one in the British Empire, from which the sun never set, including the people living next to Queen Victoria in Buckingham Palace, was in partnership with the Queen, how could the Māori be two days later? So it’s a relationship we’re working on now; not the fiction of some people in this Parliament.
civility.explanation: Robust and dismissive — calling other members' understanding "the fiction of some people in this Parliament" edges toward imputing invention to them, but it targets a position and names no one.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does he think it’s acceptable that the Minister leading this bill who has called for a discussion on Te Tiriti, didn’t even show up to Tūrangawaewae and didn’t show up to Rātana where Tiriti kōrero was actually happening?
civility.explanation: Pointed and pressing, and "didn't even" carries an edge, but the charge is about a minister's attendance record in his own portfolio, not about his character or capacity.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: For example, in the case of Health and Education, those agencies have had non-departmental spending excluded from their baseline.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific agencies and the specific mechanism (non-departmental spending removed from the savings baseline). Checkable, though it carries no figure or percentage.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Our savings programme in Budget 2024 is designed to find around $1.5 billion in savings per year, which we’ll use to deliver on our policy commitments and fund critical cost pressures.
specificity.explanation: A named programme, a dollar figure, a period and a stated use for the money. Someone could check it against the Budget.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Has the Minister spoken to the Hon Judith Collins in wake of her comments that she is “going to need money for Defence”, and what specifically in the Defence Force is she aiming to cut?
specificity.explanation: Names a person and quotes her words, and asks for the specific cuts, but supplies no figures, agencies or amounts of its own.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, we haven’t seen a draft Treaty principles bill, but what I can tell you is people should be concerned about improving outcomes for Māori and that’s what this Government is single-mindedly focused on.
specificity.explanation: Beyond noting no draft exists, this offers only a generic aspiration — "improving outcomes for Māori" — with no measure, mechanism, figure or timeframe attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: New Zealanders should take the time to learn about Te Tiriti o Waitangi—the Treaty of Waitangi—and come to their own views.
specificity.explanation: Asked who New Zealanders should believe on the partnership question, the answer commits to nothing checkable — no position, no mechanism, no action.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And this actually goes to the fundamental issue, which is that we are asking the Department of Corrections to look at what resources may have become tied up in the back office so that we can move them into the front line in our prisons.
rigor.explanation: Answers an alleged contradiction (cutting Corrections while promising it more money) with a mechanism that dissolves it: back-office savings and front-line increases are not mutually exclusive. The conclusion follows from the distinction offered; no fallacy.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Could I ask the Minister as to whether this is the problem about trying to establish what the relationship means, or is it a fact that on 5 February 1840, no one in the British Empire, from which the sun never set, including the people living next to Queen Victoria in Buckingham Palace, was in partnership with the Queen, how could the Māori be two days later? So it’s a relationship we’re working on now; not the fiction of some people in this Parliament.
rigor.explanation: False analogy: that no ordinary imperial subject stood in partnership with the Crown says nothing about whether a specific negotiated treaty created one. The general case is offered as if it settled the particular instrument, and the conclusion does not follow from it.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The core Public Service headcount has grown by almost 30 percent since 2018, and Government spending is also expected to have increased by around 80 percent between 2017 and 2024.
veracity.explanation: Two quantitative claims: core public service headcount growth of ~30% from 2018, and total government spending growth of ~80% from 2017 to 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public Service Commission Workforce Data headcount for the core public service, 2018 vs 2023/24 — true if the increase is close to 30%, false if materially below; and Treasury core Crown expenses, 2016/17 vs 2023/24 Financial Statements of the Government — true if the increase is close to 80%, false if materially below.

veracity.statement: To have two-thirds of Māori kids not in school regularly, to see Māori disadvantaged economically, to see poor housing stats, with Māori making up half of people on the social register, those are the conversations that we’re actually having with iwi leaders and with Māori across the country.
veracity.explanation: Two quantified claims: that about two-thirds of Māori students are not regularly attending school, and that Māori make up about half of those on the social housing register.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education attendance statistics for the most recent term before January 2024 — true if the share of Māori students attending regularly (90%+ of half-days) is around one-third or lower, false if materially higher; and the MSD Housing Register quarterly report — true if Māori are around 50% of main applicants, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Does he think it’s acceptable that the Minister leading this bill who has called for a discussion on Te Tiriti, didn’t even show up to Tūrangawaewae and didn’t show up to Rātana where Tiriti kōrero was actually happening?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that David Seymour, as the minister leading the Treaty principles bill, attended neither the Tūrangawaewae national hui nor Rātana.
veracity.subject: speaker
