focus.statement: We have to fund our roads, and the Government opposite us is going to have a massive challenge around how they fund the very many projects that they’ve promised, especially when they add back in the one they’ve taken away from Nelson.
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny on a funding question, pointing at promised transport projects and a specific Nelson project, though it carries some 'the Government opposite' framing rather than naming the figures.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Clean Car Discount was extremely successful, probably more successful than the transport Minister at the time thought it would be.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that EV uptake under the Clean Car Discount exceeded the forecasts held at the time the scheme was introduced.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / NZTA new light EV and plug-in hybrid registration figures for the Clean Car Discount period (July 2021 – December 2023) compared with the uptake projected in the scheme's Regulatory Impact Statement; true if actual registrations materially exceeded the projection, false if they met or fell short of it.

veracity.statement: So there’s been an amendment here where there’s a 50 percent reduction in what they pay so that there is an accounting for the fact—and it’s rough, it’s rough.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the amendment to the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill sets the plug-in hybrid road-user charge at half the rate paid by full electric vehicles.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The bill as reported back from the Transport and Infrastructure Committee, and the RUC rates gazetted for light electric vehicles versus plug-in hybrids; true if the PHEV rate is 50% of the full light-EV rate, false if it is set at any materially different proportion.

veracity.statement: The previous National Government, they put that exemption in place to encourage EV uptake, which, of course, it did, and it was successful.
veracity.explanation: Attributes the original road-user charge exemption for light electric vehicles to a previous National-led government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The enacting legislation for the light electric vehicle RUC exemption (Road User Charges (Exemption Period for Light Electric RUC Vehicles) legislation) and the government in office on its passage; true if enacted under a National-led government, false if enacted under a Labour-led one.

veracity.statement: I will just point out that the Labour Government, in 2022, put out a figure of the 20 percent discount.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous Labour government proposed a 20 percent RUC discount for plug-in hybrids in 2022.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport consultation and Cabinet papers on light electric vehicle road-user charges published in 2022; true if a 20% PHEV discount figure appears there, false if no such figure was proposed or a different figure was.

veracity.statement: That went nowhere, but, luckily, we have settled, through the select committee process, on a figure which is 15 percent, which I think is a fair amount.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the select committee settled the plug-in hybrid discount at 15 percent — a figure that conflicts with the 50 percent stated earlier in the same debate.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Transport and Infrastructure Committee report on the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill and the RUC rates set for plug-in hybrids relative to full electric vehicles; true if the discount is 15%, false if it is any materially different proportion.

veracity.statement: Way back in the day, when nearly all vehicles would have been funded through levies, there were some changes made by the Minister of Transport Annette King to ensure that the levies that were collected all went into transport projects, because they used to actually go into the general taxation pot.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Annette King, as Minister of Transport, made the change that hypothecated fuel excise/levy revenue to transport spending rather than the Crown's general account.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Land Transport Management legislation and Treasury/Ministry of Transport records on when petrol excise duty was fully directed to the National Land Transport Fund, and who held the Transport portfolio at the time; true if the change occurred under Annette King as Minister of Transport, false if it was made by a different minister or in a different way.

specificity.statement: So there’s been an amendment here where there’s a 50 percent reduction in what they pay so that there is an accounting for the fact—and it’s rough, it’s rough.
specificity.explanation: Names the mechanism (a discount on the RUC payable) and gives a figure, though not the dollar rate or the commencement date.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Just on Friday, I was in the mighty Ilam electorate and visited a company that helps repair roads, and you look at the effort they put in—we need to make sure we can support them to make sure we have safe roads.
specificity.explanation: 'Support them' and 'safe roads' commit to no mechanism, amount or timeframe; the only concrete detail is that a visit occurred.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Now, that piece of work means that there’s a whole lot of vehicles out there that are electric and that will now move into the second-hand market and will mean that a whole lot of families that would never be able to buy a car that was new electric will be getting one.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that vehicles bought new under the Clean Car Discount will flow into the used market and put EVs within reach of households that could not buy new.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA used light-EV registration and change-of-ownership data for 2024–2026; true if second-hand EV transfers rise materially over the period and median used EV prices fall, false if used EV volumes are flat or declining.

rigor.statement: But it always was designed to end, and, in the long run, all vehicles need to be part of a road-user charge system so we can have suitable upkeep of our roads.
rigor.explanation: A real inference on the policy: roads require funded upkeep and the exemption was time-limited by design, so all vehicles should eventually contribute. The conclusion tracks the premises, though the step from 'roads need funding' to 'via RUC specifically' is left implicit.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Just on Friday, I was in the mighty Ilam electorate and visited a company that helps repair roads, and you look at the effort they put in—we need to make sure we can support them to make sure we have safe roads.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to anecdote: a single electorate visit is offered as the ground for a general conclusion about supporting road maintenance, with nothing connecting the observation to the policy conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Now, if you compare original hybrids, which mostly fuel on a combustion engine and then use the electric vehicle to top them up, as opposed to plug-in hybrids that are primarily electric vehicles, what we saw in the original drafting of this bill from the Government was an inherent unfairness, where you would have those drivers paying the levies on the petrol that they put into the vehicle, as well as paying the RUC—the road-user charge.
rigor.explanation: A mechanism-level inference: because PHEVs draw on both petrol and electricity, an undiscounted RUC on top of fuel excise charges the same road use twice. The conclusion of unfairness follows from the premises offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Now, if you compare original hybrids, which mostly fuel on a combustion engine and then use the electric vehicle to top them up, as opposed to plug-in hybrids that are primarily electric vehicles, what we saw in the original drafting of this bill from the Government was an inherent unfairness, where you would have those drivers paying the levies on the petrol that they put into the vehicle, as well as paying the RUC—the road-user charge.
civility.explanation: Hard criticism of the Government's drafting as 'inherent unfairness' that attacks no person — the expected standard, and a real opportunity to be uncivil in a contested debate.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: A trade agreement with 450 million people, negotiated with 5 million people, is quite an achievement.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the EU's population is about 450 million and New Zealand's about 5 million at the time of the agreement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Eurostat EU-27 population estimate for 2023-24 and Stats NZ national population estimate for the same period; true if the EU figure rounds to ~450 million and the NZ figure to ~5 million, false if either is materially different.

veracity.statement: So, you know, up to $2.1 billion of additional gain, the largest source of economic gains from the agreement from the services sector—nothing to scoff about at all.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the tabled national interest analysis for the NZ-EU FTA puts additional gain at up to $2.1 billion, with services the largest source of economic gains.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The national interest analysis tabled with the New Zealand-EU Free Trade Agreement; true if it states an economic gain of up to $2.1 billion and identifies services as the largest contributor in absolute terms, false if the headline figure or the leading sector differs.

veracity.statement: The previous Labour Government had signed a free-trade agreement with China.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a Labour-led government signed the New Zealand-China free trade agreement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The signature record of the New Zealand-China Free Trade Agreement (MFAT treaty records); true if it was signed while a Labour-led government held office, false if signed under another government.

veracity.statement: Services that are unlimited in terms of their volume and scope can now trade into the EU with virtually no barriers, and so thank you to the officials for the technical work that they did to keep us in the game.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that under the agreement New Zealand services can be supplied into the EU without volume or scope limits and with virtually no barriers.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The services and investment chapters of the NZ-EU FTA and the EU's annexes of reservations and non-conforming measures; true if the EU schedules no material market-access limitations on New Zealand service suppliers, false if the annexes retain sectoral reservations, quantitative limits or unrecognised-qualification barriers.

specificity.statement: So, you know, up to $2.1 billion of additional gain, the largest source of economic gains from the agreement from the services sector—nothing to scoff about at all.
specificity.explanation: Carries a dollar figure and attributes it to a named sector, so the claim can be looked up in the national interest analysis; it is loosely worded, with no timeframe or baseline for the gain.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It protects geographical indicators, and then it actually allows the EU, in almost an opposite approach, to say that anything produced in any member State can be called “from EU”.
specificity.explanation: Names the particular provisions and describes what each does, so a reader could go to the relevant part of the agreement; stops short of citing clauses or the exceptions.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So what I lay on the Table, with this agreement, is a challenge to the food and beverage sectors—and wine, of course, has a few geographical indicators, as we appreciate the value, but for the other sectors in the finest quality nutrition to the world, let’s develop some of our own and turn those into valuable, clearly identifiable, and unique products for us to sell to the world.
specificity.explanation: Sets a direction — develop New Zealand geographical indicators — but names no product, no process for registering one, no target number and no timeframe, so there is nothing to check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It protects geographical indicators, and then it actually allows the EU, in almost an opposite approach, to say that anything produced in any member State can be called “from EU”.
focus.explanation: Engages a specific mechanism in the measure before the House — the geographical indicators provisions and the EU-wide origin marking — rather than the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The fact that we had a group of vehicle users that did feel that sense of unfairness, where, actually, on reflection, the Minister did go and change his view, shows the flaw in the process that the Government has applied in terms of the short period of time that we had at select committee in order to put this bill through.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real process: submitters felt unfairness, the Minister changed his view, therefore the select committee period was too short. There is a genuine gap — a Minister changing position in response to submissions is at least as consistent with the process working as with it failing — so the conclusion is under-supported rather than fallacious.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The great thing about travelling at that speed is you actually feel safer, you can go faster, and, of course, we know it’s such a great result for more productivity throughout New Zealand.
rigor.explanation: Bare assertion dressed as an inference. Higher speed is asserted to produce a feeling of safety and a national productivity gain, with nothing offered to connect them; 'of course, we know' is an appeal to assumed agreement rather than evidence.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We set a 2 percent target, and we’ve achieved it—we’ve achieved it—and now we need to refine the policy, because it’s achieved what we set out to do.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference — the incentive met its stated target, therefore it should be withdrawn and replaced. It holds only if hitting the target was the whole purpose; no reason is offered against the alternative that the target was a floor. A real argument with a real gap.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And though we’ve been criticised for moving in urgency and moving in a very truncated select committee process, it shows that we’re an open-minded, nimble, pragmatic Government, and this is a case in point.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur. The premise offered is that the Government has been criticised for a truncated process; the conclusion drawn is that it is open-minded and nimble. Being criticised for compressing scrutiny does not evidence open-mindedness, and nothing bridges the two.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The fact that we had a group of vehicle users that did feel that sense of unfairness, where, actually, on reflection, the Minister did go and change his view, shows the flaw in the process that the Government has applied in terms of the short period of time that we had at select committee in order to put this bill through.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the House and the specific process applied to it (select committee time on this bill). No party characterisation; this is scrutiny of a named procedure.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The great thing about travelling at that speed is you actually feel safer, you can go faster, and, of course, we know it’s such a great result for more productivity throughout New Zealand.
focus.explanation: On the policy — expressway speed limits and roading investment — not about the other party. High focus alongside low rigor: he is engaging the subject matter and reasoning poorly about it.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Imagine if we used road maintenance for road maintenance purposes!
focus.explanation: A sneer at the previous government implying maintenance revenue was spent elsewhere. It gestures at a policy area but names no programme, figure or diversion — strip the swipe and no policy content remains. Nothing is emitted for Rigor: a jibe is not an argument.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So there is a lesson here, that, actually, bills like this, which are so fundamental to how we ultimately collect the revenue we need to fund our critical transport infrastructure projects—it just goes to show that we actually do need to allow the committee to have the time that they need to be able to give proper consideration to a bill of this kind.
specificity.explanation: A direction with no checkable content: 'the time that they need' names no number of weeks, no standing order, no threshold. It is trying to convey substance, so it is eligible, but nobody could act on or check it as stated.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, the good thing about this road-user charge (RUC) is it’ll be equitable; it’ll be agnostic to the type of fuel, but it’ll be equitable in that it measures the amount of return we get based on weight and distance travelled.
specificity.explanation: Names the charging mechanism — fuel-agnostic, assessed on weight and distance travelled — which is checkable against the scheme. Carries no rates, thresholds or dates, so it stops short of fully concrete.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I must remind everyone in the House, too, that the primary purpose of the road-user charge is not carbon tax; the primary purpose of the Road User Charges Act 2012 is for this charge to be proportionate to the cost that the vehicle generates, and that’s, today, why we’re talking about weight and distance rather than the use of fuel.
specificity.explanation: Names the statute, states the charging basis (weight and distance) and expressly rules out an alternative basis (fuel). Someone could open the Act and check it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But it was elucidating, through the select committee process, to see that actually 80 percent of our tolling money goes into administration, and that’s far too much.
specificity.explanation: A percentage, a named cost category and a named source (the select committee process). Precise enough that the number can be looked up and contested — separately from whether it is right.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The other good thing is that, when we came into Government, on the back of the previous Government’s 2022 consultation—they went out at 20 percent reduction—we proposed a 30 percent reduction, and I’m so pleased that today we’re all in agreeance on a 50 percent reduction.
specificity.explanation: Three figures, a date, and the sequence of positions attached to them. Fully checkable against the consultation document and the bill as amended.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We set a 2 percent target, and we’ve achieved it—we’ve achieved it—and now we need to refine the policy, because it’s achieved what we set out to do.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a 2 percent electric-vehicle target was set by the National government he credits with the 2009 EV policy, and that it has now been met. Two factual components: that the target existed and was set at 2 percent, and that EV uptake has reached it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2009-era National EV policy documents and Ministry of Transport fleet statistics: true if a 2 percent uptake target is documented and EVs reach at least 2 percent of the New Zealand light vehicle fleet by 2024; false if no such target was set at that figure, or if the fleet share is materially below 2 percent.

veracity.statement: I must remind everyone in the House, too, that the primary purpose of the road-user charge is not carbon tax; the primary purpose of the Road User Charges Act 2012 is for this charge to be proportionate to the cost that the vehicle generates, and that’s, today, why we’re talking about weight and distance rather than the use of fuel.
veracity.explanation: Asserts what the Road User Charges Act 2012 is for: that its charging basis is proportionality to the cost a vehicle imposes, assessed on weight and distance, and that it carries no carbon or emissions purpose.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The purpose and charging provisions of the Road User Charges Act 2012: true if the Act sets charges by vehicle type, weight and distance to reflect the costs vehicles impose on the network and contains no emissions or carbon-pricing purpose; false if the Act states an emissions purpose or a different charging basis.

veracity.statement: But it was elucidating, through the select committee process, to see that actually 80 percent of our tolling money goes into administration, and that’s far too much.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific figure sourced to select committee evidence: that 80 percent of toll revenue collected in New Zealand is consumed by administration costs.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA tolling revenue and collection/administration cost figures, including the evidence given to the select committee on this bill: true if administration accounts for approximately 80 percent of toll revenue, false if the share is materially lower.

veracity.statement: The other good thing is that, when we came into Government, on the back of the previous Government’s 2022 consultation—they went out at 20 percent reduction—we proposed a 30 percent reduction, and I’m so pleased that today we’re all in agreeance on a 50 percent reduction.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a documented sequence of proposed plug-in hybrid RUC discount rates: 20 percent in the previous Government's 2022 consultation, 30 percent proposed by the current Government, and 50 percent as agreed at this stage of the bill.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Ministry of Transport 2022 RUC consultation document and the bill's amendment papers/select committee report: true if the 2022 consultation proposed a 20 percent discount, the Government's proposal was 30 percent, and the rate now before the House is 50 percent; false if any of the three figures differs.

veracity.statement: Because this is important, and I think it’s worth noting, actually, that the EU ratified at their end late last year, which was fantastic to see—late November they ratified it in their Parliament.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the European Parliament ratified the NZ–EU free trade agreement in late November 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: European Parliament plenary voting record on consent to the EU–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement; true if the consent vote occurred in November 2023, false if it fell in a materially different month or year.

veracity.statement: Well, we know that in that period of time, there was COVID, there were massive disruptions, and so for the Hon Damien O’Connor to be able to work alongside officials and steer that home in the way that he did and get it signed, also in the backdrop of signing the UK free-trade agreement, which commenced and concluded in a single term of Government—I don’t think that’s happened before.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the NZ–UK FTA was both commenced and concluded within a single parliamentary term, and that no previous New Zealand free trade agreement had been.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT records of negotiation launch and signature dates for New Zealand's FTAs; true if the NZ–UK negotiations began and were signed within one parliamentary term and no earlier NZ FTA did the same, false if any earlier agreement (e.g. an ASEAN, Korea or Taiwan agreement) also began and concluded inside one term.

veracity.statement: I would note in relation to labour standards that the Council of Trade Unions, New Zealand’s peak body for the labour movement, is raising questions at the International Labour Organization in Geneva about whether or not this Government’s recent moves in the area of employment relations risks putting New Zealand in breach of the commitments we made to the EU under this agreement.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that the NZCTU is currently raising New Zealand's employment relations changes with the ILO in connection with the EU agreement's labour commitments.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZCTU public statements and ILO complaint/observation records from late 2023–early 2024; true if the NZCTU had lodged or publicly raised such a matter with the ILO concerning the Government's employment relations changes, false if no such approach to the ILO existed at the time of the statement.

divination.statement: By us being able to look at having enforcement on 1 May, which is what we’re working towards now with the prompt consideration that the committee is providing on this bill, that will actually provide a direct financial benefit to a number of those exporters in terms of the percentage of product they would otherwise be exporting through that month of May, in particular.

divination.falsification_criterion: MFAT / EU Official Journal record of the entry-into-force date of the NZ–EU FTA; true if it entered into force on or about 1 May 2024 so that May exports received preferential tariff treatment, false if entry into force fell materially later.

specificity.statement: By us being able to look at having enforcement on 1 May, which is what we’re working towards now with the prompt consideration that the committee is providing on this bill, that will actually provide a direct financial benefit to a number of those exporters in terms of the percentage of product they would otherwise be exporting through that month of May, in particular.
specificity.explanation: Names a date, the mechanism (bringing entry into force forward via the committee's report-back), and the affected group, though no dollar figure is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It was their commitment to labour standards; the provisions in the agreement which provide that the parties can hold each other accountable to the commitments that we have made under the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women, the international instrument on gender equality; and our commitments, both the EU and New Zealand, to the Paris climate change commitments.
specificity.explanation: Names the particular provisions and the external instruments they hook into (CEDAW, the Paris commitments) and the accountability mechanism between the parties; someone could go to the agreement text and find them.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I think whenever there is a trade agreement—or, in fact, any sort of negotiation—if both parties come out of it a little dissatisfied, you probably got the balance about right.
rigor.explanation: Answers submitters' concerns about the level of access by appealing to a folk maxim about negotiation rather than to anything about this agreement; mutual dissatisfaction is offered as evidence of balance without any link being shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Ultimately, we got to a position where it was clear through the free-trade agreement itself that did require an administrative mechanism to be established to enable that enforcement to be carried out here in New Zealand alongside the judicial process that could occur.

rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Ultimately, we got to a position where it was clear through the free-trade agreement itself that did require an administrative mechanism to be established to enable that enforcement to be carried out here in New Zealand alongside the judicial process that could occur.

focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I’m not surprised that that member would say this was a minor detail, given his stated intention in some of his portfolios.

veracity.statement: The reason that’s important is because, on entry into force, there’s $100 million worth of tariff savings for New Zealand exporters on day one for the first year.

veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT's national interest analysis / tariff-elimination estimates for the NZ–EU FTA; true if the estimated first-year tariff saving on entry into force is about NZ$100 million, false if the official estimate is materially different.

veracity.statement: There’s a $43 million saving for New Zealand kiwifruit growers as a result of this because 90 percent of their crop going to the European Union will be covered under this agreement and the tariff rate will fall to zero.

veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT NZ–EU FTA tariff schedule for kiwifruit plus the published sector saving estimates (MFAT / Zespri); true if the schedule takes the relevant kiwifruit lines to zero covering ~90% of EU-bound crop and the estimated saving is ~$43m, false if the tariff is only phased or the estimate is materially different.

divination.statement: In the case of kiwifruit, if we can get this work done this week, then the agreement will enter into force on 1 May, not 1 June or July or even 1 August, which was what some people thought it may take the time for the House to get through.

divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The NZ–EU FTA entry-into-force date as recorded by MFAT and the EU Official Journal; true if the agreement entered into force on 1 May 2024, false if it entered into force on any later date (the condition having been met by the bill passing that week).

specificity.statement: So 91 percent of New Zealand’s current goods trade with the EU will enter duty free, increasing to 97 percent over seven years; and $1.3 billion of GDP will be boosted annually, increasing our exports to the EU by up to $1.8 million per year.
specificity.explanation: Carries percentages, a phase-in period and dollar magnitudes for the agreement's effect — precise enough that a listener could check each figure against the negotiated schedule and the modelling.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: To enact that draft would potentially impact many thousands of legitimate trade mark applications, therefore officials have suggested, and I have tabled, recommended Schedule 2 of the bill changes which set out the amendments to section 20(1) of the Trade Marks Act that amends to ensure that only relevant trade mark applications are impacted and not those that are meant to be excluded.
specificity.explanation: Names the schedule, the statutory provision and the exact defect in the drafting being corrected, with the effect of the change stated — checkable against the tabled amendment, though no figures beyond 'many thousands'.

rigor.statement: When it comes to labour standards in the European Union and New Zealand, they’re similar. In some cases, I think New Zealand’s labour standards are higher. A reasonable point resting on an appeal to the speaker's own impression.

civility.statement: I want to touch on a couple of parts of the agreement that have been raised, and I’ll do my best to answer the mischievous question from the Hon Phil Twyford.

specificity.statement: At the moment, there is a system that exists called the New Zealand ePrescription Service, and increasingly, pharmacists are adopting electronic dispensing, so it may well be that, due to advances in technology, we’re not far off the time when people can actually get a record of every purchase of pharmaceuticals and track patterns of people who are strategically shopping to stockpile pseudoephedrine drugs so they can manufacture methamphetamine.

specificity.statement: I think that, across a whole range of activities, everything from farming to finance to teaching to trying to get decent pharmaceuticals, that’s really going to do a lot for New Zealanders’ ability to make a difference in their own lives and those they care about, to provide for themselves and their families, without being restrained by unnecessary rules and regulations.
specificity.explanation: A list of sectors attached to a general benefit. No regulation is named, no mechanism, no figure, no timeframe — nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: At the moment, there is a system that exists called the New Zealand ePrescription Service, and increasingly, pharmacists are adopting electronic dispensing, so it may well be that, due to advances in technology, we’re not far off the time when people can actually get a record of every purchase of pharmaceuticals and track patterns of people who are strategically shopping to stockpile pseudoephedrine drugs so they can manufacture methamphetamine.

focus.explanation: Entirely about the mood and state of the other party during debate on a bill. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named; strip out the commentary on Labour and nothing about the legislation remains. The pseudoephedrine reference is a pun, not policy content.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: On the other hand, there’s strong indications that because, as I was saying earlier, it’s no longer economically viable to make meth out of pseudoephedrine tablets, it’s most likely that that regulation won’t make a great deal of difference.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the proposed register: if domestic manufacture from pseudoephedrine tablets is no longer economic, a register on those purchases has little left to catch. The step follows, though it rests on an unquantified 'strong indications' and does not address displacement or partial substitution.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In this particular instance, we’ve actually done a 13-year trial, if you like, and what we’ve discovered is that the regulation didn’t work.
rigor.explanation: Treats a 13-year period of restriction as if it were a controlled trial. There is no counterfactual: the absence of an observed elimination of methamphetamine does not establish that the restriction had no effect, since the comparison case (no restriction over the same period) was never run. A real inference about the policy, but it leans on an equivocation between 'a long time passed' and 'we tested it'.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: On the other hand, there’s strong indications that because, as I was saying earlier, it’s no longer economically viable to make meth out of pseudoephedrine tablets, it’s most likely that that regulation won’t make a great deal of difference.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as present fact that manufacturing methamphetamine from pseudoephedrine tablets is no longer economically viable in New Zealand — an empirical claim about the current precursor market, separate from the conclusion he draws from it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police / Customs clandestine-laboratory detection figures and NZ Drug Foundation or Police National Drug Intelligence Bureau assessments of methamphetamine supply around 2023-24; true if domestic pseudoephedrine-based manufacture has fallen to a negligible share with supply dominated by imported product, false if pseudoephedrine extraction remains a material manufacturing route.

specificity.statement: Animal welfare was one of the discussions that was had, and we do run different systems of farming, and so, as with the UK, what we agreed to do was not to direct or make judgment on animal welfare standards or indeed labour standards or environment, but to commit to uphold the highest standards that we possibly can and to not lower those standards for any trade advantage.
specificity.explanation: Names the actual mechanism agreed (no directing of each other's standards, plus a non-derogation commitment not to lower standards for trade advantage) and the UK FTA as the precedent, but gives no clause, no threshold and no enforcement detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I’m interested to know the Minister’s view about whether a move to reinstate the live animal trade, which has been subject to much criticism over the years because of the standards, or lack of them, in relation to animal welfare, would risk being in breach of the provisions in the agreement which say that neither party will lower standards or trade benefit.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific policy (reinstating live animal export) and the specific provision it is tested against (the non-derogation clause on standards), which is checkable and answerable; short of the top only because no clause, figure or timeframe is given. A precise question counts as fully as a precise answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: And all it really does is move the drug pseudoephedrine from one schedule of the Misuse of Drugs Act, where it’s a class B drug, to another schedule, where it’s made a class C2 drug.
specificity.explanation: Names the statute, the mechanism (a schedule transfer) and the before and after classifications, so a listener can go and check exactly what the bill does. Falls short of 1.0 only because the schedule parts themselves are not named.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The one unique area which followed on from the UK trade agreement was to have a Māori trade and economic cooperation chapter.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the EU agreement contains a Māori trade and economic cooperation chapter and that this followed on from an equivalent provision in the NZ–UK FTA.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published texts of the NZ–EU FTA and the NZ–UK FTA; true if the EU agreement contains a dedicated Māori trade and economic cooperation chapter and the UK agreement contains a comparable earlier chapter, false if either lacks one.

veracity.statement: The way the EU works is it’s not a collective decision; each member State has to say yes when it comes to a trade agreement, either because of the vote in the European Parliament or sitting around the table in the Council of Ministers, which is Ministers from all the States.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that concluding an EU trade agreement requires the assent of every individual member State rather than a collective EU decision.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: TFEU Articles 207 and 218 and the Council's voting rules for the NZ–EU agreement; true if each member State must individually consent for the agreement to be concluded, false if the Council acts by qualified majority (with European Parliament consent) so that no single member State can withhold assent.

veracity.statement: There have been a total of 169 people who have submitted in the very compressed time frame available of four weeks to hear from the public.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two checkable facts about the select committee process: 169 individual submissions received, and a four-week window for public submissions.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Health Committee's report on the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill and the committee's published submission dates; true if the report records 169 submissions from individuals and a submission period of about four weeks, false if either number is materially different.

veracity.statement: And it’s a concern, because methamphetamine is probably—in fact, almost certainly—the worst drug available in New Zealand and doing more social harm than any other drug.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that methamphetamine causes more social harm in New Zealand than any other drug — operationalisable even though 'worst' on its own would not be.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The New Zealand Drug Harm Index (Ministry of Health / NZ Police) and wastewater testing data for the years around the statement; true if methamphetamine accounts for the largest share of estimated social harm cost of any drug, false if another substance ranks higher.

divination.statement: That is something that we are going to have to phase out after a transition period: we won’t be able to use that term.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that New Zealand producers will lose the right to market cheese under the name 'feta' once the transition period conceded to the EU for that geographical indication expires.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZ law and the NZ–EU FTA GI annex as implemented; true if, after the stated transition period, New Zealand cheese may no longer lawfully be sold domestically under the name 'feta', false if the term remains available to NZ producers.

rigor.statement: So, as tortured as Vangelis Vitalis is, without the recognition of feta as a European GI, we would all be tortured, because I don’t think we would have got a free-trade agreement with the EU.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion (no feta GI, no agreement) does follow from the premises he has just laid out: that each member State must consent, and that feta was Greece's first, second and third priority. The support is a single visit — an anecdote — and the whole inference rests on the member-State-veto premise, which is a gap rather than a fallacy. Whether that premise is true is Veracity's question, not this one.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And yet, since 2011, when pseudoephedrine was banned, the price of pseudoephedrine has gone down; the quantity consumed, unfortunately, has gone up; and according to the availability index, it’s become more available.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference about the measure at hand — trend data since 2011 offered against the effectiveness of the ban — but it is post hoc: three trends over thirteen years are attributed to the ban with nothing offered to exclude other causes, and no counterfactual for what the trends would have done without it.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In contrast, only 1.75 kilograms of higher-efficiency precursor is needed for the same yield—2,430 packets of pseudoephedrine cough medicine to make 1,000 grams of P, and you start to understand why it is that the people who supply these drugs have started bringing it in in more pure forms from overseas rather than going round pharmacies trying to buy up pills that they can cook down into meth.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion tracks the quantities offered: if the alternative precursor gives the same yield at a fraction of the bulk, a supplier's switch to imported high-purity precursor follows. The small gap is that the market behaviour is inferred from the arithmetic rather than shown by seizure or pricing data.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But that member has been doing his own trials for far too long!
civility.explanation: A clear personal attack: in reply to an interjection about cannabis, it implies the member is himself a long-standing drug user. It engages nothing the member said and targets the person rather than the point. No Rigor score — the jibe is not an argument, so there is no inference to assess.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Addiction isn’t rational, and that is the problem that we have, as acknowledged by some of the people with experience working in addictions who submitted to the select committee.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the policy: the rational-actor argument for the bill assumes users behave rationally, so showing addiction is not rational undercuts the premise rather than the conclusion directly. Valid rebuttal, though it leans partly on submitter authority for its support.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: My point would be that the harm of these types of crimes is not just faced by pharmacists or pharmacy owners; it is faced by the community; it is faced by the workers in those stores as well.
rigor.explanation: Directly answers the counter-argument that the risk can be left to pharmacists to accept, by showing the party bearing the risk is not the same as the party consenting to it. The conclusion follows from the premise offered; it is asserted rather than evidenced, which is the only gap.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We all know the Misuse of Drugs Act isn’t working, that banning substances isn’t the right way to deal with addiction, and also there is even worse science supporting some of the other potentially very therapeutic substances that are currently class A on the schedule under the Misuse of Drugs Act that could be transformational and helpful to people who are suffering from different mental health and addictions here in New Zealand.
rigor.explanation: Engages the policy (the Act's schedules) but rests its central premises on 'we all know' — an appeal to common assent standing in for evidence. Nothing is offered to support that the Act is not working or that the classification of the named substances is unscientific.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I think where I’d like to focus my contribution is on how we mitigate those risks, because those risks are real, and to say that we have a theory that pretends that those risks are not real is reckless lawmaking.
civility.explanation: Contested debate with a real opportunity to attack the Minister. 'Reckless lawmaking' is a hard charge against the approach and the reasoning behind the bill, not against any person's character or competence — under the re-anchored scale, brutal criticism of a decision sits near the top.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: In fact, they told us that they heard from fewer than 10 people on this when they did their consultation on advice that later informed the design of this law, and only a handful of them were people with experience of pharmacy and they were some peak body representatives in pharmacies.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Ministry of Health's targeted consultation informing the bill's design reached fewer than 10 people, only a handful of whom had pharmacy experience, and those being peak-body representatives.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health Committee evidence and the Ministry of Health's departmental report / regulatory impact statement for the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill: true if the documented targeted consultation covered fewer than 10 individuals with only a small pharmacy-sector subset; false if the consultation record shows materially more consultees or a broad pharmacy sample.

veracity.statement: So the bill currently does not require pseudoephedrine to be restricted, to be stored under lock and key when it’s in a pharmacy.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the bill as introduced contains no requirement for secure (locked) storage of pseudoephedrine in pharmacies.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill as reported back on 19 March 2024: true if no clause imposes a secure-storage or lock-and-key requirement, false if such a clause exists.

veracity.statement: It also might allow real-time detection of that, and that is the case of similar registers used in Queensland.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Queensland operates a pseudoephedrine sales register capable of real-time detection of suspicious purchasing.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Queensland Health / Pharmacy Guild documentation of the pharmacy pseudoephedrine recording system (Project STOP): true if it records sales and flags suspicious purchases in real time, false if no such register exists or it is retrospective only.

veracity.statement: Despite that, nearly 200 people submitted—well, 169 individuals and nine organisations—and they didn’t have sufficient time to properly consider potentially wider changes to the Misuse of Drugs Act which would have been really helpful.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific submission count on the bill: 169 individual submitters and nine organisations.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Health Committee's report on the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill, which states the number of submissions received: true if it records 169 individuals and nine organisations, false if the counts differ materially.

veracity.statement: We’ve seen that with meth: that meth, with the precursor not being widely available, still became cheaper and more available during that period of time despite being banned.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that after pseudoephedrine was restricted in New Zealand, methamphetamine nonetheless became cheaper and more available.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police / Customs meth price series and the National Wastewater Testing Programme for the period after the 2011 reclassification of pseudoephedrine: true if street price fell and consumption/availability indicators rose, false if price rose or availability indicators fell.

veracity.statement: Ironically, some of the substances that are banned currently—class A substances that are now available in places like Australia for prescription—are some of the most effective treatments for childhood trauma, PTSD, and addiction.
veracity.explanation: Two linked assertions: that substances classified class A in New Zealand are now prescribable in Australia, and that they are among the most effective treatments for childhood trauma, PTSD and addiction.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Australian TGA authorised prescriber scheme decisions effective July 2023 (MDMA for PTSD, psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression) checked against the NZ Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 schedules for those same substances, plus published trial evidence on efficacy: true if the prescribable Australian substances are class A in NZ and the trial evidence supports 'most effective', false if the NZ classification differs (e.g. class B) or the efficacy evidence does not support the superlative.

specificity.statement: In fact, they told us that they heard from fewer than 10 people on this when they did their consultation on advice that later informed the design of this law, and only a handful of them were people with experience of pharmacy and they were some peak body representatives in pharmacies.
specificity.explanation: Carries a checkable count, names the body consulted and characterises who the consultees were; someone could go to the committee record and verify it. Short of full precision only because 'fewer than 10' and 'a handful' are bounds rather than figures.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Despite that, nearly 200 people submitted—well, 169 individuals and nine organisations—and they didn’t have sufficient time to properly consider potentially wider changes to the Misuse of Drugs Act which would have been really helpful.
specificity.explanation: Gives exact counts broken down by submitter type against a named committee process — precise enough for anyone to check against the committee report.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So we’d love to see a priority of reviewing the Misuse of Drugs Act, treating addiction as a harm minimisation and a health issue rather than as a criminal issue, and making available therapeutic substances that have for too long and with insufficient evidence been denied to New Zealanders.
specificity.explanation: Names one piece of legislation and a direction of travel, but no mechanism, no substances named, no timeframe and no scope for the review — a stated preference rather than something anyone could act on or check.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The sooner the ACT Party and Government do something to properly review the Misuse of Drugs Act, the better, from my point of view.
focus.explanation: Names a specific measure — a review of the Misuse of Drugs Act — so there is real policy content, but the demand is addressed to a party rather than to the substance, which pulls it below a fully policy-directed statement.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We’re now talking about an environment, where, just in January, we had a seizure of 4.8 tonnes that was heading to Australia and New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a single methamphetamine seizure in January 2024 amounted to 4.8 tonnes of product destined for Australia and New Zealand.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Customs / NZ Police and Australian Federal Police media releases and reporting on methamphetamine seizures in January 2024; true if a seizure of approximately 4.8 tonnes bound for Australia and New Zealand is on record for that month, false if the largest January 2024 seizure was materially smaller or was not destined for those countries.

veracity.statement: They get manipulated, and the market quickly pivoted to create a level of supply that enabled methamphetamine to become the most prevalent drug in New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that methamphetamine is the most prevalent drug in New Zealand.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police national wastewater drug testing programme and the NZ Health Survey / NZ Drug Trends Survey; true if methamphetamine is the most consumed drug on the relevant published measure, false if another drug (e.g. cannabis) ranks above it on both prevalence-of-use and consumption measures.

specificity.statement: We’re now talking about an environment, where, just in January, we had a seizure of 4.8 tonnes that was heading to Australia and New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Gives a quantity (4.8 tonnes), a timeframe (January) and a destination — checkable against seizure records. No score for truth here; that is veracity's question.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I think that we are smarter and more intelligent, and we need to be able to pivot quickly and effectively to ensure that we are responding to what New Zealanders need, and heading into winter in this environment—I think it is really important that we work together to change things that are no longer relevant to what is occurring in New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic virtues — being smarter, pivoting quickly, working together, changing what is no longer relevant. No figure, mechanism, timeframe or named step, and nothing here that someone could check or act on, even though the surrounding speech does carry detail elsewhere.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But I would suggest that purchasing, stealing, obtaining pseudoephedrine in order to set up a lab to cook, when just about everyone will know where meth can be supplied in their communities, and obtaining cash is far simpler than obtaining pseudoephedrine.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the measure: if finished methamphetamine is cheaply and widely available, the diversion pathway that justified reclassifying pseudoephedrine is no longer the attractive route, so relaxing it carries little added risk. The conclusion tracks the premises, and the seizure tonnage offered earlier supports the supply premise; the gap is that the relative ease of obtaining cash versus pseudoephedrine is asserted rather than evidenced.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But I would suggest that purchasing, stealing, obtaining pseudoephedrine in order to set up a lab to cook, when just about everyone will know where meth can be supplied in their communities, and obtaining cash is far simpler than obtaining pseudoephedrine.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the mechanism of the bill before the House — the diversion pathway pseudoephedrine reclassification was meant to close. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: But that is not going to change with pseudoephedrine being available as a suitable, practical, medical solution for colds and flus.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that restoring over-the-counter pseudoephedrine will not change methamphetamine's impact on New Zealand — i.e. that domestic pseudoephedrine-based manufacture will not revive as a result of the reclassification.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZ Police clandestine laboratory detection statistics and pseudoephedrine-diversion reporting for the two years following the bill's commencement; true if pseudoephedrine-based clandestine lab detections stay at or near the pre-2024 baseline, false if they rise materially above it.

rigor.statement: The result of that wasn’t what was wanted or anticipated, which would have been a reduction in methamphetamine availability, but the criminal organisations and the gangs found alternative routes to either manufacture or—more likely—import pseudoephedrine from international criminal syndicates into New Zealand.
rigor.explanation: A real causal inference about the 2011 reclassification: the intended reduction did not occur because supply substituted to imported precursor. The mechanism is named and the conclusion tracks it, but the substitution route is asserted rather than evidenced within the statement, leaving a gap between what is shown and what is concluded.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But the reality is that there’s already those networks available for people to obtain methamphetamine through existing drug channels out there, and this isn’t likely to lead to a dramatic increase in supply, as noted, but only for small-scale personal use.
rigor.explanation: A genuine argument about the measure: existing supply channels mean pharmacy pseudoephedrine adds little at the margin, so the risk is confined to small-scale manufacture. The inference is coherent, but 'as noted' leans on the Minister's earlier assertion rather than on anything established here — a mild appeal to authority carrying part of the conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Recent stats have shown that we have seen an increase in use recently, and we have also seen a reasonably considerable drop in the price of methamphetamine.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two facts about the present: that measured methamphetamine use has risen recently and that its price has dropped considerably.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police/ESR national wastewater drug testing programme estimates of methamphetamine consumption, and NZ Police / NZ Drug Foundation retail price data, for the periods up to March 2024. True if consumption estimates rose and the reported street price fell over the recent period; false if consumption was flat or falling, or the price was stable or rising.

veracity.statement: I think the Minister noted quite well, as well, that it would take 2,430 packets of pseudoephedrine to make 1,000 grams of P, and there are much more effective ways that that can be done now, with more intensive forms and much smaller quantities required to produce the ultimate outcome which they’re intending, which is to produce or cook P.
veracity.explanation: Relays the Associate Minister's quantitative claim about how many retail packets of pseudoephedrine are needed to produce a kilogram of methamphetamine. The speaker is reporting the Minister's figure, not asserting it from his own evidence.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: The pseudoephedrine content of a standard retail pack sold in New Zealand multiplied by typical conversion yields, as set out in the Ministry of Health / Police advice and the departmental report on the bill. True if roughly 2,430 packs are required to yield 1,000 g of methamphetamine; false if the true figure differs by an order of magnitude.

veracity.statement: I will also note that when we look at other comparable countries, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia all allow for what this bill is intending to achieve, which is the purchase of pseudoephedrine for cold and flu relief.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that all four named comparator countries permitted non-prescription purchase of pseudoephedrine at the time of speaking.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The medicines scheduling rules in force in March 2024 in each of the four named countries — US Combat Methamphetamine Epidemic Act behind-the-counter sales, UK pharmacy (P) medicine status, Health Canada scheduling, and the Australian Poisons Standard Schedule 3. True if all four permitted retail purchase of pseudoephedrine for cold and flu relief without a prescription; false if any one of them required a prescription.

specificity.statement: Recent stats have shown that we have seen an increase in use recently, and we have also seen a reasonably considerable drop in the price of methamphetamine.
specificity.explanation: A policy-relevant empirical claim carried entirely on 'recent stats' and 'reasonably considerable' — no figure, no source named, no period given, where all three were available to him. The direction is clear but nothing here is precise enough to act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I think the Minister noted quite well, as well, that it would take 2,430 packets of pseudoephedrine to make 1,000 grams of P, and there are much more effective ways that that can be done now, with more intensive forms and much smaller quantities required to produce the ultimate outcome which they’re intending, which is to produce or cook P.
specificity.explanation: Gives an exact conversion figure (2,430 packets to 1,000 grams) tied to a named risk. Someone could check the arithmetic against pack strengths and yields; the trailing clause about 'more intensive forms' is vaguer, but the core of the statement is precise and checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The committee did also ask that there be a look forward to see whether we could have a system like they have in Australia—where they have a real-time, online registry of everyone who has purchased pseudoephedrine—so that we can be aware of where someone is going around a bunch of pharmacies, purchasing in bulk, and that that can be picked up and mitigated.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete mechanism (a real-time online purchase registry), its source jurisdiction and the behaviour it would detect. Falls short of the top because it is only a request to 'look forward' at it — no timeframe, no cost, no commitment to implement.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We had 169 individual submissions and we had nine from organisations.
specificity.explanation: Exact counts, broken down by submitter type, where a vague 'we heard from a lot of submitters' was the easy alternative. Directly checkable against the select committee record.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: What was done back then hasn’t really fitted with what we wanted to see, so bringing this back in, as the Minister is doing at the moment—we don’t believe it’s going to lead to an explosion in methamphetamine consumption.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that reclassifying pseudoephedrine to C3 will not produce a large increase in methamphetamine consumption — an outcome in the world, not a commitment to act.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZ Police/ESR wastewater methamphetamine consumption estimates and NZ Police clandestine-laboratory and precursor-diversion detections for the two years after pseudoephedrine returns to pharmacy sale. True if there is no marked rise in domestic manufacture from pharmacy-sourced pseudoephedrine and consumption does not step-change following the reclassification; false if lab detections or pharmacy precursor diversion rise sharply after the change.

divination.statement: The good news for them is that in the not too distant future, there will be pseudoephedrine available from pharmacies, so they can take that and then recover their health and wellbeing and get back to work and continue living their lives in a lot more peaceful and enjoyable manner.
divination.explanation: Forecasts a market outcome — that pseudoephedrine will actually be obtainable from pharmacies soon — rather than promising an action by the speaker.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Whether pseudoephedrine-containing cold and flu products are actually on sale at New Zealand pharmacies (Medsafe product approvals plus pharmacy availability reporting). True if such products are purchasable from pharmacies within roughly a year of the bill's passage; false if supply does not materialise in that period. Note the speaker himself said importation had previously dried up for want of a market, so passage of the bill does not guarantee stock.

focus.statement: The committee did also ask that there be a look forward to see whether we could have a system like they have in Australia—where they have a real-time, online registry of everyone who has purchased pseudoephedrine—so that we can be aware of where someone is going around a bunch of pharmacies, purchasing in bulk, and that that can be picked up and mitigated.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the House: a named mitigation mechanism, the overseas comparator it comes from, and the specific abuse it is meant to catch. No party framing of any kind.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But more sinister, perhaps, is that I think the National Government has shown quite a casual and cavalier attitude to the methamphetamine issue generally through the way they have approached this process—and I’ll speak to that soon.
focus.explanation: A real policy point (the handling of this reclassification process) but the weight of the sentence is a characterisation of the governing party's general attitude rather than a named measure or outcome.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We are not seeing leadership on the meth issue, we are not seeing leadership on drugs, we are not seeing the changes that we need to make sure that the gangs are disempowered.
focus.explanation: Directed at the governing party's general performance. No policy, measure, figure or named outcome is identified, so it fails the deciding test that separates accountability from party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Associate Minister of Health (Pharmac) did appear before the Health Committee and we asked him questions on this quite closely, and he, basically, admitted that it was a political decision to reclassify.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Associate Minister of Health (Pharmac), under questioning at the Health Committee, conceded the reclassification was a political rather than an expert/Medsafe decision.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Health Committee's evidence and report on the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill: true if the Associate Minister of Health (Pharmac) accepted in questioning that the decision to reclassify was a political/ministerial one; false if the transcript shows no such concession.

veracity.statement: When we asked them closely about the numbers of pharmacists they had consulted, we were told it was fewer than 10.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that officials told the Health Committee the pharmacist consultation covered fewer than ten pharmacists.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health Committee evidence and the Ministry of Health's consultation record for the bill: true if officials stated the pharmacist focus group numbered fewer than 10; false if the record shows a larger stated consultation.

veracity.statement: We heard from the Drug Foundation that close to 50 percent of those who are incarcerated on meth-related charges have an ADHD diagnosis.
veracity.explanation: Relays a statistic attributed to the New Zealand Drug Foundation: roughly half of people incarcerated on meth-related charges carry an ADHD diagnosis.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: The New Zealand Drug Foundation's submission to the Health Committee and the study it cites: true if a source puts ADHD diagnosis prevalence among those imprisoned on meth-related charges near 50%; false if the cited figure is materially lower or no such source exists.

veracity.statement: There are 1,200 Customs staff throughout New Zealand, and the New Zealand Public Service Association has said that this redundancy process, these cuts to that public service are hamstringing Customs’ ability to keep harmful drugs out of New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Two assertions: that the New Zealand Customs Service employs about 1,200 staff, and that the PSA has publicly said the 2024 redundancy round undermines Customs' drug interdiction capability.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Customs Service annual report staffing (FTE) figures for 2023/24, and PSA public statements/media releases of early 2024 on Customs cuts: true if Customs staffing is about 1,200 and the PSA made a statement to that effect; false if staffing is materially different or no such PSA statement exists.

veracity.statement: So, during the select committee process, we received submissions from 169 individuals and nine organisations.
veracity.explanation: Asserts precise submission counts for the bill's select committee stage: 169 individual submitters and nine organisations.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Health Committee's report on the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill, which states the number of submissions received: true if it records 169 individuals and nine organisations; false if the counts differ.

veracity.statement: But let me remind everyone here, pseudoephedrine will remain a controlled drug and can only be prescribed by an authorised pharmacist prescriber who has undergone the required training and education.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that after the change pseudoephedrine remains a controlled drug and may only be supplied via an authorised pharmacist prescriber with specified training — a restriction on who can hand it over.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the Misuse of Drugs (Pseudoephedrine) Amendment Bill as reported back, and the resulting class C3 supply rules: true if supply requires an authorised pharmacist prescriber holding the stated training; false if any registered pharmacist may sell it over the counter without a prescription or prescriber authorisation.

rigor.statement: To me, that is just inadequate, and it shows the kind of time pressures that they were under from their Minister.
rigor.explanation: The premise (fewer than ten pharmacists consulted) is offered as evidence for a conclusion about ministerial pressure on officials. Nothing connects the two — a non sequitur about cause; thin consultation has many possible explanations.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, I’m not sure how the Minister can keep an eye on whether organised crime is shopping around for pseudoephedrine if the registers are not there—it simply cannot be done.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference about the policy: if the register is the monitoring instrument and there is no register, the monitoring undertaking is empty. The gap is the absolute 'it simply cannot be done', which assumes registers are the only possible source of intelligence — a point the speaker herself concedes in the next sentence.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So, actually, during the select committee process, we have been informed that there is little value to people interested in commercially supplying meth, and there are now cheaper and easier ways to manufacture it. This means that making pseudoephedrine products more available will have little effect on the New Zealand drug market.
rigor.explanation: The inference tracks its premises for the commercial supply case: if manufacturers have cheaper routes, extra pharmacy pseudoephedrine adds little. The gap is that the premise is confined to commercial suppliers while the conclusion is drawn about the whole drug market, leaving small-scale manufacture unaddressed.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We are pleased to learn that the Ministry of Health is working with Health New Zealand to explore options for improving the uptake and standardisation of a nationwide electronic dispensing system. This allows us to monitor the sales of pseudoephedrine products in real time, and that can minimise the improper use of the drugs.
rigor.explanation: The premise is that agencies are exploring options for a system; the conclusion asserts a present capability ('this allows us to monitor ... in real time'). The conclusion assumes the completed result of a process that has not begun — a non sequitur, with a further unsupported step from monitoring to reduced misuse.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: There’s also been a lot of talk about common sense, that there’s a common-sense approach, and whilst that might sound good, common sense has never been a huge leader in terms of things always turning out well, hence the fact that it is our job to not assume that people are rational actors, to not assume that when we’re talking about addiction and when we’re talking about comorbidities, with people with ADHD being the largest consumers of meth, for instance, there’s this linear assumption that a rational decision-making process will take place.
rigor.explanation: There is a real argument here about the policy — that a rational-actor assumption is unsafe where addiction and comorbidity are involved — but the load-bearing premise is a bare generalisation ('common sense has never been a huge leader'), offered without support, and the ADHD claim is asserted in passing rather than used to establish the step.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: There are 1,200 Customs staff throughout New Zealand, and the New Zealand Public Service Association has said that this redundancy process, these cuts to that public service are hamstringing Customs’ ability to keep harmful drugs out of New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Carries a headcount figure and names the agency and the union making the claim — checkable content, though no dollar figures or dates for the redundancies.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We are not seeing leadership on the meth issue, we are not seeing leadership on drugs, we are not seeing the changes that we need to make sure that the gangs are disempowered.
specificity.explanation: A tricolon of 'we are not seeing leadership' with no mechanism, figure, timeframe or named programme; nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This bill reclassifies pseudoephedrine from a class B2 to a class C3 drug, controlled drugs, under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1975 so that the cold and flu products containing pseudoephedrine can be sold in pharmacies without a prescription.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact classification change, the governing statute, and the concrete consequence for how the product is sold. Fully checkable against the bill.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I think the issue around tracking it and the issue around having that online, real-time register, as they do in Queensland, is a real missed opportunity for this Parliament not to have sought more information about that.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete mechanism (an online real-time sales register) and a working comparator jurisdiction, but supplies no cost, timeframe or design detail for adopting it here.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We expect to receive an update on how they’re progressing with the implementation of a monitoring system by the end of this year.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the Ministry of Health and Te Whatu Ora will report back to the Health Committee on progress implementing a pseudoephedrine sales monitoring system before the end of 2024.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Health Committee records and published correspondence: true if an update from the Ministry of Health or Te Whatu Ora on the pseudoephedrine monitoring/electronic dispensing system was provided to the committee on or before 31 December 2024; false if no such update was received in that period.

divination.statement: So, actually, during the select committee process, we have been informed that there is little value to people interested in commercially supplying meth, and there are now cheaper and easier ways to manufacture it. This means that making pseudoephedrine products more available will have little effect on the New Zealand drug market.
divination.explanation: The second sentence forecasts that increased pharmacy availability of pseudoephedrine will not materially change the New Zealand methamphetamine market.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Police national wastewater methamphetamine consumption data and Police/Customs/National Drug Intelligence Bureau assessments in the 12–24 months after reclassification took effect: true if no documented rise in domestic pseudoephedrine-based meth manufacture or in market supply is attributed to the change; false if enforcement agencies report a material increase in pharmacy-sourced pseudoephedrine diversion into meth production.

focus.statement: This is a Government that prides itself in removing bureaucracy, but what we’re going to have now is pharmacists who are going to have to do face-to-face transactions, process records of information, and highlight advice, including counselling and any trends with patients that shouldn’t be taking things.
focus.explanation: Engages the bill's actual mechanism — the specific obligations placed on pharmacists — rather than the other party's character. On-policy scrutiny of a named consequence.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Because of that, it’s incredibly clear to me how the criminalisation of substances hasn’t worked to actually support people, neither to stop getting them addicted nor as part of the recovery journey.
focus.explanation: Squarely about the drug-policy question before the House, not about the other side. The weak inference belongs to Rigor and is not deducted here.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: This is a Government that prides itself in removing bureaucracy, but what we’re going to have now is pharmacists who are going to have to do face-to-face transactions, process records of information, and highlight advice, including counselling and any trends with patients that shouldn’t be taking things.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real policy: the stated deregulatory aim is set against enumerated new obligations. The gap is that no comparison is made with the current burden of obtaining pseudoephedrine, so 'piling back more' is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Because of that, it’s incredibly clear to me how the criminalisation of substances hasn’t worked to actually support people, neither to stop getting them addicted nor as part of the recovery journey.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion — that criminalisation as a policy does not work — rests on the speaker's family experience and upbringing alone. Argument from anecdote: personal exposure to harm does not establish the counterfactual about the policy.
