veracity.statement: Dam safety regulations imposed by the previous Government are set to come into force on 13 May, but farmers and growers have warned us about the downstream effects, which include an unreasonable amount of compliance cost for the relatively low risk posed by small dams that are used in farms across New Zealand for water storage.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the dam safety regulations made under the previous government were scheduled to commence on 13 May (2024).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The commencement date in the Building (Dam Safety) Regulations 2022 as at March 2024; true if they were due to come into force on 13 May 2024, false if the scheduled date was materially different.

veracity.statement: These changes will mean around 1,900 fewer dams will be impacted by the new regulations, reducing compliance costs by more than $13.3 million.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two quantified impacts of the threshold change: about 1,900 fewer dams captured, and savings of more than $13.3 million in compliance costs.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE's regulatory impact/cost-benefit analysis and the March 2024 ministerial announcement for the dam safety threshold change; true if the officials' estimates are approximately 1,900 dams and $13.3m, false if the documented estimates differ materially.

veracity.statement: When meeting with mining lobbyists Straterra on 23 January, on the resources and associate energy portfolio, did he, in his capacity as fisheries Minister, communicate the longstanding opposition of the fishing industry to seabed mining?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as premise that the Minister met with Straterra on 23 January in his resources/associate energy capacity.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Shane Jones' published ministerial diary releases for January 2024; true if a meeting with Straterra is recorded on 23 January 2024, false if no such meeting appears.

veracity.statement: There are some apocryphal, unbounded, dangerous assertions in that question. The processes that are in play pertaining to applicants seeking to gain access to the half a trillion dollars’ worth of wealth on the bed of the sea are entitled to go through that process. That is shared space enjoyed also by quota owners.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the wealth on New Zealand's seabed accessible to applicants amounts to half a trillion dollars.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published NZ government (MBIE/GNS Science) or industry valuations of seabed mineral resources in New Zealand's EEZ; true if a credible published estimate is around NZ$500 billion, false if the best available estimates are an order of magnitude lower or no such estimate exists.

veracity.statement: Does she regret that the Minister for the Environment is not listed as a decision-making Minister in the Fast-track Approvals Bill when those decision-making Ministers can override Resource Management Act prohibited activities?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Fast-track Approvals Bill as introduced does not include the Minister for the Environment among the joint decision-making Ministers, and that those Ministers can approve activities prohibited under the RMA.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the Fast-track Approvals Bill as introduced in March 2024; true if the named joint Ministers are Infrastructure, Transport and Regional Development and exclude the Environment Minister, and the Bill permits approval of RMA-prohibited activities; false if the Environment Minister is listed.

veracity.statement: Does she regret contacting the Otago Regional Council to slow down its water plan to improve water quality?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as premise that the Minister contacted the Otago Regional Council in order to delay its freshwater/water quality plan.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministerial correspondence with the Otago Regional Council released under the OIA and the ORC's public record of its land and water plan notification date; true if the Minister's contact resulted in delaying notification of the plan, false if no such contact or delay is documented.

veracity.statement: The Kermadec Islands have already got a considerable amount of protection and I’ll list it for the member: there is a marine reserve around each Kermadec island out to 12 nautical miles, there are regulations prohibiting bottom trawling, there is a minerals reservation—prevents new mining permits, and there are a range of marine wildlife regulations.
veracity.explanation: Asserts four existing protections for the Kermadecs: a marine reserve out to 12 nautical miles, bottom-trawling prohibitions, a minerals reservation barring new mining permits, and marine wildlife regulations.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: DOC and Fisheries NZ records of the Kermadec Islands Marine Reserve boundary, the Benthic Protection Areas/bottom trawling regulations, and the Crown Minerals Act reservation over the Kermadec region; true if all four exist substantially as described, false if any is misstated.

veracity.statement: What is his response to the rate of suspected suicide which, according to Te Whatu Ora’s data for 2022, is 51.9 per 100,000 for Māori males aged 25-44 years compared to 16.4 per 100,000 for non-Māori males?
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific suspected-suicide rates from Te Whatu Ora 2022 data: 51.9 per 100,000 for Māori males aged 25–44 versus 16.4 per 100,000 for non-Māori males.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Te Whatu Ora / Coronial Services suspected suicide statistics for 2022 broken down by ethnicity and age band; true if the rates match the quoted figures within rounding, false if materially different or if the comparison group is misdescribed.

veracity.statement: What is his view on the impacts of statements by Government Ministers that marginalise rangatahi from their whakapapa, such as comparing Māori and Pasifika spaces to apartheid and segregation, on the mental health of rangatahi?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as premise that Government Ministers have compared Māori and Pasifika spaces to apartheid and segregation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public statements by coalition Ministers before 28 March 2024 (media reports, Hansard, speeches); true if a Minister is on record likening Māori/Pasifika spaces or provisions to apartheid or segregation, false if no such statement can be sourced to a Minister.

specificity.statement: This week, the coalition Government has agreed to raise the height threshold of the dams caught by regulations from 1 metre to 4 metres.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact regulatory parameter being changed and both the old and new numeric thresholds; directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: These changes will mean around 1,900 fewer dams will be impacted by the new regulations, reducing compliance costs by more than $13.3 million.
specificity.explanation: Gives a specific count of affected dams and a dollar figure for the saving.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why, yes; this Government is focused on reducing costs and removing unnecessary red tape so that we can get the economy back on track. You can expect to hear a lot more on how the coalition Government is going to remove unnecessary regulations that are merely adding costs and getting in the way of Kiwis trying to build.
specificity.explanation: Asked what further announcements are planned, the answer names no regulation, no measure, no timeframe and no figure — general 'red tape' framing only.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: When meeting with mining lobbyists Straterra on 23 January, on the resources and associate energy portfolio, did he, in his capacity as fisheries Minister, communicate the longstanding opposition of the fishing industry to seabed mining?
specificity.explanation: Names the organisation met, the date, the portfolio and the precise subject the answer must address.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does she regret that the Minister for the Environment is not listed as a decision-making Minister in the Fast-track Approvals Bill when those decision-making Ministers can override Resource Management Act prohibited activities?
specificity.explanation: Names the bill, the specific structural feature (which Ministers are decision-makers) and the consequence (override of RMA prohibited activities).
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I contacted the Otago Regional Council to release them from the obligation that had been placed on them by the previous Minister for the Environment, to ensure that I extended the date for their statutory deadline for notifying their freshwater planning instrument so that it was in line with all other councils.
specificity.explanation: Names the action taken, the instrument affected (freshwater planning instrument notification deadline) and the rationale (alignment with other councils), though no dates are given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The Kermadec Islands have already got a considerable amount of protection and I’ll list it for the member: there is a marine reserve around each Kermadec island out to 12 nautical miles, there are regulations prohibiting bottom trawling, there is a minerals reservation—prevents new mining permits, and there are a range of marine wildlife regulations.
specificity.explanation: Enumerates four named protection mechanisms with a stated spatial extent rather than asserting protection in general terms.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re working with our coalition partners to fund front-line services such as Gumboot Friday and the I Am Hope charity. This Government is also working to establish the mental health innovation fund to increase access to mental health services in this term of Government.
specificity.explanation: Names two funded services and a named fund with a term-of-Parliament timeframe, but gives no amounts, no delivery dates and no mechanism.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: As I have stated before, the coalition Government is committed to reducing suicide rates in New Zealand and better health outcomes for all New Zealanders. This is why we are focused on committing delivering of services close to home and as close to hapū as possible.
specificity.explanation: Asked what Māori-specific suicide prevention initiatives are funded, the answer offers a statement of commitment and a general locality principle with no named initiative, funding or measure.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What is his response to the rate of suspected suicide which, according to Te Whatu Ora’s data for 2022, is 51.9 per 100,000 for Māori males aged 25-44 years compared to 16.4 per 100,000 for non-Māori males?
specificity.explanation: Cites a named data source, a year, an age band and two precise rates per 100,000.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What procurement process, therefore, was used for the I Am Hope trust to receive $6 million of public money?
specificity.explanation: Names the recipient organisation, the sum, and the precise administrative question (which procurement process was followed).
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: By extraordinary coincidence, it was from the member’s very own electorate of the mighty Rangitata that we have heard farmers saying that they were attempting to comply with the regulations at the cost of some $5,000 each, not to mention the additional ongoing compliance burden and administrative costs.
rigor.explanation: The case for the regulatory change here rests on unquantified anecdote from a handful of farmers in one electorate — an appeal to anecdote generalised to a national compliance burden.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I’ve gone from the champion of the provinces to the leader, the leading politician, who is going to ensure that the fishing industry is not demonised or driven out of existence by stupid Green policies.
focus.explanation: Asked a specific question about seabed mining and the fishing industry's position on it, the answer names no policy, mechanism or outcome — it is entirely a characterisation of the opposing party's policies.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Obviously, within our domestic jurisdiction, there are opportunities to excavate, extract, and take rare earth seabed minerals necessary for the climate change journey. There is also the New Zealand involvement in a working group, under the UN, dealing with high-seas international waters mining. The latter does not drive the former.
focus.explanation: Engages the substance directly: distinguishes the domestic seabed minerals regime from New Zealand's participation in the UN high-seas process and states how they relate.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: What evidence-based initiatives that specifically address suicide rates is the Minister considering in the next five-year Suicide Prevention Action Plan, and how will these address the disparities of suicide rates between Māori and non-Māori?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the policy instrument before the Minister — the next five-year Suicide Prevention Action Plan — and on the specific outcome it is meant to address.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I’ve gone from the champion of the provinces to the leader, the leading politician, who is going to ensure that the fishing industry is not demonised or driven out of existence by stupid Green policies.
civility.explanation: 'Stupid Green policies' is a sneer rather than an argument, though it is aimed at a party's policies rather than at any individual member.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does she regret accepting the environment portfolio when she is powerless to protect the environment?
civility.explanation: Moves from the policy to the Minister personally, framing her as powerless and implying she should not hold the job — an attack on the person's standing rather than on a decision.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Fortunately, Māori are New Zealanders, which is a good thing.
civility.explanation: A sarcastic barb at the Minister's 'all New Zealanders' phrasing — mockery rather than engagement with the substance, though it stops well short of a personal insult.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We have the entire vehicle industry saying to us at select committee—and over 500 New Zealanders who had less than 36 hours to submit on this bill—that they opposed the bill.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the vehicle industry as a whole opposed the bill at select committee, that over 500 members of the public submitted, and that the submission window was under 36 hours.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The select committee report and submission record for the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill 2024: true if the published submission count exceeds 500, the advertised submission window was under 36 hours, and the industry bodies' submissions opposed the bill; false if the submission window was longer, submissions materially fewer, or industry submissions supported the bill.

veracity.statement: Of course, the report says they didn’t support it, but that’s OK.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the select committee report records government members as not supporting the amendment lowering the rate for plug-in hybrids, contrary to Grant McCallum's interjection.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The select committee report on the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill 2024: true if it records the amendment on plug-in hybrid rates as not supported by the government members of the committee; false if the report records their support or is silent in a way that contradicts her claim.

veracity.statement: There was an intention, a good intention in 2016, to incentivise people to get into the electric vehicle and plug-in electric vehicle market.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a 2016 policy decision established the EV road-user-charge exemption as a deliberate incentive to grow the EV market.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2016 Electric Vehicles Programme announcement and the associated amendment to the Road User Charges Act extending the light EV RUC exemption: true if a 2016 government decision extended the exemption for the stated purpose of encouraging EV uptake; false if the exemption's origin and stated purpose date from a different year or a different rationale.

divination.statement: They will import and purchase more brand-new fossil-fuel vehicles instead of electric vehicles, and that will emit more emissions on our roads for at least 20 years.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the RUC rates set by this bill will shift new-vehicle purchasing toward fossil-fuel vehicles and away from EVs over the following years.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA motor vehicle registration statistics for new light vehicles: true if the EV share of new light-vehicle registrations falls (and internal-combustion registrations rise correspondingly) over the five years from April 2024; false if EV share of new registrations continues to grow across that period.

divination.statement: Well, I will take a bet with any member of this House that we will not see that system brought in before the end of this term, and over the next three to five years, that is the critical moment which would have made a consequential difference to the vehicles coming in.
divination.explanation: Predicts that the Minister's promised full road-pricing / universal road-user-charge system will not be operating before the end of the current parliamentary term.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Legislation and NZTA implementation records: false if a full road pricing / all-vehicle road user charge system is in force and operating before Parliament is dissolved for the 2026 general election; true if it is not (still at bill, consultation or announced-intent stage).

specificity.statement: A simple change which would have said that electric vehicles pay a rate of $60 per 1,000 kilometres instead of the rate that is proposed here, which is significantly more and will mean that EV drivers are paying more than fossil fuel drivers in comparable cars for the exact same journey.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact alternative rate ($60 per 1,000 km), the mechanism (the RUC rate in the bill) and the comparison being made; someone could check or act on it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, I can give those people assurance that we will not be charging a road-user charge while they are still paying a fuel excise duty, because that’s just not fair.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete rule — no RUC on vehicles still paying fuel excise duty — but supplies no rates, thresholds or dates for the transition.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So the practical consequence of this bill is more emissions, more pollution contributing to greenhouse gases.
focus.explanation: Squarely about the measure before the House and its claimed effect, with no party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, the point is, it’s not fair and it’s just very clear from every action this Government takes that they don’t believe in climate change, they don’t believe in taking action on climate change.
focus.explanation: Leaves the bill behind for a general characterisation of what the other side 'really' believes; no policy, figure or outcome is named in the claim.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It is merely there to pay for the renewal and maintenance and improvements of our roads. We have an emissions trading scheme (ETS) which deals with a user-pays mechanism to deal with carbon emissions and pricing carbon to make sure that people who are actually emitting carbon pay for that, not people who we do or don’t want to be seeing on the roads.
focus.explanation: Engages the mechanism of the bill and the policy instrument that handles emissions, rather than the opposing party.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: He wants to ensure that children cannot even walk to school safely by stopping the survivable speed limits around schools.
rigor.explanation: Infers a deliberate intention (that children be unable to walk safely) from a policy decision to reverse speed limit rules — a non sequitur that treats a consequence she asserts as the aim, with nothing offered to bridge policy to motive.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And, if I went out there and asked any New Zealander if they think the Government should be making decisions that increase emissions and increase fossil fuel vehicles on our roads, they would say no, because most New Zealanders know about climate change.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to popularity built on a hypothetical, leading question; that people would answer 'no' to a loaded framing is offered as support for the policy conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It is merely there to pay for the renewal and maintenance and improvements of our roads. We have an emissions trading scheme (ETS) which deals with a user-pays mechanism to deal with carbon emissions and pricing carbon to make sure that people who are actually emitting carbon pay for that, not people who we do or don’t want to be seeing on the roads.
rigor.explanation: A genuine division-of-instruments argument — road charges fund roads, the ETS prices carbon — but the conclusion that the RUC rate therefore needs no emissions consideration leaves a gap, since it does not address the claim that this particular rate distorts choices between vehicle types.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: We know what this Minister cares about. He’s fighting those silly, tribal culture wars, as if it mattered.
civility.explanation: Turns from the policy to the Minister personally, imputing petty motives and mocking him rather than engaging the substance.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Now, while we’ve heard that they had 36 or so hours—I think it might’ve been between 36 and 48 hours to make submissions—we got 518 submissions, and I think they were really good quality and we got some really good input from submitters.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the select committee received 518 submissions on the bill within a submission window of roughly 36-48 hours.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Transport and Infrastructure Committee's report on the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill and the Parliament submissions page: true if the recorded number of submissions is 518 (± rounding) and the submission window was under two days, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: EVs and PHEVs have been exempted from this until we got to roughly 2 percent of the vehicle fleet, and we’ve got to that point and, therefore, Labour had started that work.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the EV/PHEV road user charge exemption was set to run until electric vehicles reached about 2 percent of the vehicle fleet, and that this threshold has now been reached.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Land Transport Management (Road User Charges Exemption) legislation and Ministry of Transport policy documents on the EV RUC exemption, plus NZTA fleet statistics: true if the exemption's stated end condition was ~2% of the light vehicle fleet and the fleet share reached that level, false if the threshold was a different figure or was never reached.

veracity.statement: We started off at 20 percent, which is where the initial consultation happened that the then Labour Government started two years ago.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a consultation begun by the previous Labour Government around 2022 proposed a 20 percent RUC discount for plug-in hybrids.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport consultation documents on bringing EVs and PHEVs into the RUC system published under the Labour Government in 2022: true if a 20 percent PHEV discount was the consulted figure, false if a different rate or no such consultation is found.

veracity.statement: I also note that during the committee stage of the House yesterday, when it came to the final vote, it was unanimous—it was unanimous.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the vote at the conclusion of the committee stage of this bill, on 27 March 2024, was unanimous.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard record and division list for the committee stage of the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill on 27 March 2024: true if the vote was recorded as unanimous or agreed without opposition, false if any party is recorded voting against.

rigor.statement: Now, perhaps the incoming coalition might’ve advanced it earlier, but look how many things we’ve had to do in the first hundred-odd days of this Government. So I don’t think that anybody should point the finger.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion — that nobody should criticise the truncated select committee timeframe — is supported only by the Government's general workload and by the previous government's inaction. Neither premise bears on whether nine days was adequate for this bill; it is a tu quoque combined with an appeal to busyness.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But the reality is, going through that process, there were opportunities to tackle this; they were not taken, and I think people should reflect on that.
rigor.explanation: Infers that opposition to the bill is not warranted because no party moved an amendment on the EV rate at select committee. The premise does not support the conclusion — declining to amend a rate does not commit a party to supporting the bill as a whole.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I think that illustrates the importance of incentives to decarbonise, because my sons are, like many youth, really concerned about their future.
rigor.explanation: Argument from a single family anecdote: his sons' purchase of a $5,000 second-hand Leaf, plus their stated concern about the future, is offered as establishing the importance of decarbonisation incentives. The anecdote does not support the general conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We had some advice that they also provided to us that came from Europe, which said they’d looked at 9,000 PHEVs in Europe, which suggested that maybe a 50 percent discount was the right number.
specificity.explanation: Names the source of the advice, the sample size (9,000 PHEVs), the jurisdiction and the resulting discount figure — all checkable against the committee's papers.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Now, if you used 11,000 kilometres, the MOT’s advice was that the average saving across a year will be $165.
specificity.explanation: Gives a precise assumption (11,000 km/year), a named source and a dollar figure for the average annual saving.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: It needs money to be able to build, to maintain, to operate roads and public transport systems and so on, and so we are going to need a new way of funding our roading system. That will be RUC, and that is where we need to move as quickly as possible.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that road user charges will become the funding mechanism for the transport system across the whole vehicle fleet, not just EVs and PHEVs.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: New Zealand legislation and Government policy announcements on extending road user charges to petrol light vehicles: true if RUC is legislated to apply across the light vehicle fleet (replacing fuel excise duty) by the resolve-by date, false if fuel excise duty remains the primary charge for petrol vehicles with no enacted transition.

civility.statement: The Climate Change Commission has been really clear on this, and that’s really the key problem with this bill, because it is sloppy work. It’s sloppy, it’s chaotic, it’s destructive. That’s what we’ve come to expect from this Government—rushed through under urgency without careful thought.
civility.explanation: Extremely harsh language, but every word is aimed at the bill and the Government's drafting process, not at any individual member. Under the re-anchored scale, brutal criticism of a measure is fully civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, we are here to debate the final reading of the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill. Unlike the previous speaker, Scott Willis, I think I have worked that much out.
civility.explanation: A named jibe at another member's grasp of what is being debated. It is mild and glancing rather than sustained abuse, but it lands on the person's competence rather than on his argument.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The Climate Change Commission has been really clear on this, and that’s really the key problem with this bill, because it is sloppy work. It’s sloppy, it’s chaotic, it’s destructive. That’s what we’ve come to expect from this Government—rushed through under urgency without careful thought.
focus.explanation: There is a real process point (rushed through under urgency) but most of the weight is generalised party framing about what 'we've come to expect from this Government' rather than the bill's content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This is the problem with this Government: it is unable to do legislation well. It would rather rush things through and do it in a sloppy and chaotic way.
focus.explanation: A general characterisation of the other side's competence at law-making. No policy, figure, mechanism or named outcome survives once the party framing is stripped out.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We need to ensure that we have land transport that is fully decarbonised, and that is going to mean low-emission vehicles, zero-emission transport, with their fair contribution to road-user charges, but let’s ensure that rural communities are not paying more because they drive on poor roads.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the policy question before the House: how road-user charges should be structured across vehicle types and who bears the cost.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Norway survived different flavours of Government to achieve substantial decarbonisation of land transport, and the main signal all Norway’s Governments have given is that it should always be economically beneficial to choose zero-emission or low-emission cars, so their ambition is to make sure that all new cars are zero-emission by 2025.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Norway has a policy goal that all new cars sold be zero-emission by 2025, and that successive Norwegian governments have maintained a consistent price-advantage signal for zero/low-emission vehicles.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Norway's National Transport Plan / Storting-adopted targets: true if an official Norwegian target that all new passenger cars be zero-emission by 2025 is documented, false if no such target exists or the date is materially different; the consistency claim checks against Norwegian EV tax exemptions (VAT/registration) maintained across the 2013, 2017 and 2021 governments.

veracity.statement: And the motor industry has almost universally contested this bill. So what this bill shows is that the Government is not listening to business.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the motor industry almost universally opposed the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Submissions and public statements from motor industry bodies (Motor Industry Association, Motor Trade Association, Drive Electric) on this bill: true if the large majority opposed it, false if industry bodies were split or largely supportive.

veracity.statement: My colleague the Hon Julie Anne Genter proposed very sensible amendments, for example, to have a fairer rate of road-user charges of $60 per 1,000 kilometres, and that aligned with the industry request.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Julie Anne Genter tabled an amendment setting light EV road-user charges at $60 per 1,000 km, and that this figure matched what the motor industry had asked for.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Amendment Papers lodged for the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill and industry submissions: true if a Genter amendment specifies $60 per 1,000 km and an industry body sought that rate, false if no such amendment exists, the rate differs, or industry sought a different figure.

rigor.statement: And the motor industry has almost universally contested this bill. So what this bill shows is that the Government is not listening to business.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur: industry opposition to a bill establishes disagreement, not a failure to listen. The conclusion treats 'did not adopt our position' as 'did not consider it', with nothing offered to bridge the two.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In relation to the cost and the disincentivisation of EVs, this is going to cost us in missing our climate targets, and that cost will come to us when we have to buy offshore credits.
rigor.explanation: A genuine causal chain — charging EVs discourages uptake, uptake shortfall widens the emissions gap, the gap is closed by purchasing offshore mitigation — but each link is asserted rather than evidenced, so there is a real gap between what is shown and what is concluded.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: What we know—what we know—is that there will be many, many billion dollars that will have to be spent because of this Government’s inaction on climate.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that New Zealand will incur costs running to several billion dollars as a consequence of the current Government's climate policy settings.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Treasury / Ministry for the Environment reporting on the cost of meeting NZ's first Nationally Determined Contribution, including offshore mitigation purchases: true if officially estimated or actual cumulative cost attributable to the shortfall exceeds NZ$2 billion, false if it is materially below that or no such liability is incurred.

specificity.statement: My colleague the Hon Julie Anne Genter proposed very sensible amendments, for example, to have a fairer rate of road-user charges of $60 per 1,000 kilometres, and that aligned with the industry request.
specificity.explanation: Names the amendment's author, the mechanism (a lower RUC rate) and an exact figure ($60 per 1,000 km) that could be checked against the Amendment Paper and acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We need to ensure that we have land transport that is fully decarbonised, and that is going to mean low-emission vehicles, zero-emission transport, with their fair contribution to road-user charges, but let’s ensure that rural communities are not paying more because they drive on poor roads.
specificity.explanation: A direction of travel — decarbonised transport, fair RUC contributions, protection for rural drivers — with no rate, threshold, mechanism or timeframe attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Auckland has just experienced, in this Government policy statement, a cut of $500 million from their public transport network.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government Policy Statement on land transport cut $500 million from Auckland's public transport funding.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: The draft Government Policy Statement on Land Transport 2024 and Auckland Transport/Auckland Council analysis of it; true if the public transport funding allocation for Auckland is reduced by approximately $500 million relative to the previous GPS, false if the reduction is materially different or non-existent.

veracity.statement: On top of that, we’ve seen the additional $50 on our registration fees for cars, an anticipated fuel-excise tax that will start in two years’ time.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a $50 increase in motor vehicle registration fees and a planned fuel excise duty increase beginning about two years from March 2024.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / NZTA announcements and Budget documents from 2024; true if the annual vehicle registration fee was raised by $50 and a fuel excise duty increase was scheduled to begin around 2026, false if the amount or timing is materially different.

veracity.statement: It started at 20 percent, it then got up to 30 percent, and then, thanks to our Labour team—acknowledging Tangi Utikere and Arena Williams for the work that they did with the Transport and Infrastructure Committee—it got up to 50 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the plug-in hybrid road-user charge rate moved from 20 to 30 to 50 percent of the light EV rate through the select committee process.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Transport and Infrastructure Committee report on the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill and the rates as enacted; true if the PHEV rate was set at 50 percent of the light EV rate having been proposed lower, false if the progression of rates differs.

veracity.statement: Add on to that 23 percent in water rates additionally for Aucklanders.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a 23 percent increase in water charges for Auckland ratepayers.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Auckland Council / Watercare long-term plan and consultation documents for 2024; true if the proposed water charge increase is approximately 23 percent, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: The previous speaker, Shanan Halbert, spent almost his entire 10-minute call talking about climate change and this Government being climate change deniers. He didn’t once talk about road-user charges (RUC) and actually talk about what we’re here to talk about.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that the preceding speech was almost entirely about climate change and climate denial, and never mentioned road-user charges.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard record of Shanan Halbert's speech immediately preceding; true if the speech is overwhelmingly about climate change/denial and contains no discussion of road-user charges, false if it discusses road-user charges (rates, who pays, the PHEV percentage) at length or does not call the Government climate deniers.

veracity.statement: They consulted with the public of a reduced rate for plug-in hybrids at 20 percent and then did nothing.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the previous government consulted publicly in 2022 on a reduced 20 percent plug-in hybrid road-user charge rate and then took no legislative action.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport 2022 consultation documents on road user charges for light electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, and the legislative record to October 2023; true if such a consultation at a 20 percent PHEV rate occurred and no implementing legislation followed, false if no such consultation exists or if implementing steps were taken.

specificity.statement: Auckland has just experienced, in this Government policy statement, a cut of $500 million from their public transport network.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific policy instrument, a specific region, a specific funding area and a dollar figure — directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: On top of that, we’ve seen the additional $50 on our registration fees for cars, an anticipated fuel-excise tax that will start in two years’ time.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dollar amount, a named fee and a timeframe for a second named charge.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The second road is the Takitimu North Link through Te Puna and Ōmokoroa. Stage one is under way, but our Government is committed to delivering stage two of that project all the way through to Ōmokoroa—an extra 7 kilometres.
specificity.explanation: Names the project, its stages, the localities and the additional distance, though no cost or completion date is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: What that means is that the cost will be offset to people that use public transport in Auckland, and their fees—as advised by Auckland Council’s submission yesterday—are likely to increase by 126 percent.
divination.explanation: Relays Auckland Council's forecast that Auckland public transport fares will rise by 126 percent as a consequence of the funding change.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: Auckland Transport published fare schedules; true if average Auckland public transport fares rise by roughly 126 percent from their March 2024 level, false if the cumulative increase is materially smaller.

focus.statement: What we’ve seen in Auckland, under the Government policy statement and under the repeal of the regional fuel tax, is actually the Minister forcing more people to take their car as opposed to taking public transport.
focus.explanation: Squarely on two named policy measures (the GPS and the regional fuel tax repeal) and their claimed effect on transport mode choice, rather than on the other party in general.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: They are so out of touch and unaware of the process that this bill has actually focused on.
focus.explanation: Characterises another party as out of touch without naming any provision, figure or outcome of the bill; the content is entirely about the other side.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: What we’ve seen in Auckland, under the Government policy statement and under the repeal of the regional fuel tax, is actually the Minister forcing more people to take their car as opposed to taking public transport.
rigor.explanation: The leap from reduced public transport funding to the Minister 'forcing' people into cars is asserted rather than supported; no mechanism or evidence of mode shift is offered, so the conclusion outruns the premises.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: They’re now complaining that this process has been rushed, yet they sat on their hands for nearly two years and did nothing to reduce the rate of plug-in hybrids in the road-user charges.
rigor.explanation: Tu quoque: the opposition's earlier inaction is offered as an answer to the charge that this bill's process was rushed, but past delay does not bear on whether the present select committee process was adequate.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: There are no savings in that, so let’s not hoodwink Aucklanders and make them think that they’re getting a tax cut and then they’re going to have more money in their back pocket.
civility.explanation: 'Hoodwink' imputes deliberate deception to those opposite rather than simply disputing the arithmetic — pointed and bad-faith-imputing, though it stops short of a personal insult.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Why didn’t he talk about it? Because he’s got no idea what the bill actually is intended to do and to deliver on.
civility.explanation: A direct attack on another member's competence and understanding rather than on his argument.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: What we’ve seen is that all those other policy initiatives to increase EV uptake have gone by the wayside, in particular the Clean Car Discount.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that EV-uptake policy initiatives, and specifically the Clean Car Discount, have been discontinued.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / NZTA records and Government announcements on the Clean Car Discount: true if the scheme was terminated (and other EV-uptake measures such as the Clean Car Standard incentives or EV charging support were withdrawn) before 28 March 2024; false if the Clean Car Discount was still operating at that date.

veracity.statement: But we also noticed that, with that Clean Car Discount, many more EVs were coming into the market.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that EV registrations/imports rose materially while the Clean Car Discount was in force.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA new and used light-vehicle registration data by fuel type: true if BEV/PHEV registrations were materially higher during the Clean Car Discount period (July 2021 – December 2023) than in the equivalent period before it; false if registrations were flat or lower.

veracity.statement: And finally, after some time—we talk about the fact that about 2 percent of the vehicles are now EVs—it’s finally reached that threshold where we believe that it’s now time to bring them into that programme itself.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that electric vehicles make up approximately 2 percent of the New Zealand vehicle fleet as at March 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Motor Vehicle Register fleet statistics for early 2024: true if BEVs (or BEVs plus PHEVs) are about 2 percent of the light vehicle fleet; false if materially different, e.g. under 1 percent or above 4 percent.

focus.statement: What we’ve seen is that all those other policy initiatives to increase EV uptake have gone by the wayside, in particular the Clean Car Discount.
focus.explanation: Names a specific policy (the Clean Car Discount) and its removal rather than attacking the other party in general terms.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We’ve signed up to the Paris Agreement, and I just keep seeing all the good work that the previous Government did be undone and nothing to replace it. And it is shameful and very depressing.
focus.explanation: A genuine policy frame (the Paris Agreement, emissions reduction) but the weight of the sentence is an undifferentiated contrast between 'the previous Government' and the current one, with no specific measure named as undone.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This bill here is about making sure that all users are contributing. This is based on kilometres and weights. So, in other words, it’s making sure that the contribution of the vehicle is appropriate to the wear and tear that it has of the actual assets.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the mechanism of the bill before the House — how the charge is calculated and what it is meant to recover.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I am disappointed that we’re not seeing the policies to decarbonise New Zealand, which is so important, particularly when we know that such a high percentage of our carbon emissions comes from our transport fleet and our light transport fleet is there.
specificity.explanation: Gestures at 'the policies to decarbonise' and 'such a high percentage' without naming a policy, a figure, a mechanism or a timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This bill here is about making sure that all users are contributing. This is based on kilometres and weights. So, in other words, it’s making sure that the contribution of the vehicle is appropriate to the wear and tear that it has of the actual assets.
specificity.explanation: Names the actual charging mechanism (distance and weight) but supplies no rates, thresholds or start date for the light-EV RUC.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: And I hear one of the Ministers talking about adaptation, and I hope that he appreciates how expensive it is to adapt when almost all of our cities in New Zealand, including, of course, the beautiful Dunedin—it has a lovely harbour and coastline—will be impacted by climate change.
civility.explanation: Directed at a Minister's argument about adaptation rather than at him personally; the only edge is the mildly didactic 'I hope that he appreciates', which stops short of impugning him.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: OK. It was rather a little bit more than little, but it was a very well-prepared and well-conditioned road, and it made me think that someone of influence actually lived up that road somewhere, but I’m not too sure about that.
civility.explanation: A jocular insinuation that a road was well maintained because 'someone of influence' lives on it — a light imputation of favouritism aimed at a colleague rather than at any argument, though immediately hedged.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And I do question the comments that have been made—particularly from the other side of the House—that this here is going to absolutely sway people away from buying such vehicles. I actually don’t believe in that; I actually believe that people have all sorts of other reasons that they take into account, and I don’t think we’re going to have the demise that the so-called speakers on the other side actually talked to.
rigor.explanation: Engages a real policy claim (whether light-EV RUCs will deter EV purchases) but rests the rebuttal entirely on personal belief and the buying choices of acquaintances in his electorate — an appeal to anecdote, with no data or mechanism offered against the opposing claim.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: And I do question the comments that have been made—particularly from the other side of the House—that this here is going to absolutely sway people away from buying such vehicles. I actually don’t believe in that; I actually believe that people have all sorts of other reasons that they take into account, and I don’t think we’re going to have the demise that the so-called speakers on the other side actually talked to.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that bringing light EVs into road-user charges will not cause a collapse in EV and plug-in hybrid purchases.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA new light-vehicle registrations by fuel type: true if combined BEV and PHEV registrations in the 12 months from 1 April 2024 are at or near the preceding 12 months' level (no collapse); false if they fall sharply (say by a third or more) over that period.

specificity.statement: That’s why we came to the final decision of reducing it from our proposed $53 per 1,000 kilometres to a very pragmatic, reasonable, consensus-driven proposal of $38 per 1,000 kilometres, because that’s equitable, that’s fair.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact prior and final RUC rates per 1,000 km for plug-in hybrids — fully checkable against the select committee report.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Now that is estimated by the Ministry of Transport to mean that there are 9,200 hospital admissions as a result of that, and the cost in childhood asthma is 13,200 childhood asthma cases and the social cost is $10.5 billion.
specificity.explanation: Three concrete, sourced figures — hospital admissions, childhood asthma cases and a dollar social cost — attributed to a named agency.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: That’s why we came to the final decision of reducing it from our proposed $53 per 1,000 kilometres to a very pragmatic, reasonable, consensus-driven proposal of $38 per 1,000 kilometres, because that’s equitable, that’s fair.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Transport and Infrastructure Committee recommended lowering the plug-in hybrid RUC rate from $53 to $38 per 1,000 km.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Transport and Infrastructure Committee report on the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill and the resulting rate schedule; true if the PHEV rate moved from a proposed $53 to $38 per 1,000 km, false if either figure differs materially.

veracity.statement: When this proposal was introduced by the previous National Government in 2009, it always had an asterisk next to it saying, “This is only in place until the vehicle fleet in New Zealand of electric vehicles reaches 2 percent.” Standing here today, we have reached that target.
veracity.explanation: Two factual assertions: that the 2009 EV RUC exemption was tied to a 2 percent share of the light vehicle fleet, and that the EV fleet share has now reached 2 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Road User Charges (Exemption Period for Light Electric RUC Vehicles) legislation and 2009 Cabinet/policy papers for the 2 percent trigger, plus Ministry of Transport fleet statistics for March 2024; true if the 2 percent threshold was the stated condition and light EVs were at or above 2 percent of the light fleet, false if either fails.

veracity.statement: Transitioning EVs and plug-in hybrids is the first step in the National and ACT Party coalition agreement to bring all vehicles into the RUC system.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the National–ACT coalition agreement contains a commitment to move all vehicles into the road user charges system.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the National–ACT coalition agreement (November 2023); true if it contains a commitment to transition all vehicles to road user charges, false if no such commitment appears.

veracity.statement: Now that is estimated by the Ministry of Transport to mean that there are 9,200 hospital admissions as a result of that, and the cost in childhood asthma is 13,200 childhood asthma cases and the social cost is $10.5 billion.
veracity.explanation: Asserts Ministry of Transport / health-and-air-pollution estimates of 9,200 hospital admissions, 13,200 childhood asthma cases and a $10.5 billion social cost attributable to vehicle emissions.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The HAPINZ 3.0 study and the Ministry of Transport Cabinet paper referenced; true if those documents give 9,200 hospital admissions, 13,200 childhood asthma cases and a social cost of about $10.5 billion for motor-vehicle emissions, false if the figures or the attribution to vehicles differ materially.

veracity.statement: Now, carbon monoxide—95 percent of the emissions from New Zealand come from our cars and that causes things like heart issues and brain issues.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 95 percent of New Zealand's carbon monoxide emissions come from motor vehicles.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry for the Environment / Stats NZ air emissions inventory for carbon monoxide by source; true if road transport accounts for about 95 percent of national CO emissions, false if the vehicle share is materially lower.

veracity.statement: Maybe they’re not able to source a vehicle to do the job required of it, especially in a commercial sense, such as those tradies and farmers, who need utes to do their job—and who, by the way, are now not forced to pay thousands of dollars extra because we got rid of the ute tax.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Clean Car Discount fee on high-emission vehicles ('the ute tax') cost buyers thousands of dollars and has been removed by this Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Clean Car Discount fee schedule and the date of its repeal; true if fees on high-emission utes ran into the thousands of dollars and the scheme was ended effective 31 December 2023, false if either is wrong.

veracity.statement: I also note that, in the report we’ve got with this bill, it says, “While the vast majority of submitters recognised that EV owners should still contribute to the land transport network, they considered the RUC rate for EVs to be unreasonable.”—and this is in relation to those light electric vehicles (EVs).
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the select committee report on the bill contains that specific finding about submitters' views on the EV RUC rate.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Transport and Infrastructure Committee report on the Road User Charges (Light Electric RUC Vehicles) Amendment Bill; true if the quoted sentence appears substantially as given, false if it does not.

veracity.statement: But also, when the exemption happened for the EVs some years ago, that was to increase the uptake of EVs. And it was always a time-limited policy idea.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the stated purpose of the original light-EV RUC exemption was to lift EV uptake and that it was designed from the outset as time-limited.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2009 Road User Charges exemption legislation and its accompanying regulatory impact statement / Cabinet paper; true if uptake was the stated purpose and an end condition or sunset was built in, false if the exemption was open-ended or justified on other grounds.

civility.statement: Now, the member opposite—Julie Anne Genter—raises her hands in disgust. She’s not supporting this bill, and I simply say to her: what the RUC—what the RUC?
civility.explanation: Pointed and personalising — characterises a named member's bodily reaction as 'disgust' and jibes at her — but stops short of attacking her character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So when I hear the gaffawing on the other side of the House with regard to some of these things, and the self-congratulatory tone, I get worried that those issues are being pushed underground.
civility.explanation: Characterises opponents' manner as laughing and self-congratulatory — edging toward the people rather than the argument, but no individual is attacked and the point returns to the substance.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: This is simply about road-user charges (RUC), and if I use the Oxford Dictionary meaning for each of these words, I might simplify it for those on the other side of the House that are feeling confused or aggrieved or feel that they shouldn’t have to contribute for whatever reason they might believe exempts them.
civility.explanation: Condescension: offers to define ordinary words for opponents on the premise they are 'confused', which mocks rather than engages them.
civility.subject: speaker

divination.statement: I look forward to seeing that detail of work, and I have no doubt that that will come through the hard-working and very diligent Transport and Infrastructure Committee as well.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the Minister of Transport's wider plan to bring all vehicles into the RUC system will be considered by the Transport and Infrastructure Committee.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Parliament's select committee records; true if legislation extending road user charges beyond light EVs is referred to and reported on by the Transport and Infrastructure Committee, false if no such referral occurs.

rigor.statement: So when I hear words like “You’ve got to pay your fair share if you’re an electric vehicle owner”, I think it’s really important that we honour electric vehicle owners for the fact that they’re not putting those things into the atmosphere so that they are not responsible for the childhood asthma that I would see as a real issue in the inner city of Auckland, including in my electorate of Mt Albert.
rigor.explanation: A real inference: the health-cost evidence just cited is offered as a reason the 'fair share' framing is incomplete. The link between vehicle particulates and childhood asthma is supported by the cited estimates, though the leap to her own electorate rests on anecdote.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So when I hear words like “You’ve got to pay your fair share if you’re an electric vehicle owner”, I think it’s really important that we honour electric vehicle owners for the fact that they’re not putting those things into the atmosphere so that they are not responsible for the childhood asthma that I would see as a real issue in the inner city of Auckland, including in my electorate of Mt Albert.
focus.explanation: Engages the substance of what 'fair share' should mean under the RUC change, naming the externality being left out of the calculation.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: There’s plenty of common sense on this side of the House.
focus.explanation: A team-versus-team boast with no policy, mechanism, figure or outcome named.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Our position in terms of the $2 billion seafood export industry needs to be consistently affirmed.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's seafood export industry is worth approximately $2 billion.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries / Seafood New Zealand export revenue figures for the year to 2023-24; true if annual seafood export revenue is approximately NZ$2 billion, false if materially different (e.g. under $1.5b or over $2.5b).

veracity.statement: So, closer to home, we have the western and central Pacific: over 6.5 percent of catch of all tuna species were found to be involved in IUU—not a good outcome.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than 6.5 percent of the tuna catch in the western and central Pacific was found to involve illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The MRAG Asia Pacific quantification of IUU in the Western and Central Pacific Ocean tuna fisheries commissioned by the Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency (2016 and 2021 updates); true if the estimated IUU share of tuna catch exceeds 6.5%, false if materially lower.

veracity.statement: Extensive consultation has informed this bill. The Ministry for Primary Industries led multiple and regular engagement sessions. All stakeholders agreed that the regime should be updated.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that MPI ran extensive consultation on the bill and that every stakeholder consulted supported updating the international fisheries regime.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The departmental disclosure statement and regulatory impact statement for the Fisheries (International Fishing and Other Matters) Amendment Bill; true if they record MPI-led consultation with stakeholder support for updating the regime, false if they record dissenting stakeholders or only limited consultation.

veracity.statement: These officials have been looking at our legislation, and there was a review of the Fisheries Act undertaken in 2020.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a review of the Fisheries Act 1996 was undertaken in 2020.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI published records of Fisheries Act review work; true if a review of the Fisheries Act was under way or completed in 2020, false if no such review occurred in that year.

veracity.statement: There was then—and new members of the House might be particularly interested in this—a regulatory impact statement, and there were no redactions to that regulatory impact statement.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the regulatory impact statement published for this bill contained no redactions.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published regulatory impact statement for the Fisheries (International Fishing and Other Matters) Amendment Bill on the MPI/Treasury RIS register; true if the document contains no withheld or blacked-out passages, false if any redactions are marked.

focus.statement: We want to accentuate every positive dimension about the primary sector that was undermined, weakened, and corroded as a consequence of foolish regulation, ill-conceived plans, and too much “Kumbaya”.
focus.explanation: Gestures at the primary sector but names no regulation, plan, cost or outcome; the weight is a generalised swipe at the previous government's approach ('foolish regulation', 'too much Kumbaya').
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This bill is limited, however, to fisheries beyond our exclusive economic zone. Whilst we commend it, we would like to see broader reform which assesses all of the Fisheries Act against New Zealand’s international obligations. This bill should be thus expanded—including our domestic fisheries and fixing them where they fall short.
focus.explanation: Engages the measure directly — identifies the bill's scope limitation to waters beyond the EEZ and proposes a specific broadening to cover the whole Fisheries Act and domestic fisheries.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Some regimes disappear and others come to the fore, and I speak on behalf of the current group of politicians who hold the privilege of constitutional ministerial positions and the obligations of governing for New Zealanders, and we want to ensure that the commercial interests of New Zealand, both internationally and domestically, are not either undermined or neglected or marginalised by people who have an excessive level of interest in joining international green NGO echo chambers.
civility.explanation: Sneering characterisation of opponents as people with 'an excessive level of interest in joining international green NGO echo chambers' — dismissive of motives, but aimed at an unnamed group rather than an individual, so short of a personal attack.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Our seafood exports will be scrutinised by import markets, without a doubt, but let no one buy into the ongoing false narrative for the small number of parliamentarians, and their fellow travellers, who are trying to use international trade obligations to intimidate New Zealand politicians who have been mandated to form the Government to come up with sensible climate change policies that make sense to ordinary Kiwis, who want to see an economic dividend and a surplus continuously generated so we can afford, through fisheries industry and other industries, the accoutrements that define us as a First World nation.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith to other MPs — that they and their 'fellow travellers' are peddling a 'false narrative' to 'intimidate' the Government. Mockery of motive, though no individual is named.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: On the Treaty of Waitangi, as the fisheries Minister, I could have consulted myself, because we’ve had far too much expansiveness and rubbery thinking fitting of a comic figure in relation to the application of the Treaty.
civility.explanation: Derides those who take a broader view of the Treaty as engaging in 'rubbery thinking fitting of a comic figure' — mockery rather than engagement with the argument, but not directed at a named person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I believe that is a forlorn hope with this Government, because we have a Minister of fisheries, who is donkey deep in dead fish, and we would have thought previously that he was an advocate for fisheries, but what we find emerging in his seeming co-advocacy for seabed mining is that he doesn’t really care how the fish die as long as as many fish die as possible—whether it’s through overfishing or through seabed mining.
civility.explanation: A direct personal attack on the Minister — 'donkey deep in dead fish' and the claim that he wants as many fish dead as possible impugns his character and motives rather than his policy.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I think when the Hon Shane Jones comes into the Chamber the fish swim for their lives.
civility.explanation: A mocking jibe aimed at a named member personally rather than at any argument or policy he advanced.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Under this bill, vessels will require a permit to fish anywhere outside our waters. This will improve our ability to ensure that our vessels comply with both international obligations and the obligations of other States.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete mechanism in the bill — a permit requirement for New Zealand vessels fishing anywhere outside the EEZ — though without figures, costs or timeframes.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This bill is limited, however, to fisheries beyond our exclusive economic zone. Whilst we commend it, we would like to see broader reform which assesses all of the Fisheries Act against New Zealand’s international obligations. This bill should be thus expanded—including our domestic fisheries and fixing them where they fall short.
specificity.explanation: Names the statute and the scope gap (beyond-EEZ only, domestic fisheries excluded), but supplies no mechanism, cost or timeframe for the broader reform proposed.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If a New Zealand - flagged vessel was to be found to have undermined a measure and New Zealand failed to take effective action, that could not only damage our reputation but it could be used in a way negative to our prospects as primary producers.
rigor.explanation: A conditional inference linking non-enforcement to reputational and market consequences; the connecting mechanism (import markets screening for IUU, stated earlier) is supplied, though the size of the effect is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I believe that is a forlorn hope with this Government, because we have a Minister of fisheries, who is donkey deep in dead fish, and we would have thought previously that he was an advocate for fisheries, but what we find emerging in his seeming co-advocacy for seabed mining is that he doesn’t really care how the fish die as long as as many fish die as possible—whether it’s through overfishing or through seabed mining.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion that broader reform is a 'forlorn hope' rests entirely on an ad hominem characterisation of the Minister's motives, inferred from his position on seabed mining; no link is offered between that position and the fate of Fisheries Act reform.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We’ve just heard from the Minister for Oceans and Fisheries that this is going to go to select committee, and it will go through the normal—because I didn’t hear anything else—Standing Orders process of six months at that select committee.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the bill will follow the standard six-month select committee process rather than a shortened reporting deadline.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The Parliament bill page for the Fisheries (International Fishing and Other Matters) Amendment Bill; true if the Primary Production Committee's report-back date was set roughly six months after referral (about late September 2024) and it reported around then, false if a shorter reporting deadline was set or the bill was progressed under urgency.

veracity.statement: On this very same day, the Kermadec sanctuary bill that was brought forward by a National Government as a flagship piece of legislation to protect our environment is taken from the Order Paper just the day after the Minister for Regional Development mentioned that there are manganese nodules in the Kermadec Islands.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary Bill (introduced under a National-led government) was discharged from the Order Paper on 28 March 2024, the day after the Minister for Regional Development publicly referred to manganese nodules in the Kermadecs.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Parliamentary Order Paper / Hansard record for 27-28 March 2024: true if the Kermadec Ocean Sanctuary Bill was discharged or removed on that date and the bill originated under the 2011-2017 National government, false if the discharge date or origin differs; plus a media/Hansard record of the Minister for Regional Development referring to manganese nodules in the Kermadecs the preceding day.

veracity.statement: We are the last country in the South Pacific to still undertake destructive bottom trawling.
veracity.explanation: Asserts New Zealand is the only remaining South Pacific nation carrying out bottom trawling (in context, on South Pacific high seas / seamounts).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: SPRFMO bottom-fishing records and member-state reporting for 2023-24: true if New Zealand-flagged vessels are the only ones recorded bottom trawling in the SPRFMO convention area, false if vessels of any other member state (e.g. Australia, Chile) also conducted bottom trawling there.

veracity.statement: And, in that international realm of responsibility at the South Pacific Regional Fisheries Management Organisation, New Zealand had previously committed to bringing a proposal for protection of the most vulnerable ocean ecosystems, and we reneged on that with the change of Government to the present Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts New Zealand had committed at SPRFMO to bring a proposal protecting vulnerable marine ecosystems, dropped that commitment after the 2023 change of government, Australia lodged the proposal instead, and New Zealand voted against it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: SPRFMO Commission meeting papers and voting records for the 2023/2024 annual meeting: true if New Zealand had lodged/undertaken to lodge a VME protection proposal, did not do so, and is recorded opposing an Australian proposal; false if no such NZ commitment exists or NZ did not vote against.

veracity.statement: Estimates from the World Economic Forum suggest that illegal, unreported, unregulated fishing in international waters equates to anywhere between the vicinity of $26 billion to $50 billion.
veracity.explanation: Relays a World Economic Forum estimate that the global value of IUU fishing in international waters is between $26 billion and $50 billion.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: World Economic Forum publications on IUU fishing: true if a WEF estimate gives a range of roughly US$26-50 billion, false if WEF's published figure is materially different or no such estimate exists.

veracity.statement: For one recent example that I would like to share for the sake of the House, it was noted in the Pacific alone that illegal tuna fishing between the years of 2017-2019 equated to approximately 192,000 tonnes, an estimated value of some $335 million.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that IUU tuna fishing in the Pacific over 2017-2019 amounted to about 192,000 tonnes worth roughly $335 million.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency / MRAG quantification of IUU tuna fishing in the Western and Central Pacific for 2017-2019: true if the volume is ~192,000 tonnes and value ~US$330-340 million, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: New Zealand, for context, in terms of our exclusive economic zone, is over 4 million square kilometres, spanning between Niue, the Cook Islands, and Tokelau.
veracity.explanation: Asserts New Zealand's exclusive economic zone exceeds 4 million square kilometres and spans the area between Niue, the Cook Islands and Tokelau.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: LINZ / Ministry for Primary Industries published figures for the area of New Zealand's EEZ: true if the stated area exceeds 4 million km², false if materially smaller; the geographic span claim checks against whether Niue, Cook Islands and Tokelau EEZs are separate from New Zealand's.

veracity.statement: According to 2020 estimates, 45 percent of the high seas is outside any—and I stress this point—jurisdictional boundary, and this is where most of the illegal fishing occurs.
veracity.explanation: Relays a 2020 estimate that 45 percent of the high seas lies outside any jurisdictional boundary and that most illegal fishing occurs there.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published ocean-governance estimates (e.g. FAO, UN BBNJ background papers) of the share of the ocean/planetary surface lying beyond national jurisdiction: true if a ~45% figure for areas beyond national jurisdiction is documented for around 2020, false if the accepted figure is materially different; plus evidence on whether the majority of IUU catch occurs beyond national jurisdiction.

rigor.statement: And Trans-Tasman Resources, this very day, also withdrew from the Environmental Protection Agency, because I am certain that they have been given the nod that they’ll be on the fast-track legislation.
rigor.explanation: The causal conclusion (the withdrawal happened because the company was privately assured of fast-track inclusion) rests solely on the speaker's own certainty plus the coincidence of timing — a bare assertion combined with post hoc reasoning; no evidence connecting the withdrawal to any assurance is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So this Government has a long way to go before it is equal and authentic in terms of its expression of support for protection of our fisheries and our ocean ecosystems.
focus.explanation: Names the policy domain (fisheries and ocean ecosystem protection) but the sentence itself is a general characterisation of the Government's sincerity rather than a specific measure, figure or outcome; the policy content is wrapped in party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I would urge this Government and this Minister to do all in their power to actually act in the common interest and broaden this bill to include everything within our ambit, including the way that fishing and oceans management is done within our exclusive economic zone in the waters of Aotearoa New Zealand.
focus.explanation: Squarely about the scope of the bill before the House — whether it should extend to fisheries management inside New Zealand's EEZ. No party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The bill will strengthen the rules around international fishing practices, especially around unreported, unregulated fishing and vessels whilst in international waters.
focus.explanation: Directly describes what the measure before the House does; no party content at all.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I would urge this Government and this Minister to do all in their power to actually act in the common interest and broaden this bill to include everything within our ambit, including the way that fishing and oceans management is done within our exclusive economic zone in the waters of Aotearoa New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Gives a clear direction (extend the bill's coverage to the EEZ) but no mechanism, clause, cost or timeframe for how that would be done.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: For one recent example that I would like to share for the sake of the House, it was noted in the Pacific alone that illegal tuna fishing between the years of 2017-2019 equated to approximately 192,000 tonnes, an estimated value of some $335 million.
specificity.explanation: Names a region, a defined period, a tonnage and a dollar value — fully checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Fines could include, for those said vessels with connections to IUU, being fined up to $250,000 and potential seizure of the vessel.
